translations.literal: Sun Teng, Gao Longzhi, Sima Ziru, Dou Tai, Wei Jing, Lou Zhao, Kudigan, Han Gui, Duan Rong, Hulü Jin
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng, Gao Longzhi, Sima Ziru, Dou Tai, Wei Jing, Lou Zhao, Kudigan, Han Gui, Duan Rong, and Hulü Jin

sentences.zh: 列傳第四十二

translations.literal: Biographies 42
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 42

sentences.zh: 孫騰高隆之司馬子如子消難裴藻兄子膺之竇泰尉景婁昭兄子睿厙狄幹孫士文韓軌段榮子韶孝言斛律金子光羨

translations.literal: Biographies 42: Sun Teng, Gao Longzhi, Sima Ziru, his son Xiaonan, Pei Zao, his elder brother's son Yingzhi, Dou Tai, Wei Jing, Lou Zhao, his elder brother's son Rui, Kudigan, his grandson Shiwen, Han Gui, Duan Rong, his son Shao, Xiaoyan, Hulü Jin, his son Guang, Xian
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 42 — Sun Teng, Gao Longzhi, Sima Ziru (and his son Xiaonan, Pei Zao, and his nephew Yingzhi), Dou Tai, Wei Jing, Lou Zhao (and his nephew Rui), Kudigan (and his grandson Shiwen), Han Gui, Duan Rong (and his sons Shao and Xiaoyan), and Hulü Jin (and his sons Guang and Xian)

sentences.zh: 孫騰，字龍雀，咸陽石安人也。

translations.literal: Sun Teng, style name Longque, was a native of Shian in Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng, whose style was Longque, came from Shian in Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 祖通，仕沮渠氏，為中書舍人。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tong served the Juqu clan as Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tong had served the Juqu as a secretariat attendant.

sentences.zh: 沮渠氏滅，因徙居北邊。

translations.literal: When the Juqu clan was destroyed, the family moved to the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Juqu, the family resettled on the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 及騰貴，魏朝贈司徒。

translations.literal: When Teng rose to eminence, the Wei court posthumously enfeoffed Tong as Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Once Teng had risen to power, the Wei court posthumously made Tong Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 父機，贈太尉。

translations.literal: His father Ji was posthumously made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji was posthumously made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 騰少質直，明解吏事。

translations.literal: Teng in youth was plain and upright and clearly understood administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Teng was plainspoken and upright, with a clear grasp of administrative business.

sentences.zh: 魏正光中，北方擾，歸爾硃榮。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang era of Wei, when the north was in turmoil, he went over to Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wei Zhengguang era, as the north fell into disorder, he joined Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 尋為齊神武都督長史。

translations.literal: Soon he became chief clerk to the commander Gao Huan of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became chief clerk on the staff of Gao Huan, the future Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 神武為晉州，又引為長史，封石安縣伯。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan became governor of Jinzhou, he again took Teng as chief clerk and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Shian County.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan took up the Jinzhou governorship, he again appointed Teng chief clerk and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Shian.

sentences.zh: 及起兵于信都，常以誠款預謀策。

translations.literal: When they raised troops at Xindu, he was always included in planning through loyal devotion.
translations.idiomatic: When they raised arms at Xindu, his steady loyalty kept him in the inner circle of counsel.

sentences.zh: 累遷郡公，入為侍中，尋兼尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to district duke, entered office as Palace Attendant, and soon also served as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted in turn to district duke, he entered court as Palace Attendant and soon added the post of Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時魏京兆王愉女平原公主寡，騰願尚之，而公主欲侍中封隆之。

translations.literal: At the time the Princess of Pingyuan, daughter of Prince Yu of Jingzhao of Wei, was a widow; Teng wished to marry her, but the princess wanted Palace Attendant Feng Longzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Pingyuan, daughter of the Wei Prince of Jingzhao Yu, was then a widow. Teng wished to marry her, but she favored Palace Attendant Feng Longzhi.

sentences.zh: 騰妒隆之，遂相間構。

translations.literal: Teng was jealous of Longzhi and so set about slandering him.
translations.idiomatic: Jealous of Longzhi, Teng set factions against him.

sentences.zh: 神武啟免騰官，俄而復之。

translations.literal: Gao Huan memorialized to remove Teng from office, but soon restored him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan had him dismissed from office, then soon restored him.

sentences.zh: 與斛其椿同掌機密，隆之見忌慮禍，奔晉陽。

translations.literal: Together with Huqizong he held confidential affairs; Longzhi, seeing himself envied and fearing disaster, fled to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He and Huqizong jointly held confidential affairs. Feng Longzhi, seeing himself targeted and fearing ruin, fled to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 神武入討椿，留騰行并州事。

translations.literal: Gao Huan entered to attack Huqizong and left Teng to administer Bingzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan marched in to punish Huqizong and left Teng to run Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 入為尚書左僕射，內外之事，騰咸知之。

translations.literal: He entered as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; of matters within and without, Teng knew them all.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as Left Vice Director, and nothing within the court or beyond it escaped Teng's knowledge.

sentences.zh: 兼司空，除侍中，兼尚書令。

translations.literal: He also served as Minister of Works, was appointed Palace Attendant, and concurrently held the post of Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as Minister of Works, was made Palace Attendant, and concurrently directed the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時西魏攻南袞州，詔騰率諸將討之。

translations.literal: At the time Western Wei attacked southern Yanzhou; an edict ordered Teng to lead the generals against them.
translations.idiomatic: When Western Wei attacked southern Yanzhou, an edict ordered Teng to lead the generals against them.

sentences.zh: 騰性怯無威略，失利而還。

translations.literal: Teng by nature was timid and lacked authority and strategy; he suffered defeat and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Timid by nature and without military authority, he met defeat and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 又除司徒，餘官如故。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Grand Tutor; his other offices remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Grand Tutor while keeping his other posts.

sentences.zh: 初北境亂，騰亡一女。

translations.literal: When the northern frontier was first in turmoil, Teng lost a daughter.
translations.idiomatic: During the early turmoil on the northern frontier, Teng lost a daughter.

sentences.zh: 及貴，推訪不得，疑其為人婢。

translations.literal: When he became eminent he searched but could not find her and suspected she had become someone's bondwoman.
translations.idiomatic: After he rose to power he searched in vain and suspected she had been sold into servitude.

sentences.zh: 及為司徒，奴婢訴良者皆免之，願免千人，冀得其女。

translations.literal: When he became Grand Tutor, he freed all bondmen and bondwomen who sued for free status, wishing to free a thousand people in hope of recovering his daughter.
translations.idiomatic: As Grand Tutor he freed every bond servant who sued for free status—he hoped to manumit a thousand people and thereby recover his daughter.

sentences.zh: 神武知之大怒，解司徒。

translations.literal: Gao Huan learned of it and was greatly angered and removed him from the Grand Tutorship.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was furious when he learned of this and stripped him of the Grand Tutorship.

sentences.zh: 尋為尚書左僕射、太保，仍侍中，遷太傅。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Grand Guardian, still Palace Attendant, and promoted to Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as Left Vice Director and Grand Guardian, kept Palace Attendant, and was promoted to Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 初，博陵崔孝芬取貧家子賈氏為養女。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cui Xiaofen of Boling took a poor family's daughter, the Jia clan, as an adopted daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Cui Xiaofen of Boling had taken a poor family's daughter surnamed Jia as his foster child.

sentences.zh: 孝芬死，其妻元更適鄭伯猷，攜賈于鄭氏。

translations.literal: When Xiaofen died, his wife of the Yuan clan remarried Zheng Boyou and took Jia into the Zheng household.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaofen's death his widow of the Yuan clan remarried Zheng Boyou and brought Jia into the Zheng household.

sentences.zh: 賈有色，騰納之為妾。

translations.literal: Jia was beautiful; Teng took her as a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Jia was beautiful, and Teng took her as a concubine.

sentences.zh: 其妻袁死，騰以賈有子，正以為妻，詔封丹陽郡君。

translations.literal: When his wife of the Yuan clan died, Teng, because Jia had borne a son, made her his principal wife; an edict enfeoffed her as Lady of Danyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After his wife Yuan died, Teng—because Jia had borne him a son—elevated her to principal wife; an edict enfeoffed her as Lady of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 復請以袁氏爵回授其女。

translations.literal: He again requested that the Yuan clan's noble rank be transferred back to his daughter.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned to have his late wife Yuan's noble title reassigned to his daughter.

sentences.zh: 其違禮肆情，多此類也。

translations.literal: His violations of ritual and indulgence of whim were mostly of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Such breaches of ritual and indulgence of private whim were typical of him.

sentences.zh: 騰早依神武，神武深信待之，置於魏朝，寄以心腹。

translations.literal: Teng had long relied on Gao Huan; Gao Huan deeply trusted and favored him, placed him in the Wei court, and entrusted him as a confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Teng had long served Gao Huan, who trusted him deeply, stationed him at the Wei court, and treated him as a confidant.

sentences.zh: 遂志氣驕盈，與奪自己。

translations.literal: Thereupon his spirit grew proud and overbearing; grants and denials were at his own pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: His pride swelled until he himself decided who received favor and who did not.

sentences.zh: 納賄不知紀極，官贈非財不行。

translations.literal: He accepted bribes beyond reckoning; official gifts would not move without wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Bribes flowed to him without limit; no official favor moved unless paid for.

sentences.zh: 肴藏銀器，盜為家物，親狎小人，專為聚斂。

translations.literal: Delicacies and stored silver vessels he stole as household goods; he was intimate with petty men and devoted himself solely to amassing wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He stole delicacies and silver from the stores for his household, kept company with petty men, and devoted himself to extortion.

sentences.zh: 與高岳、高隆之、司馬子如，號四貴。

translations.literal: Together with Gao Yue, Gao Longzhi, and Sima Ziru, they were called the Four Exalted.
translations.idiomatic: With Gao Yue, Gao Longzhi, and Sima Ziru he was known as one of the Four Exalted.

sentences.zh: 非法專恣，騰為甚焉。

translations.literal: Among those who acted unlawfully and willfully, Teng was the worst.
translations.idiomatic: Of those who abused power unlawfully, Teng was the worst offender.

sentences.zh: 神武、文襄，屢加誚讓，終不悛改，朝野深非笑之。

translations.literal: Gao Huan and Wenxiang repeatedly reproved him, but he never repented; court and countryside deeply derided him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan and Gao Cheng rebuked him again and again, yet he never mended his ways, and court and countryside alike mocked him.

sentences.zh: 武定六年薨，贈太師、開府、錄尚書事，諡曰文。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wuding he died; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, with an opening office, and Recorder of the Department of State Affairs; his posthumous title was Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Wuding and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with an opening office and charge over the Department of State Affairs; his posthumous name was Wen.

sentences.zh: 天保初，以騰佐命，詔祭告其墓。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, because Teng had aided in establishing the mandate, an edict ordered sacrifices announced at his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianbao, in recognition of his service at the founding, an edict ordered sacrifices at his tomb.

sentences.zh: 皇建中，配饗神武廟庭。

translations.literal: In the Huangjian era he was given a place in the sacrifices at Gao Huan's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huangjian era he was granted a place in the offerings at Gao Huan's temple.

sentences.zh: 子鳳珍嗣，性庸暗，卒於儀同三司。

translations.literal: His son Fengzhen succeeded him; by nature he was mediocre and dull and died as a third-rank commissioner with protocol equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fengzhen succeeded him—a man mediocre and dull—who died holding the third-rank commissioner's protocol.

sentences.zh: 高隆之，字延興，洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Gao Longzhi, style name Yanxing, was a native of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Longzhi, styled Yanxing, was a native of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 為閹人徐成養子。

translations.literal: He was the adopted son of the eunuch Xu Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was the adopted son of the eunuch Xu Cheng.

sentences.zh: 少時，以賃升為事。

translations.literal: In youth he worked as a hired hand carrying goods upstairs.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he worked as a porter hired to carry loads upstairs.

sentences.zh: 或曰父幹為姑婿高氏所養，因從其姓。

translations.literal: Some say his father Gan was raised by his aunt's husband's Gao clan and therefore took their surname.
translations.idiomatic: Some say his father Gan had been raised by his aunt's husband's Gao family and had taken their surname.

sentences.zh: 隆之後有參定功。

translations.literal: Longzhi later had merit in participating in the settlement.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhi later earned merit in the founding settlement.

sentences.zh: 神武命為弟，仍雲勃海蓚人。

translations.literal: Gao Huan ordered that he be treated as a younger brother and still declared him a native of Su in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan treated him as a younger brother and had him recorded as a native of Su in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 幹贈司徒公。

translations.literal: Gan was posthumously made Duke Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Gan was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 隆之身長八尺，美須髯，深沉有志氣。

translations.literal: Longzhi was eight chi tall, with fine beard and whiskers, deep and reserved, with ambition and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhi stood eight chi tall, with a fine beard, a reserved depth of manner, and strong ambition.

sentences.zh: 初，行台於暉引為郎中，與神武深相結托。

translations.literal: At first the Mobile Secretariat's Yu Hui brought him in as a gentleman-attendant; he and Gao Huan formed a deep bond of trust.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Hui of the mobile secretariat first brought him in as a gentleman-attendant, and he and Gao Huan formed a deep bond.

sentences.zh: 後從起兵于山東，累遷并州刺史，入為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Later he followed in raising troops in Shandong, was promoted in succession to governor of Bingzhou, and entered as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Gao Huan in raising troops in Shandong, rose to governor of Bingzhou, and entered court as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時初給人田，權貴皆占良美，貧弱咸受脊薄，隆之啟神武，更均平之。

translations.literal: At the time fields were first allotted to people; the powerful all seized the good land while the poor and weak all received lean plots; Longzhi memorialized Gao Huan to redistribute them more evenly.
translations.idiomatic: When land was first allotted, the powerful seized the best fields while the poor got the worst. Longzhi petitioned Gao Huan for a fairer distribution.

sentences.zh: 又領營構大將，以十萬夫徹洛陽宮殿，運於鄴，構營之制，皆委隆之。

translations.literal: He also led as Grand Marshal for Construction, using a hundred thousand laborers to dismantle the Luoyang palaces and transport them to Ye; the design of construction was all entrusted to Longzhi.
translations.idiomatic: As Grand Marshal for Construction he employed a hundred thousand men to dismantle Luoyang's palaces and move them to Ye; he controlled every detail of the rebuilding.

sentences.zh: 增築南城，周二十五里。

translations.literal: He enlarged and built the southern city, twenty-five li in circumference.
translations.idiomatic: He expanded the southern city to a circuit of twenty-five li.

sentences.zh: 以漳水近帝城。

translations.literal: Because the Zhang River was close to the imperial city.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Zhang River ran close to the imperial city,

sentences.zh: 起長堤以防泛溢。

translations.literal: he raised a long embankment to guard against flooding.
translations.idiomatic: he built a long embankment against flooding.

sentences.zh: 又鑿渠引漳水，周流城郭，造水碾磑並有利於時。

translations.literal: He also dug canals to draw the Zhang River to flow around the city walls and built water-powered mills and querns, all benefiting the age.
translations.idiomatic: He also cut canals to channel the Zhang around the walls and built water mills—works of real benefit to the time.

sentences.zh: 魏自孝昌之後，天下多難。

translations.literal: From the Xiaochang era onward in Wei, the realm had many troubles.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wei Xiaochang era the realm knew endless troubles.

sentences.zh: 刺史、太守皆為當部都督，雖無兵事，皆立佐僚，所在頗為煩擾。

translations.literal: Prefects and governors all became area commanders; though there were no military affairs, they all established assistant staffs, and everywhere was quite harassing.
translations.idiomatic: Every prefect and governor became a regional commander; even where there was no fighting they set up staffs, and the land groaned under the burden.

sentences.zh: 隆之請非實邊要，見兵馬者，悉斷之。

translations.literal: Longzhi requested that where it was not a true frontier need, wherever troops and horses were seen, all be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhi petitioned to strip military staffs from every post that was not a genuine frontier command.

sentences.zh: 又朝貴多假常侍以取貂蟬之飾，隆之自表解侍中，並陳諸假侍中服者，請亦罷之。

translations.literal: Moreover many court nobles falsely took the title of Regular Attendant to obtain the cicada and marten insignia; Longzhi himself memorialized to resign as Palace Attendant and also listed all who falsely wore Attendant garb, requesting that they too be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Many court grandees had falsely taken the title of Regular Attendant to wear the cicada insignia. Longzhi resigned his own Palace Attendant post and asked that all such false claimants be stopped as well.

sentences.zh: 詔皆如表。

translations.literal: An edict approved all as memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved all his requests.

sentences.zh: 自軍國多事，冒名竊官者，不可勝數，隆之奏請檢括，旬日獲五萬餘人。

translations.literal: Since military and state affairs were many, those who falsely assumed names and stole offices were beyond counting; Longzhi memorialized to investigate and within ten days seized more than fifty thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: With military and civil affairs in chaos, impostors holding office were beyond count. Longzhi petitioned for a review and in ten days uncovered more than fifty thousand.

sentences.zh: 而群小訁雚囂，隆之懼而止。

translations.literal: But the petty crowd clamored and made an uproar; Longzhi feared and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men raised an uproar, and Longzhi, afraid, abandoned the effort.

sentences.zh: 詔監起居事，進位司徒。

translations.literal: By edict he oversaw the recording of imperial activity and was promoted to Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to supervise the recording of imperial activity and promoted to Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 武定中，除尚書令，遷太保。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era he was appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs and promoted to Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: During Wuding he was made Director of the Department of State Affairs and then Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 文襄作宰，風俗肅清。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang served as chief minister, customs were made austere and pure.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng took power as chief minister, public morals were sharply tightened.

sentences.zh: 隆之時有受納，文襄於尚書省大加責讓。

translations.literal: Longzhi at times accepted bribes; Wenxiang at the Department of State Affairs greatly reproved and blamed him.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhi still took bribes at times, and Gao Cheng publicly rebuked him in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，進爵為王。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his noble rank was advanced to king.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi was founded he was advanced to prince.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官錄尚書事，領大宗正卿，監國史。

translations.literal: Soon with his original office he recorded affairs of the Department of State Affairs, headed the Grand Director of the Imperial Clan, and supervised the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he recorded Department affairs in his existing post, headed the imperial clan directorate, and supervised the national history.

sentences.zh: 隆之性好小巧，至於公家羽儀，百戲服制，時有改易，不循典故。

translations.literal: Longzhi by nature loved petty novelties; as for the state's regalia, and the costumes of the hundred entertainments, he at times altered them and did not follow ancient precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhi loved petty novelties; he altered state regalia and the costumes of court entertainments without regard for precedent.

sentences.zh: 時論非之。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion criticized this.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries criticized him for it.

sentences.zh: 於射堋土上立三人像，為壯勇之勢。

translations.literal: On the shooting mound's earthen bank he set up three human figures in a posture of stalwart valor.
translations.idiomatic: On the archery mound he set up three human figures in heroic poses.

sentences.zh: 文宣曾至東山，因射，謂隆之曰：「堋上可作猛獸，以存古義，何為終日射人？」

translations.literal: Wenxuan once came to the Eastern Hills and, while shooting, said to Longzhi: "On the mound one could set up fierce beasts to preserve the ancient meaning—why spend the whole day shooting at men?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan once visited the Eastern Hills and, while shooting, said to Longzhi, "The mound should hold beasts, as the ancients did—why spend all day shooting at men?"

sentences.zh: 隆之無以對。

translations.literal: Longzhi had nothing to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhi had no answer.

sentences.zh: 先是，文襄委任崔暹、崔季舒等。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wenxiang had entrusted Cui Xian, Cui Jishu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Gao Cheng had entrusted Cui Xian, Cui Jishu, and others.

sentences.zh: 及文襄崩，隆之啟文宣，並欲害之，不見許。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang died, Longzhi memorialized Wenxuan that they should all be killed; this was not approved.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng died, Longzhi urged Wenxuan to have them all killed, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 文宣以隆之舊齒，委以政事。

translations.literal: Wenxuan, because Longzhi was an elder of long standing, entrusted him with government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan, honoring Longzhi's long service, still entrusted him with government.

sentences.zh: 隆之子淫于楊遵彥前妻，帝妹也，故遵彥讒毀日至。

translations.literal: Longzhi's son debauched Yang Zunyan's former wife, who was the emperor's sister, and so Zunyan's slander came day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhi's son had an affair with Yang Zunyan's former wife—the emperor's own sister—so Zunyan's slanders came daily.

sentences.zh: 崔季舒等仍以前隙，譖云：「隆之每見訴訟者，輒加哀矜之意，以示非己能裁。」

translations.literal: Cui Jishu and others, still because of old grievances, slandered him, saying: "Whenever Longzhi sees litigants, he always shows pity and compassion to show that he himself cannot decide.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Jishu and others, nursing old grudges, accused him: "Whenever Longzhi sees litigants he shows pity—to suggest that he cannot decide cases himself.

sentences.zh: 文宣以其受任既久，知有冤狀，便宜申浟，何過要名，非大臣義。

translations.literal: Wenxuan said: "He has long held office and knows when there are wrongful cases; he should simply grant redress—what fault is there in seeking a name? This is not a minister's duty."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "He has served long and knows when men are wronged; he should simply grant relief. What fault is there in seeking a good name? That is not how a minister should act."

sentences.zh: 天保五年，禁止尚書省。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianbao the Department of State Affairs was sealed off.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianbao the Department of State Affairs was sealed off.

sentences.zh: 隆之曾與元昶宴，語昶曰：「與王交遊，當死生不相背。」

translations.literal: Longzhi had once feasted with Yuan Chang and said to Chang: "In friendship with you, my lord, I would not turn my back in life or death."
translations.idiomatic: Longzhi had once feasted with Yuan Chang and told him, "In friendship with you, my lord, I would stand by you in life and death."

sentences.zh: 人有密言之者。

translations.literal: Someone reported this in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported this in secret.

sentences.zh: 又帝未登庸日，隆之意常侮帝。

translations.literal: Moreover, before the emperor had taken the throne, Longzhi's intent had often been to slight the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, before the emperor took the throne Longzhi had often treated him with contempt.

sentences.zh: 帝將受禪，大臣咸言未可，隆之又在其中。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to receive the abdication, the great ministers all said it was not yet possible, and Longzhi was among them.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to accept the abdication, the great ministers—including Longzhi—had all urged delay.

sentences.zh: 帝深銜之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply harbored resentment against him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bore a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 因此大怒，罵曰：「徐家老公！」

translations.literal: Because of this he was greatly enraged and cursed: "Old man of the Xu family!"
translations.idiomatic: In his rage he cursed, "You old Xu-family wretch!"

sentences.zh: 令壯士築百餘拳，放出。

translations.literal: He ordered strong men to beat him more than a hundred blows with clubs and then released him.
translations.idiomatic: He had brawny men beat him more than a hundred blows with clubs, then released him.

sentences.zh: 渴，將飲水，人止之，隆之曰：「今日何在！」

translations.literal: Thirsty, he was about to drink water; people stopped him. Longzhi said: "Where am I today!"
translations.idiomatic: Thirsty, he started to drink; attendants tried to stop him. Longzhi said, "Where am I today?

sentences.zh: 遂飲之。

translations.literal: He then drank it.
translations.idiomatic: Then he drank it.

sentences.zh: 因從駕，死于路中。

translations.literal: Thereupon he followed the imperial carriage and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the imperial procession and died on the road.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉、太保、陽夏王，竟不得諡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant, Grand Guardian, and Prince of Yangxia, but in the end received no posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant and Grand Guardian and enfeoffed as Prince of Yangxia, but was denied a posthumous name.

sentences.zh: 隆之雖不學涉，而欽尚文雅，搢紳名流，必存禮接。

translations.literal: Although Longzhi had not studied broadly, he revered and esteemed refinement; gentry and famous men he always treated with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Though Longzhi was no scholar, he revered culture and always received gentry and men of note with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 寡姊為尼，事之如母。

translations.literal: His widowed elder sister became a nun; he served her as a mother.
translations.idiomatic: His widowed elder sister had become a nun, and he treated her as he would a mother.

sentences.zh: 訓督諸子，必先文義。

translations.literal: In instructing and supervising his sons, he always put literary learning first.
translations.idiomatic: When he tutored and disciplined his sons, he always began with letters and moral principle.

sentences.zh: 世以此稱之。

translations.literal: The world praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: On this account he won wide renown.

sentences.zh: 文宣末年，多猜害，追忿隆之，執其子司徒中兵慧登等二十人於前。

translations.literal: In the late years of Wenxuan, when suspicion and harm were rife, bearing a grudge against Longzhi, he seized before him Longzhi's son Huideng, chief clerk of the household troops of the Minister over the Masses, and nineteen others.
translations.idiomatic: In Wenxuan's last years, when the court seethed with suspicion and slaughter, the emperor, still nursing wrath against Gao Longzhi, had Longzhi's son Huideng—chief clerk of the Minister over the Masses' household troops—and nineteen others brought before him.

sentences.zh: 慧登言乞命，帝曰：「不得已。」

translations.literal: Huideng pleaded for his life; the emperor said: "There is no help for it.
translations.idiomatic: Huideng begged for his life. The emperor said, "It cannot be helped.

sentences.zh: 以鞭扣鞍，一時頭絕，並投之漳水。

translations.literal: Striking the saddle with his whip, in an instant their heads were severed, and all were cast into the Zhang River.
translations.idiomatic: He struck the saddle with his whip; in a single moment their heads were struck off, and all were thrown into the Zhang River.

sentences.zh: 發隆之塚，出屍，其貌不敗。

translations.literal: They opened Longzhi's tomb and removed the corpse; his features had not decayed.
translations.idiomatic: They opened Gao Longzhi's tomb and brought out the body—his face had not spoiled.

sentences.zh: 斬骸骨焚之，棄於漳流。

translations.literal: They cut up the remains, burned them, and discarded them in the waters of the Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: They hacked the bones apart, burned them, and cast the ashes into the Zhang's current.

sentences.zh: 天下冤之。

translations.literal: All under Heaven deemed it a grievous injustice.
translations.idiomatic: The realm looked on and called it a monstrous wrong.

sentences.zh: 隆之嗣遂絕。

translations.literal: Thus Longzhi's line came to an end.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Longzhi's line was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 乾明中，詔其兄子子遠為隆之後，襲爵陽夏王，還其財產。

translations.literal: In the Qianming era, an edict appointed his nephew Ziyuan as Longzhi's heir, to inherit the title Prince of Yangxia, and restored his property.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianming, an edict made his nephew Ziyuan heir to Gao Longzhi, restored the title Prince of Yangxia, and returned his estates.

sentences.zh: 隆之見信神武，性陰毒，儀同三司崔孝芬以結婚姻不果，太僕卿任集同知營構，頗相乖異；

translations.literal: Longzhi had gained Gao Huan's trust; by nature he was secretive and cruel. Honorary Three Grand Ministers Cui Xiaofen, when a marriage alliance failed to materialize, and Minister of Public Works Ren Ji, who jointly managed military construction affairs, became quite estranged from him;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Longzhi had won Gao Huan's confidence, yet his nature was covert and venomous. Cui Xiaofen, Honorary Three Grand Ministers, failed to secure a marriage tie with him; Ren Ji, Minister of Public Works, who shared charge of military construction, grew sharply at odds with him;

sentences.zh: 瀛州刺史元晏請托不遂。

translations.literal: Yuan Yan, Governor of Yingzhou, likewise failed to obtain what he had sought through entreaty.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yan, governor of Yingzhou, likewise could not obtain what he sought by petition.

sentences.zh: 並構成其罪，誅害之，終至家門殄滅。

translations.literal: They all fabricated charges against him, had him executed, until at last his entire household was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Together they contrived his crimes and had him put to death, until his whole house was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 論者謂有報應焉。

translations.literal: Commentators held that this was retribution.
translations.idiomatic: Observers said retribution had come due.

sentences.zh: 司馬子如，字遵業，自雲河內溫人也，徙居雲中，因家焉。

translations.literal: Sima Ziru, courtesy name Zunye, was originally from Wen in Henei; he moved to Yunzhong and made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ziru, styled Zunye, was a native of Wen in Henei who moved to Yunzhong and settled there.

sentences.zh: 子如初為懷朔鎮省事，與齊神武相結托，分義甚深。

translations.literal: When Ziru first served as administrative clerk at Huaiyuan Garrison, he and Gao Huan formed a bond of deep mutual trust.
translations.idiomatic: Ziru began as a clerk at Huaiyuan Garrison; he and Gao Huan pledged themselves to each other, and their bond ran very deep.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，北州淪陷，子如南奔肆州，為爾硃榮所禮，封平遙子，稍遷大行台郎。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era, when the northern provinces fell, Ziru fled south to Sizhou, was treated with honor by Erzhu Rong, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingyao, and gradually promoted to secretary of the Grand Expeditionary Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaochang, when the northern provinces were lost, Ziru fled south to Sizhou. Erzhu Rong received him with honor, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Pingyao, and gradually raised him to secretary of the Grand Expeditionary Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 榮死，隨榮妻子與爾硃世隆等走出京城。

translations.literal: When Rong died, he fled the capital with Rong's wife and children and Erzhu Shilong and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong died, Ziru fled the capital with Rong's wife and children, together with Erzhu Shilong and the rest.

sentences.zh: 節閔帝立，以前後功，進爵陽平郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jiemin ascended the throne, in recognition of his earlier and later services, his noble rank was advanced to Duke of Yangping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jiemin took the throne, his earlier and later merits were rewarded with promotion to Duke of Yangping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 神武入洛，以為大行台尚書，朝夕左右，參知軍國。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan entered Luoyang, Ziru was appointed Grand Expeditionary Headquarters Minister, attending him morning and night and participating in military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan entered Luoyang, Ziru was made minister of the Grand Expeditionary Headquarters, kept at his side day and night, and consulted on military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 天平初，除尚書左僕射、開府，與高岳、孫騰、高隆之等共知朝政，甚見信重。

translations.literal: Early in the Tianping era, he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and granted an opening office; together with Gao Yue, Sun Teng, Gao Longzhi, and others he shared authority over court governance, and was greatly trusted and esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianping he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and granted an opening office. With Gao Yue, Sun Teng, Gao Longzhi, and others he shared governance of the court, and was deeply trusted.

sentences.zh: 神武鎮晉陽，子如時往謁見。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan held Jinyang, Ziru would from time to time go there to pay his respects.
translations.idiomatic: While Gao Huan held Jinyang, Ziru would visit him from time to time.

sentences.zh: 及還，神武、武明後俱有齎遺，率以為常。

translations.literal: On returning, both Gao Huan and the Lady Wuming would send him gifts—this became his usual custom.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he returned, Gao Huan and Lady Wuming both sent him gifts; it became his fixed custom.

sentences.zh: 子如性既豪爽，兼恃恩舊，簿領之務，與奪任情，公然受納。

translations.literal: Ziru's nature was bold and open; relying moreover on old favor, in matters of registers and accounts he granted or withheld as he pleased and openly accepted bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Ziru was by nature bold and expansive, and, trusting in old favor besides, handled ledgers and appointments as whim dictated and took bribes openly.

sentences.zh: 興和中，以北道行台巡檢諸州守令已下，至定州，斬深澤令；

translations.literal: In the Xinghe era, as Northern Route Grand Expeditionary Inspector, he toured and inspected officials from prefectural governors and magistrates downward; reaching Dingzhou, he executed the magistrate of Shenze;
translations.idiomatic: In Xinghe, as inspector of the Northern Route Grand Expeditionary Headquarters, he toured the provinces and examined officials down to prefects and magistrates. At Dingzhou he executed the magistrate of Shenze;

sentences.zh: 至冀州，斬東光令，皆稽留時刻，致之極刑。

translations.literal: reaching Jizhou, he executed the magistrate of Dongguang—all for delays measured in hours, inflicted with the ultimate penalty.
translations.idiomatic: at Jizhou he executed the magistrate of Dongguang—both for delays counted in hours, punished with the utmost severity.

sentences.zh: 進退少不合旨者，便令武士頓曳，白刃臨頸。

translations.literal: Anyone whose demeanor fell even slightly short of his wishes would be seized and dragged by armed retainers, a naked blade at the throat.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever in bearing or speech fell even slightly short of his wish was seized and dragged by armed men, a naked blade at the throat.

sentences.zh: 士庶惶懼，不知所為。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners alike were stricken with fear, uncertain what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and common folk alike were terrified, not knowing what to do.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the post of Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to the post of Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 及文襄輔政，以賄為御史中尉崔暹劾，在獄一宿而發皆白。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang assumed regency, he was impeached for bribery by Censor-in-Chief Cui Xian; after one night in prison, his hair turned completely white.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng took charge of government, Cui Xian, Censor-in-Chief, impeached him for bribery. After one night in prison, his hair had turned entirely white.

sentences.zh: 辭曰：「司馬子如本從夏州策一杖投相王，王給露車一乘，觠牸牛犢。

translations.literal: He declared: "Sima Ziru originally came from Xiazhou leaning on a staff to seek out the Prince of Xiang; the Prince gave him one open cart and a spotted hornless cow with calf.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Sima Ziru originally came from Xiazhou leaning on a single staff to seek out the Prince of Xiang. The Prince gave him one open cart and a spotted hornless cow with her calf.

sentences.zh: 犢在道死，唯觠角存。

translations.literal: The calf died on the road; only its spotted horns remained.
translations.idiomatic: The calf died on the road; only the spotted horns were left.

sentences.zh: 此外，皆人上取得。」

translations.literal: Apart from this, everything else was obtained from others above me.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else came from gifts from my superiors.

sentences.zh: 神武書敕文襄曰：「馬令是吾故舊，汝宜寬之。」

translations.literal: Gao Huan wrote instructing Wenxiang: "Sima is an old friend of mine—you should treat him leniently."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan wrote Gao Cheng: "Sima is an old friend of mine. You should show him leniency."

sentences.zh: 文襄駐馬行街，以出子如，脫其鎖。

translations.literal: Wenxiang reined in his horse on the street outside and had Ziru released, removing his chains.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng halted his horse in the street outside, had Ziru brought out, and removed his fetters.

sentences.zh: 子如懼曰：「非作事邪？」

translations.literal: Ziru said in fear: "Was this not a capital case?
translations.idiomatic: Ziru said in alarm, "Was this not a matter for execution?

sentences.zh: 於是，除削官爵。

translations.literal: Thereupon his offices and titles were stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon his offices and titles were removed.

sentences.zh: 神武后見之，哀其憔悴，以膝承其首，親為擇虱，賜酒百瓶，羊五百口，粳米五百石。

translations.literal: When the Lady Wuming saw him, pitying his wasted state, she took his head upon her knee and picked lice for him herself, granting him a hundred jars of wine, five hundred sheep, and five hundred shi of polished rice.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Wuming saw him, she pitied his haggard state, rested his head on her knee, picked lice for him with her own hands, and gave him a hundred jars of wine, five hundred sheep, and five hundred shi of polished rice.

sentences.zh: 子如曰：「無事尚被囚幾死，若受此，豈有生路邪？」

translations.literal: Ziru said: "Though guilty of nothing I was nearly killed in prison—if I accept these gifts, where will I find a way to live?
translations.idiomatic: Ziru said, "Though I had done nothing, I was nearly killed in prison. If I accept this, what road to life remains?

sentences.zh: 未幾，起行冀州事，能自改厲，甚有聲譽。

translations.literal: Before long he was restored to office to administer Jizhou affairs; able to reform himself sternly, he gained considerable renown.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored to office to handle Jizhou affairs. He reformed himself sternly and won a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 詔復官爵，別封野王縣男。

translations.literal: An edict restored his offices and titles and separately enfeoffed him as Baron of Yewang County.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored his offices and titles and separately enfeoffed him as Baron of Yewang County.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，以翼贊功，別封須昌縣公。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, for his supporting merit he was separately enfeoffed as Duke of Xuchang County.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi was founded he was separately enfeoffed Duke of Xuchang County for his supporting merit.

sentences.zh: 尋除司空。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 消難字道融。

translations.literal: Xiaonan, courtesy name Daorong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaonan, styled Daorong.

sentences.zh: 幼聰慧，微涉經史，有風神，好自矯飾，以求名譽。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and sharp; he dipped lightly into the classics and histories, had an air of grace, and liked to adorn himself to win renown.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he was clever; he touched lightly on the classics and histories, carried himself with grace, and liked to polish his manner to win a name.

sentences.zh: 子如既當朝貴盛，消難亦愛賓客，邢子才、王元景、魏收、陸仰、崔瞻等皆遊其門。

translations.literal: Once Ziru stood among the great of the court, Xiaonan too delighted in hosting guests—Xing Zicao, Wang Yuanjing, Wei Shou, Lu Yang, Cui Zhan, and others all frequented his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ziru stood at the height of court power, Xiaonan too loved to gather guests. Xing Zicao, Wang Yuanjing, Wei Shou, Lu Yang, Cui Zhan, and others all passed through his door.

sentences.zh: 稍遷光祿卿，出為北豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Director of the Imperial Household and sent out as Governor of North Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose gradually to Director of the Imperial Household, then went out as governor of North Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 文宣末年，昏虐滋甚，消難常有自全之謀，曲意撫納，頗為百姓所附。

translations.literal: In the late years of Wenxuan, when tyranny grew fiercer, Xiaonan often plotted means of self-preservation, bending himself to soothe and win people, and was rather well beloved by the common folk.
translations.idiomatic: In Wenxuan's last years, as cruelty deepened, Xiaonan often plotted how to save himself, bending to soothe and win people, and won no small attachment from the common folk.

sentences.zh: 不能廉潔，為御史所劾。

translations.literal: He could not remain incorrupt; he was impeached by the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He could not keep himself clean; the censorate impeached him.

sentences.zh: 又尚公主，而情好不睦，公主訴之。

translations.literal: He had also married a princess, but affection between them was poor; the princess brought complaint against him.
translations.idiomatic: He had also married a princess, yet affection between them was cold; the princess lodged complaint against him.

sentences.zh: 屬文宣在并州，驛召上党王煥，煥懼害，斬使者東奔，鄴中大擾，後竟獲於濟州。

translations.literal: Just then Wenxuan was at Bingzhou; by imperial post he summoned Prince Huan of Shangdang. Huan, fearing harm, slew the messenger and fled east, throwing Ye into great turmoil—he was finally captured at Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wenxuan was at Bingzhou and summoned by post Prince Huan of Shangdang. Huan, fearing death, killed the messenger and fled east; Ye was thrown into uproar, and he was finally taken at Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 煥之初走，朝士疑赴成皋，云：「若與司馬北豫連謀，必為國患。」

translations.literal: When Huan first fled, court officials suspected he had gone to Chenggao, saying: "If he joins in conspiracy with Sima of North Yuzhou, he will surely become a peril to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan first fled, court officials suspected he had gone to Chenggao and said, "If he joins Sima of North Yuzhou in conspiracy, he will surely become a danger to the state.

sentences.zh: 此言達于文宣，頗見疑。

translations.literal: This report reached Wenxuan, and Xiaonan fell under considerable suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: This reached Wenxuan, and Xiaonan came under heavy suspicion.

sentences.zh: 消難懼，密令所親人河東裴藻間行入關，請降。

translations.literal: Xiaonan grew afraid and secretly sent his confidant Pei Zao of Hedong by hidden route across the pass to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaonan, in fear, secretly sent his trusted man Pei Zao of Hedong by hidden route through the passes to offer surrender.

sentences.zh: 入周，封滎陽郡公，累遷大司寇。

translations.literal: Entering Zhou, he was enfeoffed Duke of Xingyang Commandery and rose cumulatively to Grand Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Zhou, he was enfeoffed Duke of Xingyang Commandery and rose step by step to Grand Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 從武帝東伐，還除梁州總管。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Wu on the eastern campaign, upon return he was appointed Governor-General of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Wu on the eastern campaign and, on returning, was appointed governor-general of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 大象初，遷大後丞，女為靜帝后。

translations.literal: At the start of the Daxiang era, he was moved to Grand Empress's Secretary; his daughter became empress to Emperor Jing.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Daxiang he was moved to Grand Empress's Secretary; his daughter became empress to Emperor Jing.

sentences.zh: 尋出為雲阝州總管。

translations.literal: Shortly after he was sent out as Governor-General of Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was sent out as governor-general of Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 及隋文帝輔政，消難乃與蜀公尉遲回合勢舉兵，使其子永質于陳，以求援。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui held the regency, Xiaonan joined forces with Duke of Shu Yuchi Cong to raise troops, sending his son Yong as hostage to Chen to seek aid.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui held the regency, Xiaonan joined Duke of Shu Yuchi Cong in raising arms, sending his son Yong as hostage to Chen to seek help.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝命襄州總管王誼討之，消難奔陳。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen ordered Wang Yi, Governor-General of Xiangzhou, to suppress him; Xiaonan fled to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen ordered Wang Yi, governor-general of Xiangzhou, to suppress him. Xiaonan fled to Chen.

sentences.zh: 位司空，隨郡公。

translations.literal: He held the rank of Minister of Works and was Duke of Sui Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He held the rank of Minister of Works and was Duke of Sui Commandery.

sentences.zh: 初，隋武元帝之迎消難，結為兄弟，情好甚篤，隋文每以叔禮事之。

translations.literal: At first, when Emperor Wu of Chen welcomed Xiaonan, they swore brotherhood and affection ran deep; Emperor Wen of Sui always treated him with the courtesy due an uncle.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Emperor Wu of Chen received Xiaonan, they swore brotherhood and were deeply fond of each other; Emperor Wen of Sui always treated him with the courtesy due an uncle.

sentences.zh: 及平陳，消難至，特免死配為樂戶，二旬而免。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified and Xiaonan arrived, he was specially spared death and assigned as a music-house serf; after twenty days he was released.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen was pacified and Xiaonan came in, he was specially spared death and assigned to the music-house registers; after twenty days he was released.

sentences.zh: 猶以舊恩，特被引見。

translations.literal: Still on account of old kindness, he was granted a special audience.
translations.idiomatic: Still on account of old favor, he was granted a special audience.

sentences.zh: 尋卒於家。

translations.literal: Before long he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died at home.

sentences.zh: 消難性貪淫，輕於去就，故世言反覆者，皆以方之。

translations.literal: Xiaonan was greedy and licentious by nature, light in choosing sides—hence when people speak of the inconstant, they take him as their measure.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaonan was greedy and licentious by nature and quick to change sides; hence when people speak of the fickle, they measure them against him.

sentences.zh: 其妻高，齊神武女也，在鄴極加禮敬，入關便相棄薄。

translations.literal: His wife was a Gao, daughter of Gao Huan; in Ye she was treated with utmost respect, but once he crossed into Guan he cast her aside coldly.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was a Gao, daughter of Gao Huan. In Ye she had been treated with the greatest respect; once he entered the passes he cast her off coldly.

sentences.zh: 及赴雲阝州，留妻及三子在京。

translations.literal: When he went to Yunzhou, he left his wife and three sons in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When he went to Yunzhou, he left his wife and three sons in the capital.

sentences.zh: 妻言于文帝曰：「滎陽公攜寵自隨，必不顧妻子，願防慮之。」

translations.literal: His wife said to Emperor Wen: "The Duke of Xingyang takes his favorites with him and will surely neglect wife and children—I beg you to take precautions.
translations.idiomatic: His wife told Emperor Wen, "The Duke of Xingyang takes his favorites with him and will surely not care for wife and children. I beg Your Majesty to guard against this.

sentences.zh: 及消難入陳，高母子因此獲免。

translations.literal: When Xiaonan entered Chen, the Gao mother and sons were thereby spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaonan fled into Chen, the Gao mother and sons were spared on that account.

sentences.zh: 子譚，即高氏所生，以消難勳，拜儀同大將軍，坐消難除名。

translations.literal: His son Tan, born of the Gao lady, on account of Xiaonan's merit was appointed Honorary Grand General; on account of Xiaonan he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tan, born of the Gao lady, was appointed Honorary Grand General for Xiaonan's merit, then struck from the rolls because of Xiaonan.

sentences.zh: 裴藻字文芳。

translations.literal: Pei Zao, courtesy name Wenfang.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zao, styled Wenfang.

sentences.zh: 少機辨，有不羈之志，為子如太傅主簿。

translations.literal: From youth quick-witted and clever, with a free-ranging spirit, he served as chief clerk to Ziru when the latter was Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was quick and sharp, with an untamed spirit; he served as chief clerk to Ziru when Ziru was Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 消難鎮北豫，又以為中兵參軍。

translations.literal: When Xiaonan held North Yuzhou, he was again appointed household troops adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaonan held North Yuzhou, he was again made adjutant of the household troops.

sentences.zh: 入周，封聞喜縣男，除晉州刺史。

translations.literal: Entering Zhou, he was enfeoffed Baron of Wenxi County and appointed Governor of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Zhou, he was enfeoffed Baron of Wenxi County and appointed governor of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 子如兄纂。

translations.literal: Ziru's elder brother Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ziru's elder brother was Zuan.

sentences.zh: 纂長子世雲，輕險無行。

translations.literal: Zuan's eldest son Shiyun was frivolous and reckless, without proper conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's eldest son Shiyun was light, reckless, and without principle.

sentences.zh: 累遷潁州刺史，肆行奸穢。

translations.literal: After repeated promotions he became Governor of Yingzhou and there practiced debauchery wantonly.
translations.idiomatic: Raised step by step to governor of Yingzhou, he there gave free rein to lewdness and corruption.

sentences.zh: 將見推，懼，遂從侯景。

translations.literal: When he was about to be impeached, in fear he joined Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When impeachment was imminent, he took fright and went over to Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 文襄猶以子如恩舊，免其諸弟死罪，徙北邊。

translations.literal: Wenxiang still, for Ziru's old favor, spared his younger brothers the death penalty and exiled them to the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng, still honoring Ziru's old tie, spared his younger brothers death and exiled them to the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 世雲以侯景敗于渦陽，復有異志，為景所殺。

translations.literal: Shiyun, after Hou Jing's defeat at Woyang, again harbored treacherous designs and was killed by Jing.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing was defeated at Woyang, Shiyun again harbored disloyal designs and was killed by Jing.

sentences.zh: 世雲弟膺之。

translations.literal: Shiyun's younger brother Yingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyun's younger brother was Yingzhi.

sentences.zh: 膺之字仲慶。

translations.literal: Yingzhi, courtesy name Zhongqing.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhi, styled Zhongqing.

sentences.zh: 美須髯，有風貌，好學，厚自封植，神氣甚高。

translations.literal: Handsome in beard and whiskers, with a commanding presence, he loved learning and cultivated himself deeply; his bearing was lofty indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Fine of beard and whiskers, with a striking presence, he loved learning and cultivated himself deeply; his spirit stood very high.

sentences.zh: 曆中書、黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He served successively as Secretariat Gentleman and Palace Gate Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Secretariat Gentleman and Palace Gate Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 天平中，叔父子如執鈞當軸。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era, his uncle Ziru held the balance of power.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping his uncle Ziru held the scales of power.

sentences.zh: 膺之既宰相猶子，兼自有名望，所與遊集，盡一時名流。

translations.literal: Yingzhi was both a grand minister's nephew and himself a man of name and standing; those with whom he gathered were all luminaries of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhi was both a chief minister's nephew and a man of name in his own right; those who gathered with him were all leading figures of the day.

sentences.zh: 與邢子才、王景等，並為莫逆之交。

translations.literal: With Xing Zicao, Wang Jing, and others he formed bonds of the closest friendship.
translations.idiomatic: With Xing Zicao, Wang Jing, and others he was on terms of the closest friendship.

sentences.zh: 及兄世雲陷於逆亂，期親皆應誅。

translations.literal: When his elder brother Shiyun fell into rebellion, all kin within the mourning circle ought by law to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother Shiyun fell into rebellion, all kin within the circle of mourning were liable to execution.

sentences.zh: 膺之及諸弟並有人才，為朝廷所惜，文襄特減死徙近鎮。

translations.literal: Yingzhi and his brothers all possessed talent; the court prized them, and Wenxiang specially commuted death to exile at nearby garrison towns.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhi and his brothers all had talent, and the court was loath to lose them; Gao Cheng specially reduced the sentence from death to exile at nearby garrisons.

sentences.zh: 文宣嗣業，得還。

translations.literal: When Wenxuan succeeded to the enterprise, they were permitted to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxuan succeeded to power, they were allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，子如別封須昌縣公，回授膺之。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, Ziru's separate enfeoffment as Duke of Xuchang County was transferred to Yingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi was founded, Ziru's separate enfeoffment as Duke of Xuchang County was transferred to Yingzhi.

sentences.zh: 子如撫愛甚慈，膺之昆季，事之如父。

translations.literal: Ziru nurtured them with great affection; Yingzhi and his brothers served him as a father.
translations.idiomatic: Ziru cherished them with great tenderness; Yingzhi and his brothers served him as they would a father.

sentences.zh: 性方古，不會俗舊。

translations.literal: His nature was upright and old-fashioned; he would not conform to worldly customs.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was upright and antique; he would not bend to the customs of the age.

sentences.zh: 與楊愔同為黃門郎。

translations.literal: He and Yang Yin served together as Palace Gate Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yang Yin served together as Palace Gate Gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 至愔為尚書令，抗禮如初。

translations.literal: When Yin became Director of the Department of State Affairs, Yingzhi treated him with the same equality as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin became Director of the Department of State Affairs, Yingzhi still treated him as an equal, just as before.

sentences.zh: 愔嘗有從姊慘，尚書卿尹皆跪吊，膺之執手而出。

translations.literal: When Yin suffered the bereavement of a paternal cousin, directors and senior officials of the secretariat all knelt in condolence—Yingzhi grasped his hand and walked out.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin mourned a paternal cousin, directors and senior officials of the secretariat all knelt in condolence; Yingzhi took his hand and walked out.

sentences.zh: 曾路逢愔，威儀道引，乃於樹下側避之。

translations.literal: Once on the road he encountered Yin with full ceremonial escort; he stepped aside beneath a tree to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the road he met Yin with full ceremonial escort and stepped aside beneath a tree to avoid him.

sentences.zh: 愔于車望見，令呼謂曰：「兄何意避弟？」

translations.literal: Yin saw him from his carriage and had him called: "Brother, why do you shun your younger brother?
translations.idiomatic: Yin saw him from his carriage and had him summoned. "Brother, why do you avoid your younger brother?

sentences.zh: 膺之曰：「我自避赤棒，本不避卿。」

translations.literal: Yingzhi replied: "I was avoiding the red staves—I was not avoiding you at all."
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhi said, "I was avoiding the red staves. I was not avoiding you at all."

sentences.zh: 愔甚重之。

translations.literal: Yin thought very highly of him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin thought very highly of him.

sentences.zh: 然以其疏簡傲物，竟天保間，淪滯不齒。

translations.literal: However, because of his aloofness, simplicity, and disdain for others, throughout the Tianbao era he languished without rank among his peers.
translations.idiomatic: But because he was aloof, plain in manner, and disdainful of others, he languished throughout the Tianbao era without standing among his peers.

sentences.zh: 乾明中，除衛尉少卿，遷國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In Qianming he was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and transferred to Director of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianming he was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and promoted to Director of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 河清末，拜金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the end of Heqing he was granted the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Purple-girdle Privilege.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Heqing he was granted the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Purple-girdle Privilege.

sentences.zh: 患泄痢，積年不起。

translations.literal: He suffered from dysentery and for many years could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: He suffered from dysentery and for years could not get up.

sentences.zh: 武平中，就家拜儀同三司。

translations.literal: In Wuping he was appointed Bearer of the Three Special Equipments at his home.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuping he was appointed Bearer of the Three Special Equipments at his home.

sentences.zh: 班台之貴，近世專以賞勳勤，膺之雖為猥雜，名器猶重。

translations.literal: The honor of office in recent times was devoted solely to rewarding merit and diligence; though Yingzhi's appointment was unseemly and irregular, the insignia of rank was still weighty.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times high office had been reserved chiefly to reward merit and service; though Yingzhi's appointment was unseemly, the insignia of rank still carried weight.

sentences.zh: 初，司徒趙彥深起自孤微，為子如管記，膺之甚相忽略，不為之禮。

translations.literal: Initially, Minister of Education Zhao Yanshen had risen from solitude and low estate; when he served Ziru as chief clerk, Yingzhi greatly slighted him and showed him no courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhao Yanshen, Minister of Education, had risen from humble obscurity. When he served Ziru as chief clerk, Yingzhi greatly slighted him and showed him no courtesy.

sentences.zh: 及彥深為宰相，朝士輻氵奏，膺之自念，故被延請，永不至門，每與相見，捧袂而已。

translations.literal: When Yanshen became chief minister, court officials gathered around him in droves. Yingzhi reflected that he had once been invited but would never go to his door; whenever they met, he would merely clasp his sleeves in greeting.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanshen became chief minister, court officials flocked to him. Yingzhi remembered that he had once been invited, yet he never went to Yanshen's door; whenever they met, he merely clasped his sleeves in greeting.

sentences.zh: 太常卿段孝言，左丞相孝先之弟也，位望甚隆，嘗詣其弟幼之，舉座傾敬。

translations.literal: Duan Xiaoyan, Director of Ceremonies and younger brother of Left Chief Minister Xiaoxian, held lofty rank and prestige. Once when he called on his younger brother Youzhi, the whole assembly turned deferential.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Xiaoyan, Director of Ceremonies and younger brother of Left Chief Minister Xiaoxian, enjoyed great rank and prestige. Once when he called on his younger brother Youzhi, the whole company turned deferential.

sentences.zh: 膺之時牽疾，在外齋馮幾而坐，不為動容。

translations.literal: Yingzhi was then afflicted with illness; he sat in an outer hall fasting, leaning on an armrest, and showed no change of countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhi was then ill; he sat fasting in an outer hall, leaning on an armrest, and did not change expression.

sentences.zh: 直言：「我患痢久，太常不得致怪。」

translations.literal: He said plainly: "I have long suffered from dysentery—the Director of Ceremonies must not take offense.
translations.idiomatic: He said plainly, "I have long suffered from dysentery. The Director of Ceremonies must not take offense.

sentences.zh: 黃門郎陸杳，貴遊後進，膺之嘗與棋。

translations.literal: Lu Yao, a Palace Gate Gentleman and scion of the noble clans, was a rising young man with whom Yingzhi had once played chess.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yao, a Palace Gate Gentleman and scion of the noble clans, was a rising young man with whom Yingzhi had once played chess.

sentences.zh: 杳忽後至，寒溫而已，棋遂輟。

translations.literal: When Yao arrived late, Yingzhi exchanged only brief greetings, and the game was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao arrived late, Yingzhi exchanged only brief greetings, and the game was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 園宅閑素，門無雜客，性不飲酒，而不愛重賓遊。

translations.literal: His garden and residence were plain and quiet; no miscellaneous guests came to his gate. By nature he did not drink, nor did he prize heavy entertaining.
translations.idiomatic: His garden and home were plain and quiet, and no casual guests came to his gate. By nature he did not drink, nor did he care for lavish hospitality.

sentences.zh: 病久，不復堪讀書，或以奕棋永日。

translations.literal: His illness was long; he could no longer bear reading, and sometimes passed whole days playing chess.
translations.idiomatic: His illness dragged on; he could no longer bear to read, and sometimes passed whole days playing chess.

sentences.zh: 名士有素懷者，時相尋候。

translations.literal: Men of name with old affinities would from time to time call on him.
translations.idiomatic: Men of name with old affinities would from time to time call on him.

sentences.zh: 無雜言，唯論經史。

translations.literal: There was no idle talk—only discussion of the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: There was no idle talk—only discussion of the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 好讀《太玄經》，又注揚雄《蜀都賦》。

translations.literal: He loved reading the Classic of the Supreme Mystery and also annotated Yang Xiong's Rhapsody on the Shu Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He loved reading the Classic of the Supreme Mystery and also annotated Yang Xiong's Rhapsody on the Shu Capital.

sentences.zh: 每云：「我欲與揚子雲周旋。」

translations.literal: He often said: "I wish to keep company with Master Yang Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "I wish to keep company with Master Yang Yun.

sentences.zh: 患痢十七年，竟不愈。

translations.literal: He suffered dysentery for seventeen years and never recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He suffered dysentery for seventeen years and never recovered.

sentences.zh: 齊亡歲，以痢疾終。

translations.literal: In the year Qi fell, he died of dysentery.
translations.idiomatic: In the year Northern Qi fell, he died of dysentery.

sentences.zh: 膺之弟子瑞，為御史中丞，正色舉察，為朝廷所許。

translations.literal: Yingzhi's nephew Zirui served as Imperial Censor and, with stern rectitude in investigation and accusation, won the court's approval.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhi's nephew Zirui served as Imperial Censor; with stern rectitude in investigation and accusation, he won the court's approval.

sentences.zh: 以疾去職，就拜祠部尚書。

translations.literal: He left office on account of illness and was appointed at home Minister of Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He left office on account of illness and was appointed at home Minister of Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈儀同三司、瀛州刺史，諡曰文節。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously granted Bearer of the Three Special Equipments and Governor of Yingzhou, with the posthumous title Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously granted Bearer of the Three Special Equipments and Governor of Yingzhou, with the posthumous title Wenjie.

sentences.zh: 子瑞妻，陸令萱妹。

translations.literal: Zirui's wife was the younger sister of Lu Lingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zirui's wife was the younger sister of Lu Lingxuan.

sentences.zh: 及令萱得寵於後主，重贈子瑞開府儀同三司、中書監、溫縣伯。

translations.literal: When Lingxuan won favor with the Later Sovereign, Zirui was again posthumously granted Bearer of the Three Special Equipments with Bespoke Staff, Director of the Secretariat, and Baron of Wen County.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingxuan won favor with the Later Sovereign, Zirui was again posthumously granted Bearer of the Three Special Equipments with Bespoke Staff, Director of the Secretariat, and Baron of Wen County.

sentences.zh: 諸子亦並居顯職：同游，給事黃門侍郎；

translations.literal: His sons also all held prominent offices: Tongyou, Attendant Gentleman of the Palace Gate;
translations.idiomatic: His sons also all held prominent offices: Tongyou, Attendant Gentleman of the Palace Gate;

sentences.zh: 同回，太常少卿；

translations.literal: Tonghui, Vice Director of Ceremonies;
translations.idiomatic: Tonghui, Vice Director of Ceremonies;

sentences.zh: 同憲，通直常侍。

translations.literal: Tongxian, Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Tongxian, Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 同遊終為佳吏，隨開皇中，為尚書戶部侍郎，卒于遂州刺史。

translations.literal: Tongyou in the end proved an excellent official; in Sui Kaihuang he served as Vice Minister of the Revenue Section of the Masters of Writing and died as Governor of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tongyou in the end proved an excellent official; in Sui Kaihuang he served as Vice Minister of the Revenue Section of the Masters of Writing and died as Governor of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 子瑞弟幼之，清貞有行。

translations.literal: Zirui's younger brother Youzhi was pure, upright, and principled.
translations.idiomatic: Zirui's younger brother Youzhi was pure, upright, and principled.

sentences.zh: 武平末，為大理卿。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuping he served as Director of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuping he served as Director of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，卒于眉州刺史。

translations.literal: In Kaihuang he died as Governor of Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang he died as Governor of Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 竇泰，字世甯，太安捍殊人也。

translations.literal: Dou Tai, styled Shining, was a native of Taian Hanshu.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Tai, styled Shining, was a native of Taian Hanshu.

sentences.zh: 本出清河觀津胄。

translations.literal: His family originally descended from Guanjin in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: His family originally came from Guanjin in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 祖羅，魏統萬鎮將，因居北邊。

translations.literal: His grandfather Luo was commander of the Tongwan garrison in Wei and settled in the northern borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Luo was commander of the Tongwan garrison in Wei and settled in the northern borderlands.

sentences.zh: 父樂，魏末破六韓拔陵為亂，與鎮將楊鈞固守，遇害。

translations.literal: His father Yue, when at the end of Wei the rebel Boledu Buli raised disorder, held firm with the garrison commander Yang Jun and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yue, when at the end of Wei the rebel Boledu Buli raised disorder, held firm with the garrison commander Yang Jun and was killed.

sentences.zh: 泰貴，追贈司徒。

translations.literal: When Tai rose to eminence, [Yue] was posthumously granted the title Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Tai rose to eminence, his father was posthumously granted the title Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 初，泰母夢風雷暴起，若有雨狀。

translations.literal: At first Tai's mother dreamed that wind and thunder burst forth, as though rain were coming.
translations.idiomatic: At first Tai's mother dreamed that wind and thunder burst forth, as though rain were coming.

sentences.zh: 出庭觀之，見電光奪目，駛雨沾灑。

translations.literal: She went out into the courtyard to watch and saw dazzling lightning and driving rain.
translations.idiomatic: She went out into the courtyard to watch and saw dazzling lightning and driving rain.

sentences.zh: 寤而驚汗，遂有娠。

translations.literal: She woke in a sweat of alarm and then conceived.
translations.idiomatic: She woke in a sweat of alarm and then conceived.

sentences.zh: 期而不產，大懼。

translations.literal: The term passed without her giving birth, and she was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The term passed without her giving birth, and she was greatly afraid.

sentences.zh: 有巫曰：「度河湔裙，產子必易。」

translations.literal: A shaman said: "Cross the river and wash your skirt—the birth will come easily.
translations.idiomatic: A shaman said, "Cross the river and wash your skirt—the birth will come easily.

sentences.zh: 便向水所。

translations.literal: She went at once to the water.
translations.idiomatic: She went at once to the water.

sentences.zh: 忽見一人曰：「當生貴子，可徙而南。」

translations.literal: Suddenly a man appeared and said: "You are about to bear a noble son; move southward.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a man appeared and said, "You are about to bear a noble son. Move southward.

sentences.zh: 泰母從之，俄而生泰。

translations.literal: Tai's mother followed his advice, and soon afterward Tai was born.
translations.idiomatic: Tai's mother followed his advice, and soon afterward Tai was born.

sentences.zh: 及長，善騎射，有勇略。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he excelled at horsemanship and archery and possessed courage and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, he excelled at horsemanship and archery and possessed courage and stratagem.

sentences.zh: 泰父兄戰歿於鎮，泰身負骸骨歸爾硃榮。

translations.literal: Tai's father and elder brother died fighting at the garrison; Tai personally carried their bones back to Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Tai's father and elder brother died fighting at the garrison; Tai personally carried their bones back to Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 以從討邢杲功，賜爵廣阿子。

translations.literal: For following the campaign against Xing Gao, he was granted the title Baron of Guanga.
translations.idiomatic: For following the campaign against Xing Gao, he was granted the title Baron of Guanga.

sentences.zh: 神武之為晉州，請泰為鎮城都督，參謀軍事。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan was prefect of Jinzhou, he requested Tai as commandant of the fortified city and staff adviser on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan was prefect of Jinzhou, he requested Tai as commandant of the fortified city and staff adviser on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍中、京畿大都督，尋領御史中尉。

translations.literal: He rose through appointments as Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant of the Capital Region, and soon also served as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through appointments as Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant of the Capital Region, and soon also served as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 泰以勳戚居台，雖無多糾舉，而百僚畏懼。

translations.literal: As a meritorious relative holding the censorate, though Tai did not lodge many accusations, all officials feared him.
translations.idiomatic: As a meritorious kinsman holding the censorate, though Tai did not lodge many accusations, all officials feared him.

sentences.zh: 天平三年，神武西討，令泰自潼關入。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianping, Gao Huan marched west on campaign and ordered Tai to enter through Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianping, Gao Huan marched west on campaign and ordered Tai to enter through Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 四年，泰至小關，為周文帝所襲，眾盡沒，泰自殺。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when Tai reached Xiaoguan, he was attacked by Emperor Wen of Zhou; his entire force was destroyed, and Tai killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when Tai reached Xiaoguan, he was attacked by Emperor Wen of Zhou; his entire force was destroyed, and Tai killed himself.

sentences.zh: 初，泰將發鄴，鄴有惠化尼，謠云：「竇行台，去不回。」

translations.literal: At first, when Tai was about to set out from Ye, a nun of Huihua in Ye had a song that ran: "Commissioner Dou goes forth and does not return.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Tai was about to set out from Ye, a nun of Huihua in Ye had a song that ran, "Commissioner Dou goes forth and does not return.

sentences.zh: 未行之前夜，三更，忽有硃衣冠幘數千人入台，雲收竇中尉。

translations.literal: On the night before he departed, at the third watch, several thousand men in vermilion robes and caps suddenly entered the censorate, saying they had come to take Censor-in-Chief Dou.
translations.idiomatic: On the night before he departed, at the third watch, several thousand men in vermilion robes and caps suddenly entered the censorate, saying they had come to take Censor-in-Chief Dou.

sentences.zh: 宿直兵吏皆驚。

translations.literal: The officers on night duty were all alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: The officers on night duty were all alarmed.

sentences.zh: 其人入數屋。

translations.literal: The men entered several rooms.
translations.idiomatic: The men entered several rooms.

sentences.zh: 俄頃而去。

translations.literal: After a moment they departed.
translations.idiomatic: After a moment they departed.

sentences.zh: 旦視關鍵不異，方知非人，皆知其必敗。

translations.literal: At dawn the locks and bolts were unchanged, and only then did they know the visitors were not human; all understood that Tai was doomed to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the locks and bolts were unchanged, and only then did they know the visitors were not human; all understood that Tai was doomed to defeat.

sentences.zh: 贈大司馬、太尉、錄尚書事，諡曰武貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Marshal, Grand Tutor, and Manager of Affairs for the Masters of Writing, with the posthumous title Wuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Grand Marshal, Grand Tutor, and Manager of Affairs for the Masters of Writing, with the posthumous title Wuzhen.

sentences.zh: 泰妻，武明婁後妹也。

translations.literal: Tai's wife was a younger sister of Empress Wuming of the Lou clan.
translations.idiomatic: Tai's wife was a younger sister of Empress Wuming of the Lou clan.

sentences.zh: 泰雖以親見待，而功名自建。

translations.literal: Though Tai was treated with favor as a kinsman, his fame and achievements were of his own making.
translations.idiomatic: Though Tai was treated with favor as a kinsman, his fame and achievements were of his own making.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，祭告其墓。

translations.literal: When Northern Qi received the abdication, [the court] offered sacrifice and announcement at his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi received the abdication, the court offered sacrifice and announcement at his tomb.

sentences.zh: 皇建初，配享神武廟庭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangjian he was given shared sacrifice in Gao Huan's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Huangjian he was given shared sacrifice in Gao Huan's temple court.

sentences.zh: 子孝敬嗣，位儀同三司。

translations.literal: His son Xiaojing succeeded him and held the rank Bearer of the Three Special Equipments.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaojing succeeded him and held the rank Bearer of the Three Special Equipments.

sentences.zh: 尉景，字士真，善無人也。

translations.literal: Wei Jing, styled Shizhen, was a native of Shanwu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jing, styled Shizhen, was a native of Shanwu.

sentences.zh: 泰、漢置尉堠官，其先有居此職者，因以氏焉。

translations.literal: Qin and Han established the post of frontier-signal officer; an ancestor had held that office, and the clan took it as their surname.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Han established the post of frontier-signal officer; an ancestor had held that office, and the clan took it as their surname.

sentences.zh: 景性溫厚，頗有俠氣。

translations.literal: Jing's nature was mild and generous, with something of the chivalrous spirit about him.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's nature was mild and generous, with something of the chivalrous spirit about him.

sentences.zh: 魏孝昌中，北鎮反，景與神武入杜洛周中，仍共歸爾硃榮。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era of Wei, when the northern garrisons rebelled, Jing and Gao Huan entered Du Luozhou's ranks, then together returned to Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiaochang era of Wei, when the northern garrisons rebelled, Jing and Gao Huan entered Du Luozhou's ranks, then together returned to Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 以軍功，封博野縣伯。

translations.literal: For military merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Boye County.
translations.idiomatic: For military merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Boye County.

sentences.zh: 後從神武起兵信都。

translations.literal: Later he followed Gao Huan in raising troops at Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Gao Huan in raising troops at Xindu.

sentences.zh: 韓陵之戰，唯景所統失利。

translations.literal: At the battle of Hanling, only the force under Jing's command suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Hanling, only the force under Jing's command suffered defeat.

sentences.zh: 神武入洛，留景鎮鄴。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan entered Luoyang, he left Jing to garrison Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan entered Luoyang, he left Jing to garrison Ye.

sentences.zh: 尋進封為公。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to enfeoffment as duke.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was advanced to enfeoffment as duke.

sentences.zh: 景妻常山君，神武之姊也。

translations.literal: Jing's wife was the Lady of Changshan, elder sister of Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's wife was the Lady of Changshan, elder sister of Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 以勳戚，每有軍事，與厙狄幹常被委重。

translations.literal: As a meritorious kinsman, whenever there was military business he and Kudigan were regularly entrusted with weighty duties.
translations.idiomatic: As a meritorious kinsman, whenever there was military business he and Kudigan were regularly entrusted with weighty duties.

sentences.zh: 而不能忘懷財利，神武每嫌責之。

translations.literal: Yet he could not put wealth from his mind, and Gao Huan often reproached him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he could not put wealth from his mind, and Gao Huan often reproached him for it.

sentences.zh: 轉冀州刺史，又大納賄，發夫獵，死者三百人。

translations.literal: When transferred to Governor of Jizhou, he again accepted bribes on a large scale; he conscripted laborers for a hunt, and three hundred men died.
translations.idiomatic: When transferred to Governor of Jizhou, he again accepted bribes on a large scale; he conscripted laborers for a hunt, and three hundred men died.

sentences.zh: 厙狄幹與景在神武坐，請作御史中尉。

translations.literal: Kudigan and Jing were in Gao Huan's presence when Kudigan asked to be made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Kudigan and Jing were in Gao Huan's presence when Kudigan asked to be made Censor-in-Chief.
