sentences.zh: 神武曰：「何意下求卑官？」

translations.literal: Gao Huan said: "Why do you seek so low an office?
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "Why do you seek so low an office?

sentences.zh: 幹曰：「欲捉尉景。」

translations.literal: Kudigan said: "I want to catch Wei Jing."
translations.idiomatic: Kudigan said, "I want to catch Wei Jing."

sentences.zh: 神武大笑，令優者石董桶戲之。

translations.literal: Gao Huan laughed loudly and had the actor Shi Dongtong mock him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan laughed loudly and had the actor Shi Dongtong mock him.

sentences.zh: 董桶剝景衣曰：「公剝百姓，董桶何為不剝公？」

translations.literal: Dongtong stripped Jing of his clothes and said: "My lord strips the common people—why should Dongtong not strip my lord?
translations.idiomatic: Dongtong stripped Jing of his clothes and said, "My lord strips the common people—why should Dongtong not strip my lord?

sentences.zh: 神武誡景曰：「可以無貪也。」

translations.literal: Gao Huan admonished Jing: "You really ought to stop being greedy."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan admonished Jing, "You really ought to stop being greedy."

sentences.zh: 景曰：「與爾計生活孰多，我止人上取，爾割天子調。」

translations.literal: Jing said: "Let us reckon whose livelihood is greater—I take only from men above me, while you skim off the Son of Heaven's taxes."
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "Let us reckon whose livelihood is greater—I take only from men above me, while you skim off the Son of Heaven's taxes."

sentences.zh: 神武笑不答。

translations.literal: Gao Huan laughed and made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan laughed and made no reply.

sentences.zh: 改封長樂郡公，歷位太保、太傅。

translations.literal: His fief was changed to Duke of Changle Commandery; he rose through the posts of Grand Mentor and Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was changed to Duke of Changle Commandery; he rose through the posts of Grand Mentor and Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 坐匿亡人，見禁止。

translations.literal: For harboring fugitives he was placed under detention.
translations.idiomatic: For harboring fugitives he was placed under detention.

sentences.zh: 使崔暹謂文襄曰：「語阿惠，兒富貴，欲殺我邪？」

translations.literal: He had Cui Xian tell Wenxiang: "Tell Ah Hui—now that the boy is rich and noble, does he mean to kill me?
translations.idiomatic: He had Cui Xian tell Gao Cheng, "Tell Ah Hui—now that the boy is rich and noble, does he mean to kill me?

sentences.zh: 神武聞之泣，詣闕曰：「臣非尉景無以至今日。」

translations.literal: When Gao Huan heard this he wept and went to the palace, saying: "Your servant would never have reached this day without Wei Jing."
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan heard this he wept and went to the palace, saying, "Your servant would never have reached this day without Wei Jing."

sentences.zh: 三請，帝乃許之。

translations.literal: After three petitions the emperor granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: After three petitions the emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 於是黜為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jing was demoted to General of Agile Cavalry and Bearer of the Three Special Equipments with Bespoke Staff.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Jing was demoted to General of Agile Cavalry and Bearer of the Three Special Equipments with Bespoke Staff.

sentences.zh: 神武造景，景恚，臥不動，叫曰：「殺我時趣邪？」

translations.literal: Gao Huan visited Jing; Jing, furious, lay motionless and shouted: "If you're going to kill me, why not hurry up?
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan visited Jing; Jing, furious, lay motionless and shouted, "If you're going to kill me, why not hurry up?

sentences.zh: 常山君謂神武曰：「老人去死近，何忍煎迫至此！」

translations.literal: The Lady of Changshan told Gao Huan: "The old man is close to death—how can you bear to torment him so!"
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Changshan told Gao Huan, "The old man is close to death—how can you bear to torment him so!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「我為爾汲水，胝生。」

translations.literal: She also said: "I drew water for you till calluses formed."
translations.idiomatic: She also said, "I drew water for you till calluses formed."

sentences.zh: 因出其掌。

translations.literal: And she held out her palm.
translations.idiomatic: And she held out her palm.

sentences.zh: 神武撫景，為之屈膝。

translations.literal: Gao Huan comforted Jing and dropped to his knees for him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan comforted Jing and dropped to his knees for him.

sentences.zh: 先是，景有果下馬，文襄求之，景不與，曰：「土相扶為牆，人相扶為王。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jing had a pony under five feet; Wenxiang asked for it, but Jing would not give it up and said: "Earth piled together makes a wall; men who support one another make a king.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jing had a pony under five feet; Gao Cheng asked for it, but Jing would not give it up and said, "Earth piled together makes a wall; men who support one another make a king.

sentences.zh: 一馬亦不得畜而索也？」

translations.literal: Not even one horse may be kept without being demanded?
translations.idiomatic: Must I not even be allowed to keep a single horse without you seizing it?

sentences.zh: 神武對景及常山君責文襄而杖之。

translations.literal: Gao Huan, facing Jing and the Prince of Changshan, reproved Gao Cheng and beat him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan, in the presence of Wei Jing and the Prince of Changshan, rebuked Gao Cheng and had him beaten.

sentences.zh: 常山君泣救之，景曰：「小兒慣去，放使作心腹，何須幹啼濕哭，不聽打邪？」

translations.literal: The Prince of Changshan wept and pleaded for him. Jing said: 'The boy has grown spoiled; I let him serve as a trusted confidant—why dry crying and wet crying? Won't you allow a beating?
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Changshan wept and interceded for him. Wei Jing said, 'The boy has grown spoiled; I allowed him to serve as my trusted confidant—why these loud tears and sobbing? Can I not even discipline him?

sentences.zh: 尋授青州刺史，操行頗改，百姓安之。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Qingzhou governor; his conduct greatly improved, and the people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed governor of Qing Province; his conduct improved markedly, and the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 征授大司馬，遇疾，薨於州。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Grand Marshal; he fell ill and died in the province.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Grand Marshal, but fell ill and died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈太師、尚書令。

translations.literal: Posthumously conferred Grand Preceptor and Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，以景元勳，詔祭告其墓。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, because of Jing's founding merit, an edict ordered sacrifice and announcement at his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the mandate, Wei Jing's founding merit was honored with an edict ordering sacrifice and announcement at his tomb.

sentences.zh: 皇建初，配享神武廟庭，追封長樂王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangjian, he was granted a place in the sacrifices at Gao Huan's temple court and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Huangjian era, he was granted a place in the offerings at Gao Huan's temple and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Changle.

sentences.zh: 子粲，少曆顯職，性粗武。

translations.literal: His son Can, in youth, held distinguished posts; his nature was coarse and martial.
translations.idiomatic: His son Can held distinguished posts from youth; he was rough and martial by nature.

sentences.zh: 天保初，封厙狄幹等為王，粲以父不預王爵，大恚恨，十餘日閉門不朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, Kudigan and others were enfeoffed as princes. Can, because his father was not included among the princely titles, was greatly resentful and for more than ten days closed his doors and did not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianbao era, Kudigan and others were enfeoffed as princes. Can, furious that his father had been passed over, shut himself in for more than ten days and refused to attend court.

sentences.zh: 帝怪，遣使就宅問之。

translations.literal: The Emperor wondered at this and sent an envoy to his residence to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was puzzled and sent an envoy to Can's residence to ask what was wrong.

sentences.zh: 隔門謂使人曰：「天子不封粲父作王，粲不如死。」

translations.literal: Through the door he told the envoy: 'If the Son of Heaven will not enfeoff Can's father as a prince, Can would rather die.
translations.idiomatic: Through the closed door he told the envoy, 'If the Son of Heaven will not make my father a prince, I would rather die.

sentences.zh: 使云：「須開門受敕。」

translations.literal: The envoy said: 'You must open the door to receive the edict.'
translations.idiomatic: The envoy replied, 'You must open the door to receive the imperial edict.'

sentences.zh: 粲遂彎弓隔門射。

translations.literal: Can then bent his bow and shot through the door.
translations.idiomatic: Can then strung his bow and shot at the envoy through the door.

sentences.zh: 使者以狀聞之，文宣使段韶諭旨。

translations.literal: The envoy reported the matter; Gao Yang had Duan Shao convey the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy reported what had happened, and Gao Yang sent Duan Shao to explain the emperor's wishes.

sentences.zh: 粲見韶，唯撫膺大哭，不答一言。

translations.literal: When Can saw Shao, he only beat his chest and wept bitterly, answering not a single word.
translations.idiomatic: When Can met Duan Shao, he could only beat his breast and weep; he did not utter a single word.

sentences.zh: 文宣親詣其宅慰之，方復朝請。

translations.literal: Gao Yang personally went to his residence to comfort him, and only then did he resume court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang went in person to Can's home to console him, and only then did Can return to court.

sentences.zh: 尋追封景長樂王，粲襲爵。

translations.literal: Soon Wei Jing was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Changle, and Can inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jing was soon posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Changle, and Can inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 位司徒、太傅，薨。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Minister over the Masses and Grand Tutor, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister over the Masses and Grand Tutor, then died.

sentences.zh: 子世辨嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shibian succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shibian succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 周師將入鄴，令世辨率千餘騎覘候。

translations.literal: When the Zhou armies were about to enter Ye, Shibian was ordered to lead more than a thousand cavalry to reconnoiter.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou forces were about to enter Ye, Shibian was ordered to lead more than a thousand horsemen on reconnaissance.

sentences.zh: 出滏口，登高阜西望，遙見群鳥飛起，謂是西軍旗幟，即馳還。

translations.literal: He went out through Fokou, climbed a high mound, and looked west; seeing a flock of birds rise in the distance, he took them for the banners of the Western army and immediately galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: He passed through Fokou, climbed a high hill, and looked west; when he saw birds rise in the distance, he took them for Western army banners and galloped back at once.

sentences.zh: 比至紫陌橋，不敢顧。

translations.literal: By the time he reached Zimo Bridge, he dared not look back.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Zimo Bridge, he did not dare look back.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，卒于浙州刺史。

translations.literal: During the Kaihuang era of Sui, he died while serving as governor of Zhe Province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang era of Sui, he died in office as governor of Zhe Province.

sentences.zh: 婁昭，字菩薩，代郡平城人也，武明皇后之母弟也。

translations.literal: Lou Zhao, style Pusa, was a native of Pingcheng in Dai Commandery and the younger maternal brother of Empress Wuming.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Zhao, styled Pusa, was a native of Pingcheng in Dai Commandery and the Empress Wuming's younger brother on their mother's side.

sentences.zh: 祖父提，雄傑有識度，家僮千數，牛馬以穀量。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ti was heroic and far-sighted; his household had thousands of servants, and his cattle and horses were counted by the grain-bin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ti was a man of heroic stature and keen judgment; he kept thousands of household servants, and measured his cattle and horses by the bin.

sentences.zh: 性好周給，士多歸附之。

translations.literal: He was by nature generous in giving, and many gentlemen attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Generous by nature, he drew many gentlemen to his service.

sentences.zh: 魏太武時，以功封真定侯。

translations.literal: During the reign of Wei Emperor Taiwu, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhending for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei Emperor Taiwu, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhending for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 父內幹，有武力，未仕而卒。

translations.literal: His father Neigan had martial strength but died before taking office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Neigan was a man of martial prowess but died before ever holding office.

sentences.zh: 昭貴，魏朝贈司徒。

translations.literal: Zhao was honored; the Wei court posthumously made him Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Zhao rose to high honor; the Wei court posthumously made his father Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，追封太原王。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the mandate, Lou Zhao was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 昭方雅正直，有大度深謀，腰帶八尺，弓馬冠時。

translations.literal: Zhao was upright and elegant, with great breadth and deep strategy; his girdle was eight feet long, and in archery and horsemanship he stood foremost of his age.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Zhao was upright and refined, broad-minded and deeply strategic; eight feet around the waist, he stood unmatched in archery and horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 神武少親重之，昭亦早識人雄，曲盡禮敬。

translations.literal: Gao Huan from youth treated him with close esteem, and Zhao also early recognized a hero among men, showing him the fullest courtesy and respect.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Gao Huan held him in close esteem, and Lou Zhao early recognized greatness in him and showed him every courtesy.

sentences.zh: 數隨神武獵，每致請，不宜乘危歷險。

translations.literal: He often followed Gao Huan on hunts and each time petitioned that it was not fitting to ride through peril and danger.
translations.idiomatic: He often accompanied Gao Huan on the hunt and each time urged that it was unwise to court peril on steep and dangerous ground.

sentences.zh: 神武將出信都，昭贊成大策，即以為中軍大都督。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan was about to leave Xindu, Zhao approved the great plan and was immediately made Grand Commander of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan prepared to march from Xindu, Lou Zhao endorsed the grand design and was at once made Grand Commander of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 從破爾硃兆于廣阿，封安喜縣伯，改濟北公，又徙濮陽郡公，授領軍將軍。

translations.literal: He followed in the defeat of Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a, was enfeoffed Baron of Anxi County, then made Duke of Jibei, then transferred to Duke of Puyang Commandery, and appointed General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the defeat of Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a, was enfeoffed Baron of Anxi, then Duke of Jibei, then Duke of Puyang, and appointed General of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武將貳于神武，昭以疾辭還晉陽。

translations.literal: When Wei Emperor Xiaowu was about to turn against Gao Huan, Zhao pleaded illness and returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei was about to break with Gao Huan, Lou Zhao pleaded illness and withdrew to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 後從神武入洛。

translations.literal: Later he followed Gao Huan into Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Gao Huan into Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史樊子鵠反，以昭為東道大都督討之。

translations.literal: When Yanzhou governor Fan Zihu rebelled, Zhao was made Grand Commander of the Eastern Route to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Zihu, governor of Yan Province, rebelled, Lou Zhao was made Grand Commander of the Eastern Route to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 子鵠既死，諸將勸昭盡捕誅其黨。

translations.literal: After Zihu died, the generals urged Zhao to capture and execute all his partisans.
translations.idiomatic: After Fan Zihu's death, the generals urged Lou Zhao to capture and execute all his followers.

sentences.zh: 昭曰：「此州無狀，橫被殘賊，其賊是怨，其人何罪？」

translations.literal: Zhao said: 'This province is worthless and has wantonly suffered bandits—the bandits are to be hated, but what crime have the people committed?
translations.idiomatic: Lou Zhao said, 'This province has been wretchedly overrun by bandits—the bandits deserve hatred, but what crime have the people committed?

sentences.zh: 遂皆舍焉。

translations.literal: Then he released them all.
translations.idiomatic: He released them all.

sentences.zh: 後轉大司馬，仍領軍。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Grand Marshal while still commanding the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Grand Marshal while retaining command of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒，出為定州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister over the Masses and sent out as governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Minister over the Masses, he was sent out as governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 昭好酒，晚得偏風，雖愈，猶不能處劇務。

translations.literal: Zhao loved wine; in later years he suffered hemiplegia, and though he recovered, he still could not handle heavy duties.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Zhao loved wine; in his later years he suffered a stroke, and though he recovered, he could no longer manage heavy affairs.

sentences.zh: 在州，事委僚屬，昭舉其大綱而已。

translations.literal: In the province he delegated affairs to his subordinates; Zhao handled only the broad outlines.
translations.idiomatic: In the province he entrusted affairs to his staff and attended only to the larger design.

sentences.zh: 薨于州，贈假黃鉞、太師、太尉，諡曰武。

translations.literal: He died in the province and was posthumously conferred the golden axe, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Commandant, with the posthumous name Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously granted the golden axe, the titles of Grand Preceptor and Grand Commandant, and the posthumous name Wu.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，詔祭告其墓，封太原王。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, an edict ordered sacrifice at his tomb and enfeoffed him as Prince of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the mandate, an edict ordered sacrifice at his tomb and enfeoffed him as Prince of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 皇建初，配享神武廟庭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangjian, he was granted a place in the sacrifices at Gao Huan's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Huangjian era, he was granted a place in the offerings at Gao Huan's temple.

sentences.zh: 長子仲達嗣，改封濮陽王。

translations.literal: His eldest son Zhongda succeeded him; the title was changed to Prince of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Zhongda succeeded him, and the title was changed to Prince of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 次子定遠，少曆顯職。

translations.literal: His second son Dingyuan, in youth, held distinguished posts.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Dingyuan held distinguished posts from youth.

sentences.zh: 外戚中，偏為武成愛狎，別封臨淮郡王。

translations.literal: Among the maternal relatives, he was especially favored and doted on by Wucheng and was separately enfeoffed as Prince of Linhuai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Among the empress's kin he was especially favored by Emperor Wucheng and was separately enfeoffed as Prince of Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 武成大漸，與趙郡王等同受顧命，位司空。

translations.literal: When Wucheng grew critically ill, Dingyuan, together with the Prince of Zhao Commandery and others, received the final imperial charge and held the post of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Wucheng fell gravely ill, Dingyuan received the deathbed charge together with the Prince of Zhao and others, and held the post of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 趙郡王之奏黜和士開，定遠與其謀。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Zhao Commandery memorialized to dismiss He Shikai, Dingyuan joined in the plot.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Zhao memorialized to remove He Shikai from office, Dingyuan joined the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 遂納士開賄賂，成趙郡之禍，其貪鄙如此。

translations.literal: He then accepted Shikai's bribes and brought calamity upon the Prince of Zhao—such was his greed and baseness.
translations.idiomatic: He then accepted bribes from He Shikai and brought ruin upon the Prince of Zhao—such was his greed and baseness.

sentences.zh: 尋除瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 初，定遠弟季略，穆提婆求其伎妾，定遠不許。

translations.literal: Earlier, Dingyuan's younger brother Jilue had a courtesan whom Mutipo sought; Dingyuan refused.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Dingyuan's younger brother Jilue had a courtesan whom Mutipo demanded; Dingyuan refused.

sentences.zh: 因高思好作亂，提婆令臨淮國郎中金造遠陰與思好通。

translations.literal: When Gao Sihao raised rebellion, Mutipo had Jinzao, director of the Linhuai principality, secretly communicate with Sihao.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Sihao rebelled, Mutipo had Jinzao, director of the Linhuai principality, secretly communicate with him.

sentences.zh: 後主令開府段暢率三千騎掩之，令侍御史趙秀通至州，以贓貨事劾定遠。

translations.literal: The Later Lord ordered Duan Chang, honorary cabinet minister, to lead three thousand cavalry in a surprise attack, and ordered Supervising Censor Zhao Xiu to arrive at the province and impeach Dingyuan on charges of corruption.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord ordered Duan Chang, honorary cabinet minister, to lead three thousand horsemen in a surprise raid, and sent Supervising Censor Zhao Xiu to the province to impeach Dingyuan for corruption.

sentences.zh: 定遠疑有變，遂縊而死。

translations.literal: Dingyuan suspected treachery and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a trap, Dingyuan hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 子子產嗣，位開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: His son Zichan succeeded him and held the rank of Honorary Grand General of Agile Cavalry with status equal to the Three Preceptors.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zichan succeeded him and held the rank of Honorary Grand General of Agile Cavalry, equal in status to the Three Preceptors.

sentences.zh: 厙狄幹，善無人也。

translations.literal: Kudigan was a man of Shanwu.
translations.idiomatic: Kudigan was a man of Shanwu.

sentences.zh: 曾祖越豆眷，魏道武時，以功割善無之西臘汗山地方百里以處之。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yuedoujuan, in the time of Wei Emperor Daowu, for merit had a hundred li of territory at Xilahanshan west of Shanwu cut off to settle them there.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yuedoujuan, under Wei Emperor Daowu, was granted a hundred li of land at Xilahanshan west of Shanwu for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 後率部落北遷，因家朔方。

translations.literal: Later he led the tribe north in migration and established his household in Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: He later led his tribe northward and made his home in Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 幹鯁直少言，有武藝。

translations.literal: Gan was blunt and upright, spoke little, and had martial skill.
translations.idiomatic: Kudigan was blunt and upright, sparing of speech, and skilled in arms.

sentences.zh: 魏正光初，除掃逆党，授將軍，宿衛於內。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wei Zhengguang, he was appointed to purge rebellious factions, granted the rank of general, and served as an inner palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhengguang era, he was appointed to purge rebel factions, made a general, and served in the inner palace guard.

sentences.zh: 以家在寒鄉，不宜毒暑，冬得入京師，夏歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Because his family lived in a cold region and could not endure intense heat, in winter he was allowed to enter the capital and in summer he returned to his homeland.
translations.idiomatic: Because his homeland lay in a cold country ill suited to fierce summer heat, he was permitted to enter the capital in winter and return home in summer.

sentences.zh: 孝昌元年，北邊擾亂，奔雲中，為刺史費穆送于爾硃榮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaochang, when the northern frontier was in turmoil, he fled to Yunzhong and was sent by governor Fei Mu to Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiaochang, when the northern frontier fell into chaos, he fled to Yunzhong and was sent by Governor Fei Mu to Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 以軍主隨榮入洛。

translations.literal: As an army commander he followed Rong into Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: As an army commander he followed Erzhu Rong into Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 後從神武起兵，破四胡于韓陵，封廣平縣公，尋進郡公。

translations.literal: Later he followed Gao Huan in raising troops, defeated the Four Hu at Hanling, was enfeoffed Duke of Guangping County, and soon advanced to commandery duke.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Gao Huan in raising arms, helped defeat the Four Hu at Hanling, was enfeoffed Duke of Guangping, and soon raised to commandery duke.

sentences.zh: 河陰之役，諸將大捷，唯幹兵退。

translations.literal: At the Battle of Heyin the generals won a great victory, but only Gan's troops retreated.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Heyin the other generals won a great victory, but Kudigan's troops alone fell back.

sentences.zh: 神武以其舊功，竟不責黜。

translations.literal: Gao Huan, because of his old merit, ultimately did not blame or dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan, honoring his long service, did not blame or punish him.

sentences.zh: 尋轉太保、太傅。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Grand Guardian and Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Grand Guardian and Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 及高仲密以武牢叛，神武討之，以幹為大都督，前驅。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhongmi rebelled with Wulao fortress, Gao Huan marched against him and made Gan Grand Commander as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi rebelled from Wulao fortress, Gao Huan marched against him and made Kudigan Grand Commander in the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 幹上道不過家，見侯景，不遑食，景使騎追饋之。

translations.literal: Gan, on the march, did not pass by home; he saw Hou Jing but had no time to eat, and Jing sent riders in pursuit to provision him.
translations.idiomatic: Kudigan, marching out, did not stop at home; he met Hou Jing but had no time to eat, and Hou Jing sent horsemen after him with provisions.

sentences.zh: 時周文自將兵至洛陽，軍容甚盛。

translations.literal: At the time Yuwen Tai personally led troops to Luoyang, and his military array was very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuwen Tai personally led an army to Luoyang, and his forces were arrayed in great strength.

sentences.zh: 諸將未欲南度，幹決計濟河，神武大兵繼至，遂大破之。

translations.literal: The generals did not wish to cross south; Gan resolved to cross the river, Gao Huan's main force followed, and they utterly defeated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The other generals hesitated to cross south of the river, but Kudigan resolved to ford it; Gao Huan's main army followed, and they won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 還為定州刺史。

translations.literal: He returned and became governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He returned and was made governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 不閑吏事，事多煩擾，然清約自居，不為吏人所患。

translations.literal: Unskilled in administrative affairs, affairs were often tangled, yet he kept himself frugal and was not troubled by clerks and officials.
translations.idiomatic: He was unversed in civil administration and affairs often grew tangled, yet he lived plainly and was not harassed by clerks and underlings.

sentences.zh: 遷太師。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 天平初，以幹元勳佐命，封章武郡王，轉太宰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, because of Gan's founding merit and support of the mandate, he was enfeoffed Prince of Zhangwu Commandery and transferred to Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianping era, for his founding merit and support of the new mandate, Kudigan was enfeoffed Prince of Zhangwu and made Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 幹尚神武妹樂陵長公主，以親地見待。

translations.literal: Gan married Gao Huan's sister, the Princess of Leling, and because of this kinship was treated with honor.
translations.idiomatic: Kudigan married Gao Huan's sister, the Princess of Leling, and by virtue of this tie was treated with special honor.

sentences.zh: 自預勤王，常總大眾，威望之重，為諸將所伏。

translations.literal: From the time he joined in the rescue of the throne, he often commanded the main force; the weight of his prestige made the generals submit to him.
translations.idiomatic: From his service in the rescue of the throne he often commanded the main army, and the generals bowed to the weight of his prestige.

sentences.zh: 而最為嚴猛。

translations.literal: Yet he was the sternest and fiercest of all.
translations.idiomatic: Yet among them all he was the sternest and most formidable.

sentences.zh: 曾詣京師，魏譙王元孝友于公門言戲過常，無能面折者，幹正色責之，孝友大慚，時人稱善。

translations.literal: Once when he went to the capital, Wei Prince of Qiao Yuan Xiaoyou jesting at the gate exceeded the norm; none could rebuke him to his face, but Gan with stern countenance reproved him. Xiaoyou was greatly ashamed, and men of the time praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Once at the capital, Yuan Xiaoyou, Prince of Qiao, carried his jesting at the gate beyond all bounds, and none dared rebuke him to his face—until Kudigan sternly reproved him. Xiaoyou was deeply shamed, and men of the time praised Kudigan for it.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈假黃鉞、太宰，給轀輬車，諡曰景烈。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously conferred the golden axe and Grand Tutor, given the imperial hearse, and granted the posthumous name Jinglie.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the golden axe and the title of Grand Tutor, given the imperial hearse, and honored with the posthumous name Jinglie.

sentences.zh: 幹不知書，署名為幹字，逆上畫之，時人謂之穿錘。

translations.literal: Gan did not know writing; when signing his name he wrote the character gan, drawing the stroke upward in reverse, and men of the time called this 'piercing awl.'
translations.idiomatic: Kudigan could not read; when he signed his name he wrote the character for Gan with the final stroke drawn upward in reverse, and people called it 'the piercing awl.'

sentences.zh: 又有武將王周者，署名先為吉，而後成其外。

translations.literal: There was also the martial officer Wang Zhou, who when signing first wrote ji and then completed the outer form.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the warrior Wang Zhou, who when signing his name first wrote the character for 'lucky' and then completed the rest.

sentences.zh: 二人至孫，始並知書。

translations.literal: In both families it was not until the grandsons' generation that they came to know writing.
translations.idiomatic: In both families literacy did not come until the grandsons' generation.

sentences.zh: 幹，皇建初配享神武廟庭。

translations.literal: Gan, at the beginning of Huangjian, was granted a place in the sacrifices at Gao Huan's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: Kudigan, at the beginning of the Huangjian era, was granted a place in the offerings at Gao Huan's temple.

sentences.zh: 子伏敬，位儀同三司卒，子士文嗣。

translations.literal: His son Fujing died while holding rank equal to the Three Preceptors; his son Shiwen succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fujing died while holding rank equal to the Three Preceptors; Fujing's son Shiwen succeeded.

sentences.zh: 士文性孤直，雖鄰里至親，莫與通狎。

translations.literal: Shiwen's nature was solitary and upright; even with the closest neighbors and kin, none kept familiar intimacy with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shiwen was solitary and upright by nature; even neighbors and close kin kept no familiar intimacy with him.

sentences.zh: 在齊，襲封章武郡王，位領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Under Qi he inherited the title Prince of Zhangwu Commandery and held the post of General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Northern Qi he inherited the title Prince of Zhangwu and served as General of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 周武帝平齊，山東衣冠多來迎，唯士文閉門自守。

translations.literal: When Zhou Emperor Wu conquered Qi, the gentry of Shandong mostly came out to welcome him, but Shiwen alone closed his doors and held himself aloof.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, the gentry of Shandong mostly came out to welcome the conquerors—Shiwen alone shut his doors and held himself apart.

sentences.zh: 帝奇之，授開府儀同三司、隨州刺史。

translations.literal: The Emperor admired this and appointed him Honorary Grand General of Agile Cavalry with status equal to the Three Preceptors and governor of Sui Province.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired this and appointed him Honorary Grand General of Agile Cavalry, equal in rank to the Three Preceptors, and governor of Sui Province.

sentences.zh: 隋文受禪，加上開府，封湖陂縣子，尋拜貝州刺史。

translations.literal: When Sui Emperor Wen received the abdication, he added honorary grand general status, enfeoffed him as Viscount of Hubei County, and soon appointed him governor of Bei Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the mandate, he added further honorary rank, enfeoffed Shiwen as Viscount of Hubei, and soon made him governor of Bei Province.

sentences.zh: 性清苦，不受公料，家無餘財。

translations.literal: His nature was austere and hardship-loving; he accepted no official stipend, and his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in austere simplicity, took no official stipend, and kept no surplus wealth in his house.

sentences.zh: 其子嘗啖官廚餅，士文枷之於獄累日，杖之二百，步送還京。

translations.literal: His son once ate cakes from the official kitchen; Shiwen put him in the cangue and prison for many days, beat him two hundred strokes, and sent him back to the capital on foot.
translations.idiomatic: When his son once ate cakes from the official kitchen, Shiwen clapped him in the cangue for days, beat him two hundred strokes, and sent him on foot back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 僮隸無敢出門。

translations.literal: Servants and retainers dared not go out the door.
translations.idiomatic: His servants and retainers did not dare step outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 所買鹽菜，必於外境。

translations.literal: Whatever salt and vegetables he bought had to be from outside his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever salt and vegetables he purchased had to be bought beyond the borders of his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 凡有出入，皆封署其門，親故絕跡，慶吊不通。

translations.literal: Whenever anyone went in or out, the doors were all sealed and stamped; relatives and friends vanished without trace; congratulations and condolences did not pass through.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone entering or leaving had the door sealed and signed; kin and old friends ceased to visit; neither celebrations nor mourning calls were exchanged.

sentences.zh: 法令嚴肅，吏人股戰，道不拾遺。

translations.literal: The laws were strict and solemn; officials and clerks trembled in their thighs; no one picked up lost items on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The laws were stern and unyielding; officials and clerks shook with fear; lost goods lay untouched in the streets.

sentences.zh: 有細過，必深文陷害。

translations.literal: For minor faults, he inevitably twisted the law to entrap and frame people.
translations.idiomatic: Even for trifling offenses, he invariably twisted the statutes to ensnare and ruin people.

sentences.zh: 嘗入朝，遇上賜公卿入左藏，任取多少。

translations.literal: Once on a court visit, he happened upon the emperor granting ministers and nobles entry to the Left Treasury, allowing them to take as much as they wished.
translations.idiomatic: On one visit to court he found the emperor admitting the chief ministers into the Left Treasury and letting each take as much as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 人皆極重，士文獨口銜絹一匹，兩手各持一匹。

translations.literal: Everyone took extremely heavy loads; Shiwen alone held one bolt of silk in his mouth, one in each hand.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone else loaded themselves to the utmost; Shiwen alone took one bolt of silk in his mouth and one in each hand.

sentences.zh: 上問其故，士文曰：「臣口手俱足，餘無所須。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason. Shiwen said: "Your subject's mouth and hands are fully provided for; I need nothing else."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked why. Shiwen said, "Your servant's mouth and hands are already full; I want nothing more.

sentences.zh: 上異之，別賞遺之。

translations.literal: The emperor was struck by this and gave him a separate reward and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was astonished and gave him a special reward before sending him on his way.

sentences.zh: 士文至州，發摘奸諂，長吏尺布鬥粟之贓，無所寬貸。

translations.literal: When Shiwen arrived at the province, he exposed and seized the treacherous and sycophantic; for senior officials, embezzlement even of a foot of cloth or a peck of grain — none was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shiwen reached his province, he rooted out flattery and deceit; senior officials guilty of even the smallest theft — a foot of cloth, a peck of grain — received no mercy.

sentences.zh: 得千人，奏之，悉配防嶺南。

translations.literal: Finding a thousand, he memorialized it; all were assigned to garrison duty in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: He uncovered a thousand offenders, reported them to the throne, and had them all sent to garrison Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 親戚相送，哭聲遍於州境。

translations.literal: Relatives saw them off; weeping filled the whole province.
translations.idiomatic: Kinfolk came to see them off, and the sound of weeping spread across the entire province.

sentences.zh: 至嶺南遇瘴厲，死者十八九。

translations.literal: On reaching Lingnan they encountered malarial pestilence; eight or nine in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Lingnan they met malarial plague, and eight or nine out of ten perished.

sentences.zh: 於是父母妻子，唯哭士文。

translations.literal: Thereupon parents, wives, and children wept only against Shiwen.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter parents, wives, and children wept only against Shiwen.

sentences.zh: 士文聞之，令人捕搦，捶楚盈前而哭孝彌甚。

translations.literal: Shiwen heard of it and had people arrested; blows and floggings piled up before them, yet their mourning wails grew only louder.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiwen heard of it, he had them seized; beatings piled up before them, yet their wails of grief only grew louder.

sentences.zh: 司馬京兆韋焜、清河令河東趙達，二人並苛刻，唯長史有惠政。

translations.literal: Master of Records Wei Kun of Jingzhao and Prefect of Qinghe Zhao Da of Hedong — both men were harsh and exacting; only the Chief Administrator had beneficent administration.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Records, Wei Kun of Jingzhao, and the Prefect of Qinghe, Zhao Da of Hedong, were both merciless; only the Chief Administrator governed with kindness.

sentences.zh: 時人語曰：「刺史羅殺政，司馬蝮蛇瞋，長史含笑判，清河生吃人。」

translations.literal: People of the time said: "The prefect's demon-killing governance, the Master of Records like an angry viper, the Chief Administrator judging with a smile, Qinghe Prefecture eating men alive."
translations.idiomatic: People of the time said, "The prefect governs like a demon of slaughter, the Master of Records glares like an enraged viper, the Chief Administrator passes judgment with a smile, and Qinghe Prefecture devours men alive.

sentences.zh: 上聞，歎曰：「士文暴過毒獸！」

translations.literal: The emperor heard and sighed: "Shiwen is violent beyond poisonous beasts!"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this, he sighed, "Shiwen is savage beyond any venomous beast!

sentences.zh: 竟坐免。

translations.literal: In the end he was removed from office on that account.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was dismissed from office on that account.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為雍州長史。

translations.literal: Before long he became Chief Administrator of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Chief Administrator of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 謂人曰：「我向法深，不能窺候貴要，無乃必死此官！」

translations.literal: He told people: "I have long enforced the law severely; I cannot fawn on the great and powerful — will I not surely die in this post!"
translations.idiomatic: He told others, "I have always been harsh in enforcing the law and cannot court the powerful and privileged — surely I am fated to die in this office!

sentences.zh: 及下車，執法嚴正，不避貴戚，賓客莫敢至門，人多怨望。

translations.literal: When he took up the post, he enforced the law with strict rectitude, never avoiding the noble and powerful; guests dared not come to his door; many bore resentment against him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took office, he enforced the law with stern impartiality and never shrank from the great and powerful; guests dared not cross his threshold, and many nursed grievances against him.

sentences.zh: 士文從妹為齊氏嬪，有色，齊滅後，賜薛公長孫覽。

translations.literal: Shiwen's cousin by marriage had been a consort of the Qi house, beautiful; after Qi's fall she was granted to Duke of Xue's grandson Sun Lan.
translations.idiomatic: Shiwen's cousin had been a consort of the Qi royal house and was beautiful; after Qi's fall she was given to Sun Lan, grandson of the Duke of Xue.

sentences.zh: 覽妻鄭氏妒，譖之文獻後，令覽離絕。

translations.literal: Lan's wife Lady Zheng was jealous; she slandered her to Empress Dowager Wenxian, causing Lan to break off relations.
translations.idiomatic: Lan's wife, Lady Zheng, was jealous; she slandered the woman to Empress Dowager Wenxian and had Lan sever all ties with her.

sentences.zh: 士文恥之，不與相見。

translations.literal: Shiwen was shamed by this and refused to meet with her.
translations.idiomatic: Shiwen was shamed by this and refused to see her.

sentences.zh: 後應州刺史唐君明居母憂，娉以為妻。

translations.literal: Later Tang Junming, governor of Yingzhou, was in mourning for his mother; Shiwen married her to him as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Tang Junming, governor of Yingzhou, was in mourning for his mother, Shiwen gave her to him in marriage.

sentences.zh: 由是君明、士文並為御史劾。

translations.literal: On this account Junming and Shiwen were both impeached by the censor.
translations.idiomatic: On this account both Junming and Shiwen were impeached by the censor.

sentences.zh: 士文性剛，在獄數日，憤恚而死。

translations.literal: Shiwen's nature was stubborn; after several days in prison he died of rage and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Shiwen was unyielding by nature; after several days in prison he died of rage and indignation.

sentences.zh: 家無餘財，有三子，朝夕不繼，親賓無贍之者。

translations.literal: The household had no surplus wealth; there were three sons; morning and evening they lacked sustenance; neither kin nor guests had anyone to support them.
translations.idiomatic: The family had no money left; with three sons they could barely eat from one day to the next, and neither relatives nor friends had anyone to support them.

sentences.zh: 韓軌，字伯年，太安狄那人也。

translations.literal: Han Gui, styled Bonian, was a native of Dina in Tai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gui, styled Bonian, came from Dina in Tai'an.

sentences.zh: 少有志操，深沈，喜怒不形於色。

translations.literal: In youth he had resolve and principle; deep and reserved; joy and anger did not show on his face.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had firm resolve and integrity; grave and reserved, he never let joy or anger show on his face.

sentences.zh: 神武鎮晉州，引為鎮城都督。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan held Jinzhou, he brought him in as Fortress Commander of the garrison town.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan governed Jinzhou, he took Gui on as commander of the garrison town.

sentences.zh: 及起兵於信都，軌贊成大策。

translations.literal: When arms were raised at Xindu, Gui helped formulate the grand strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised arms at Xindu, Gui helped shape the grand strategy.

sentences.zh: 從破爾硃兆于廣阿，又從韓陵陣，封平昌縣侯。

translations.literal: He followed in defeating Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a, and again at the battle line at Hanling, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingchang County.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Gao Huan in defeating Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a and again at the battle of Hanling, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingchang County.

sentences.zh: 仍督中軍，從破爾硃兆於赤谼嶺。

translations.literal: He continued to command the center army and followed in defeating Erzhu Zhao at Chihong Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to command the center army and again helped defeat Erzhu Zhao at Chihong Ridge.

sentences.zh: 再遷秦州刺史，甚得邊和。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Governor of Qinzhou, and won great harmony on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to governor of Qinzhou, where he kept the frontier remarkably peaceful.

sentences.zh: 神武巡秦州，欲以軌還，仍賜城人戶別絹布兩疋，州人田昭等七千戶皆辭不受，唯乞留軌。

translations.literal: Gao Huan inspected Qinzhou and wished to recall Gui; he also granted the city households two bolts each of silk and cloth; seven thousand households including Tian Zhao of the province all declined to accept, asking only that Gui be kept.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan toured Qinzhou and planned to recall Gui, he granted every household in the city two bolts of silk and cloth; seven thousand households, including Tian Zhao and others, all refused the gift and asked only that Gui be allowed to remain.

sentences.zh: 神武嘉歎，乃留焉。

translations.literal: Gao Huan was pleased and admiring, and so kept him there.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was delighted and moved, and so kept him in place.

sentences.zh: 頻以軍功，進封安德郡公，遷瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Through repeated military merit he was advanced to Duke of Ande Commandery and transferred to Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Through repeated military achievements he was promoted to Duke of Ande Commandery and transferred to governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 在州聚斂，為御史糾劾，削除官爵。

translations.literal: In the province he amassed wealth; the censor impeached him and stripped his office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: In his province he amassed wealth; the censor impeached him and stripped him of office and rank.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復其安德郡公。

translations.literal: Before long his ducal title of Ande Commandery was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his title as Duke of Ande Commandery was restored.

sentences.zh: 歷位中書令、司徒。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Director of the Secretariat and Minister over the Masses in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Director of the Secretariat and Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，封安德郡王。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Ande Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the imperial abdication, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Ande Commandery.

sentences.zh: 軌妹為神武所納，生上党王渙，復以勳庸，曆登臺鉉，常以謙恭自處，不以富貴驕人。

translations.literal: Gui's younger sister was taken in by Gao Huan and bore Prince Huan of Shangdang; again through merit at founding the state, he rose repeatedly to the highest posts; he always conducted himself with humility and deference, never lording his wealth and rank over others.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's younger sister was taken in by Gao Huan and bore Prince Huan of Shangdang; through repeated merit in founding the state he rose to the highest offices, yet always conducted himself with humility and never flaunted his wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 後拜大司馬，從文宣征蠕蠕，在軍暴疾，薨。

translations.literal: Later appointed Grand Marshal; he followed Emperor Wenxuan on campaign against the Rouran; in the army he suddenly fell gravely ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later appointed Grand Marshal, he followed Emperor Wenxuan on campaign against the Rouran; in camp he was suddenly stricken with a grave illness and died.

sentences.zh: 贈假黃鉞、太宰、太師，諡曰肅武。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted the ceremonial axe, Grand Tutor, and Grand Preceptor; posthumous title Suwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the ceremonial axe, the titles of Grand Tutor and Grand Preceptor, and the posthumous name Suwu.

sentences.zh: 皇建初，配享文襄廟庭。

translations.literal: At the start of Huangjian, given a place in the sacrifices at Wenxiang's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Huangjian era he was granted a place in the offerings at Gao Cheng's temple.

sentences.zh: 子晉明嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jinming succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jinming succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 天統中，改封東萊王。

translations.literal: During the Tiantong era, the enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiantong era his title was changed to Prince of Donglai.

sentences.zh: 晉明有俠氣，諸勳貴子孫中，最留心學問。

translations.literal: Jinming had a chivalrous spirit; among the descendants of meritorious nobles, he was most devoted to learning.
translations.idiomatic: Jinming had a chivalrous temperament; among the sons and grandsons of meritorious nobles, he was the most devoted to learning.

sentences.zh: 好酒誕縱。

translations.literal: He loved wine and was unrestrained and wild.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine and lived with reckless abandon.

sentences.zh: 招引賓客，一席之費，動至萬錢，猶恨儉率。

translations.literal: He invited guests; the cost of a single feast often reached ten thousand cash, yet he still regretted its frugality.
translations.idiomatic: He entertained guests lavishly; a single banquet often cost ten thousand cash, yet he still thought it mean.

sentences.zh: 朝廷欲處之貴要地，必以疾辭，告人云：「廢人飲美酒，對名勝。

translations.literal: When the court wished to place him in an important post, he invariably declined on grounds of illness, telling people: "A good-for-nothing drinks fine wine before famous scenery.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court wanted to place him in an important post, he always declined on grounds of illness, telling people, "A worthless man should drink fine wine amid famous scenery.

sentences.zh: 安能作刀筆吏，披反故紙乎？」

translations.literal: How could I serve as a clerk with brush and knife, poring over old paperwork?"
translations.idiomatic: How could I become a clerk with brush and knife, poring over old paperwork?

sentences.zh: 武平末，除尚書左僕射，百餘日，便謝病解官。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuping he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; after a little over a hundred days he pleaded illness and resigned.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wuping era he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, but after little more than a hundred days he pleaded illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 段榮，字子茂，姑臧武威人也。

translations.literal: Duan Rong, styled Zimao, was a native of Wuwei in Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Rong, styled Zimao, came from Wuwei in Guzang.

sentences.zh: 祖信，仕沮渠氏。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xin served the Juqu house.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xin served the Juqu regime.

sentences.zh: 後入魏，以豪族徙北邊，仍家于五原郡。

translations.literal: Later entering Wei, as a powerful clan they were moved to the northern frontier and settled in Wuyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after entering Wei, the family was relocated to the northern frontier as a powerful clan and settled in Wuyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父連，安北府司馬。

translations.literal: His father Lian was Master of Records in the Northern Pacification Office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lian served as Master of Records in the Northern Pacification Office.

sentences.zh: 榮少好曆術，專意星象。

translations.literal: Rong in youth loved calendrical arts and devoted himself to stars and constellations.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Rong loved calendrical science and devoted himself to the stars.

sentences.zh: 正光中，謂人曰：「吾今觀玄象，察人事，不及十年，當有亂矣。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang era he told people: "I have now observed the dark signs above and examined affairs among men; within ten years there will be turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengguang era he told people, "I have now read the heavens and watched affairs among men; within ten years turmoil will come.

sentences.zh: 亂起此地，天下因此橫流，無可避也。」

translations.literal: Turmoil will rise from this place; the empire will thereby be swept into chaos; there will be no escaping it."
translations.idiomatic: The upheaval will begin here, and the realm will be swept into chaos from it; there will be no escape.

sentences.zh: 未幾如言。

translations.literal: Before long it came to pass as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Before long events unfolded exactly as he had said.

sentences.zh: 榮初之杜洛周，因奔爾硃榮。

translations.literal: Rong at first went to Du Luozhou, then fled to Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Rong first joined Du Luozhou, then fled to Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 及神武起兵，榮贊成之。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan raised arms, Rong supported and accomplished it.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised arms, Rong supported the enterprise.

sentences.zh: 神武南討鄴，留榮鎮信都，仍授定州刺史。

translations.literal: Gao Huan marched south against Ye and left Rong to hold Xindu, also appointing him Governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan marched south against Ye, he left Rong to hold Xindu and also appointed him governor of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時攻鄴未克，榮轉輸無闕。

translations.literal: At the time the assault on Ye had not yet succeeded; Rong's transport of supplies never failed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the assault on Ye had not yet succeeded, yet Rong's supply lines never faltered.

sentences.zh: 神武入洛，論功封姑臧縣侯，轉授瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan entered Luoyang, for merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Guzang County and transferred to Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan entered Luoyang, Rong was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guzang County for his merit and transferred to governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 榮妻，武明皇后長姊也，榮恐神武招私親之議，固推諸將，竟不之州。

translations.literal: Rong's wife was the eldest sister of Empress Wuming; Rong feared Gao Huan would draw criticism for favoring private kin, firmly pushed it on other generals, and in the end never went to that province.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's wife was the eldest sister of Empress Wuming; fearing that Gao Huan would be accused of favoring a relative, he firmly pushed the appointment onto other generals and in the end never took up the governorship.

sentences.zh: 尋曆相、濟、秦三州，所在百姓愛之。

translations.literal: Soon he served in succession the three provinces of Xiang, Ji, and Qin; wherever he was, the common people loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he served in succession at Xiang, Ji, and Qin, and wherever he went the people loved him.

sentences.zh: 神武將圖關右，榮稱未可，及渭曲敗，神武曰：「不用段榮言，以至於此。」

translations.literal: Gao Huan was about to plan for the Guanxi region; Rong said it was not yet feasible; after defeat at Weiqu, Gao Huan said: "Had I not taken Duan Rong's counsel, I would not have come to this."
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan planned to move against Guanxi, Rong said the time was not right; after the defeat at Weiqu, Gao Huan said, "Had I heeded Duan Rong's advice, I would not have come to this.

sentences.zh: 尋除山東大行台，領本州流人大都督，甚得物情。

translations.literal: Soon removed and made Grand Commissioner of the Eastern Mountain region, heading the Great Commander of displaced persons of his native province; he won people's hearts greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made Grand Commissioner of the Eastern Mountain region and head commander of displaced persons from his native province, and he won the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太尉，諡曰昭景。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Grand Commandant; posthumous title Zhaojing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Grand Commandant with the posthumous name Zhaojing.

sentences.zh: 皇建初，配享神武廟庭。

translations.literal: At the start of Huangjian, given a place in the sacrifices at Gao Huan's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Huangjian era he was granted a place in the offerings at Gao Huan's temple.

sentences.zh: 二年，重贈大司馬、尚書令、武威王。

translations.literal: In the second year, posthumously given again as Grand Marshal, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Prince of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was posthumously honored again as Grand Marshal, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Prince of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 長子韶嗣。

translations.literal: His eldest son Shao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Shao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 韶字孝先，少工騎射，有將領才略。

translations.literal: Shao, styled Xiaoxian, in youth was skilled at mounted archery and had the talent and strategy of a commander.
translations.idiomatic: Shao, styled Xiaoxian, was skilled in horsemanship and archery from youth and possessed the talent and strategy of a commander.

sentences.zh: 以武明皇后甥，神武益器愛之，常置左右，以為心腹，領親信都督。

translations.literal: As nephew of Empress Wuming, Gao Huan valued and loved him all the more, kept him always at his side as a trusted confidant, and made him Director of Trusted Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: As nephew of Empress Wuming, he was all the more prized and favored by Gao Huan, who kept him constantly at his side as a trusted confidant and made him Director of Trusted Attendants.

sentences.zh: 神武拒爾硃兆于廣阿，憚兆兵眾。

translations.literal: Gao Huan held Erzhu Zhao at bay at Guang'a and feared Zhao's numerous troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan faced Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a, he feared the size of Zhao's army.

sentences.zh: 韶曰：「所謂眾者，得眾人之死；

translations.literal: Shao said: "What is called 'numerous' is winning the people's willingness to die;
translations.idiomatic: Shao said, "What is called 'numerous' is winning men willing to die for you;

sentences.zh: 所謂強者，得天下之心。

translations.literal: what is called 'strong' is winning the heart of All-under-Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: what is called 'strong' is winning the heart of the realm.

sentences.zh: 爾硃裂冠毀冕，拔本塞原。

translations.literal: The Erzhu clan tore the cap and ruined the crown, uprooted the trunk and blocked the source.
translations.idiomatic: The Erzhu tore the cap and destroyed the crown, uprooted the trunk and choked off the source.

sentences.zh: 芒山之會，搢紳何罪？

translations.literal: At the Mangshan assembly, what crime had the gentry?
translations.idiomatic: At the assembly on Mangshan, what crime had the gentry committed?

sentences.zh: 殺主立君，不脫旬朔。

translations.literal: They killed the ruler and raised a new one — within ten days or a month.
translations.idiomatic: They killed the ruler and set up another in less than a month.

sentences.zh: 天下從亂，士室而九。

translations.literal: All-under-Heaven followed chaos; of scholar households, nine in ten.
translations.idiomatic: The realm slid into chaos, and nine out of ten genteel households were swept under.

sentences.zh: 王躬昭德義，誅君側之惡，何往而不克哉！」

translations.literal: Your Highness personally displays virtue and righteousness, punishing evil beside the throne — where could you not prevail!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness yourself embodies virtue and righteousness and punishes the evil at the ruler's side — where could you fail to prevail!

sentences.zh: 神武曰：「吾雖以順討逆，恐無天命。」

translations.literal: Gao Huan said: "Though I use righteousness to punish rebellion, I fear I lack Heaven's mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "Though I march in righteousness against rebellion, I fear Heaven has not granted me the mandate.

sentences.zh: 韶曰：「聞小能敵大，小道大淫，皇天無親，唯德是輔。

translations.literal: Shao said: "I have heard that the small can overcome the large, the narrow path can overflow greatly; High Heaven is without partiality — only virtue is what it assists.
translations.idiomatic: Shao said, "I have heard that the small can overcome the large, that a narrow way may yet run to excess, and that High Heaven shows no partiality — it assists only virtue.

sentences.zh: 今爾硃外賊天下，內失善人，智者不為謀，勇者不為鬥。

translations.literal: Now the Erzhu outwardly harry All-under-Heaven, inwardly have lost good men; the wise will not plan for them, the brave will not fight for them.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Erzhu plunder the realm abroad and have lost good men at home; the wise will not counsel them, and the brave will not fight for them.

sentences.zh: 不肖失職，賢者取之，復何疑也！」

translations.literal: When the unworthy lose their posts, the worthy take them — what further doubt is there!"
translations.idiomatic: When the unworthy lose their place, the worthy take it — what further doubt can there be!

sentences.zh: 遂與挑戰，敗之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they offered battle and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they offered battle and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 頻以軍功，封下洛縣男，後回賜父爵姑臧縣侯。

translations.literal: Through repeated military merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Xialuo County; later the father's title of Marquis of Guzang County was returned to him as grant.
translations.idiomatic: Through repeated military achievements he was enfeoffed as Baron of Xialuo County; later his father's title as Marquis of Guzang County was returned to him by imperial grant.

sentences.zh: 芒山之役，為賀拔勝所窘，韶從傍馳馬反射，斃其馬，追騎不敢進，遂免。

translations.literal: At the battle of Mangshan, hard pressed by Helü Ba Sheng, Shao rode up from the side and shot back while galloping, killed Sheng's horse; the pursuing horsemen dared not advance, and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Mangshan, when hard pressed by Helü Ba Sheng, Shao galloped up from the side and shot back on the run, killing Sheng's horse; the pursuers dared not press on, and he escaped.

sentences.zh: 賜鞍下馬並金，進爵為公。

translations.literal: He was granted the saddle, dismount horse, and gold; his rank was advanced to Duke.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with the saddle, the horse he had dismounted from, and gold, and his rank was advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 及征玉壁，攻城未下，神武不豫。

translations.literal: When campaigning against Yubi, the city was not taken by assault; Gao Huan was unwell.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Yubi, when the city had still not fallen, Gao Huan fell ill.

sentences.zh: 謂大司馬斛律金、司徒韓軌、左衛將軍劉豐等曰：「吾每謂孝先論兵，殊有英略，若比來用其謀，可無今日之勞矣。

translations.literal: He said to Grand Marshal Hulü Jin, Minister over the Masses Han Gui, General of the Left Guard Liu Feng and others: "Whenever I discuss warfare with Xiaoxian, he shows truly brilliant strategy; had I used his plans throughout, we might have been spared today's toil.
translations.idiomatic: He said to Grand Marshal Hulü Jin, Minister over the Masses Han Gui, General of the Left Guard Liu Feng, and the others, "Whenever I discuss warfare with Xiaoxian, he shows truly brilliant strategy; had I followed his counsel all along, we might have been spared today's hardship.

sentences.zh: 吾患危篤，欲委孝先以鄴下事，若何？」

translations.literal: I am gravely ill; I wish to entrust affairs under Ye to Xiaoxian — what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: I am gravely ill and wish to entrust affairs at Ye to Xiaoxian — what do you think?

sentences.zh: 金等咸曰：「知臣莫若君，實無出孝先者。」

translations.literal: Jin and the others all said: "None knows a minister as his lord does; truly none surpasses Xiaoxian."
translations.idiomatic: Jin and the others all said, "No one knows a minister as his lord does; truly none surpasses Xiaoxian.

sentences.zh: 仍令韶從文宣鎮鄴，召文襄赴軍顧命。

translations.literal: He then ordered Shao to follow Wenxuan in holding Ye, and summoned Wenxiang to the army for a final charge.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Shao to accompany Gao Yang in garrisoning Ye and summoned Gao Cheng to the army to receive his deathbed instructions.

sentences.zh: 文襄以孝先為托，令軍旅大事，並與籌之。

translations.literal: Wenxiang entrusted affairs to Xiaoxian, ordering that all major military matters be deliberated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng entrusted affairs to Xiaoxian and ordered that all major military matters be decided with him.

sentences.zh: 及神武崩，侯景反，文襄還鄴，留韶守晉陽，委以軍事。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan died, Hou Jing rebelled; Wenxiang returned to Ye, left Shao to hold Jinyang, and entrusted him with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan died and Hou Jing rebelled, Gao Cheng returned to Ye, left Shao to hold Jinyang, and entrusted him with military affairs.

sentences.zh: 加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of the State with the honorific Three Divisions.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and made Grand Master of the State with the honorific Three Divisions.

sentences.zh: 文宣受禪，除尚書右僕射，遷冀州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenxuan received the abdication, Shao was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and transferred to Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenxuan took the throne, Shao was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and then transferred to Inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 天保四年，梁將東方白額潛至宿豫，詔韶討之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianbao, Liang general Dongfang Baie secretly reached Suyu; an edict ordered Shao to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianbao, the Liang general Dongfang Baie stole into Suyu; the court ordered Shao to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 既至，會梁將嚴超達等軍逼涇州，陳霸先將攻廣陵，尹令思謀襲盱眙，三軍咸懼。

translations.literal: When he arrived, it happened that Liang generals Yan Chaoda and others pressed Jingzhou with their army, Chen Baxian was about to attack Guangling, and Yin Lingsi plotted to strike Xuyi—the three armies were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his arrival, Liang generals led by Yan Chaoda were pressing Jingzhou, Chen Baxian was preparing to attack Guangling, and Yin Lingsi was plotting a raid on Xuyi; all three armies were seized with fear.

sentences.zh: 韶謂諸將曰：「自梁氏喪亂，國無定主，人懷去就。

translations.literal: Shao said to the generals: "Since the Liang house fell into chaos, the state has had no fixed ruler, and the people weigh whether to stay or go.
translations.idiomatic: Shao told the generals, "Since the Liang dynasty collapsed into disorder, the realm has lacked a settled sovereign, and men everywhere are deciding whom to follow.

sentences.zh: 霸先外托同德，內有離心，吾揣之熟矣。」

translations.literal: Baxian outwardly professes shared purpose but inwardly bears divided loyalty—I have gauged this thoroughly."
translations.idiomatic: Baxian puts on a show of unity, but in his heart he is already divided from us. I have taken his measure, and I know it well."

sentences.zh: 乃留儀同三司敬顯俊等圍宿豫，自倍道赴涇州。

translations.literal: He then left Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes Jing Xianjun and others to besiege Suyu, while he himself hurried by forced marches to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He left Jing Xianjun, Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes, and others to continue the siege of Suyu, while he himself raced by forced marches to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 塗出盱眙，令思不虞大軍卒至，望旗而奔。

translations.literal: Passing through Xuyi on the way, Yin Lingsi did not expect the main army to arrive so suddenly; at the sight of the banners he fled.
translations.idiomatic: When his route brought him through Xuyi, Yin Lingsi never imagined the main army would appear so suddenly; the moment he saw its banners he broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 進破超達軍。

translations.literal: Advancing, he defeated Yan Chaoda's army.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing forward, he routed Yan Chaoda's force.

sentences.zh: 回赴廣陵，霸先遁走。

translations.literal: Turning back toward Guangling, Baxian fled.
translations.idiomatic: He then swung back toward Guangling, and Baxian fled before him.

sentences.zh: 旋師宿豫，遣辨士喻白額。

translations.literal: He wheeled his army back to Suyu and sent an eloquent envoy to persuade Baie.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to Suyu, he sent a skilled persuader to reason with Baie.

sentences.zh: 白額開門請盟。

translations.literal: Baie opened the gates and requested a covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Baie opened the gates and asked to make peace under oath.

sentences.zh: 盟訖，度白額終不為用，斬之，並其諸弟，並傳首京師。

translations.literal: When the covenant was concluded, judging that Baie would never serve them, he beheaded him together with all his younger brothers and sent their heads to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Once the pact was sealed, Shao decided that Baie would never truly submit; he executed him along with all his brothers and sent their heads to the capital.

sentences.zh: 封平原郡王，曆司空、司徒、大將軍、尚書令、太子太師。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Pingyuan Commandery and in succession served as Minister of Works, Minister over the Masses, Grand General, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Pingyuan and rose in turn through Minister of Works, Minister over the Masses, Grand General, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 以繼母憂，去職。

translations.literal: On mourning for his stepmother, he left office.
translations.idiomatic: When his stepmother died, he resigned his posts to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 尋起為大司馬，仍為尚書令，遷錄尚書事、并州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as Grand Marshal, still Director of the Department of State Affairs, and transferred to Recorder of the Department of State Affairs and Inspector of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled as Grand Marshal, retained as Director of the Department of State Affairs, and promoted to Recorder of the Department of State Affairs and Inspector of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 後與東安王婁睿平高歸彥，遷太傅，仍蒞并州。

translations.literal: Later, together with Prince of Dong'an Lou Rui he pacified Gao Guiyan; he was promoted to Grand Tutor and still took up Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Prince of Dong'an Lou Rui in putting down Gao Guiyan, was promoted to Grand Tutor, and continued to govern Bingzhou in person.

sentences.zh: 為政不存小察，甚得人和。

translations.literal: In governing he did not dwell on petty scrutiny and greatly won popular harmony.
translations.idiomatic: In administration he did not fuss over trifles, and he won broad goodwill among the people.

sentences.zh: 周文遣將率羌夷與突厥合眾逼晉陽，武成自鄴倍道赴之。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen Di sent generals leading Qiang and tribal peoples together with the Turks in a combined host pressing Jinyang; Emperor Wucheng hurried from Ye by forced marches to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen Di sent generals at the head of Qiang tribesmen and other frontier peoples, together with the Turks in a great combined force, to press Jinyang; Emperor Wucheng raced from Ye by forced marches to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 時大雪，諸將或欲逆之，韶曰：「不如陣以待之。

translations.literal: Snow was heavy at the time; some generals wished to meet the enemy head-on; Shao said: "Better to form battle lines and wait for them.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow was falling, and some of the generals wanted to meet the enemy at once. Shao said, "It is better to draw up in formation and wait.

sentences.zh: 彼勞我逸，破之必矣。」

translations.literal: They are weary while we are rested—defeating them is certain."
translations.idiomatic: They are exhausted and we are fresh; if we hold our ground, victory is assured."

sentences.zh: 遂大破之。

translations.literal: They therefore inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: They did so and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 進位太師。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 周塚宰宇文護母閻氏，先配中山宮，護聞尚存，乃因邊境移書，請還其母，並通鄰好。

translations.literal: The mother of Zhou's Grand Minister Yuwen Hu, Lady Yan, had earlier been assigned to Zhongshan Palace; when Hu learned she was still alive he sent a letter through the border requesting her return and also seeking neighborly amity.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu, Grand Minister of Zhou, had a mother, Lady Yan, who had earlier been consigned to Zhongshan Palace. Learning that she still lived, Hu sent a letter across the frontier asking for her return and proposing good relations between the two states.

sentences.zh: 韶以為護外托為相，其實王也。

translations.literal: Shao held that Hu outwardly styled himself chancellor but was in fact a king.
translations.idiomatic: Shao argued that Hu called himself chancellor only in name while in truth he ruled like a king.

sentences.zh: 為母請和，不通一介之使，據移送書，恐示以弱。

translations.literal: To seek peace for his mother's sake without sending even a single envoy, but relying on a transferred letter—he feared this would show weakness.
translations.idiomatic: To sue for peace on behalf of his mother without exchanging a single envoy, and to answer only a letter passed across the border, would reveal weakness, he warned.

sentences.zh: 且外許之，待通和往復，放之未晚。

translations.literal: Moreover, outwardly promise it, wait until amity had been exchanged back and forth—it would not be too late to release her then.
translations.idiomatic: Better to agree outwardly, let negotiations run their course, and only then release her; it would not be too late.

sentences.zh: 不聽，遂遣使以禮將送。

translations.literal: His advice was not heeded; they therefore sent envoys to escort her back with full ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The court would not listen. Envoys were sent instead to return her with full ceremonial honors.

sentences.zh: 護得母，仍遣將尉遲迥等襲洛陽。

translations.literal: When Hu recovered his mother, he still sent generals Yuchi Jiong and others to raid Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hu had his mother back, he nevertheless dispatched Yuchi Jiong and other generals to strike at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 詔蘭陵王長恭、大將軍斛律光擊之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Prince of Lanling Gao Changgong and Grand General Hulü Guang to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Prince of Lanling Gao Changgong and Grand General Hulü Guang to repel them.

sentences.zh: 軍次芒山下，逗留未進。

translations.literal: The army halted below Mount Mang and lingered without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: The army camped below Mount Mang and hung back, refusing to advance.

sentences.zh: 武成召韶，欲赴洛陽圍，但以突厥為慮。

translations.literal: Emperor Wucheng summoned Shao, wishing to go relieve the siege of Luoyang, but was concerned about the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng summoned Shao, eager to march to lift the siege of Luoyang but worried about the Turks on the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 韶曰：「北虜侵邊，事等疥癬；

translations.literal: Shao said: "Northern barbarians harassing the frontier are like scabies;
translations.idiomatic: Shao said, "Barbarian raids in the north are a mere itch on the skin;

sentences.zh: 西羌窺逼，是膏肓之病。」

translations.literal: Western Qiang probing and pressing—that is a disease in the vital organs.
translations.idiomatic: the Western Qiang pressing in from the west are a sickness in the marrow.

sentences.zh: 帝仍令韶督精騎一千發晉陽，五日便濟河。

translations.literal: The emperor still ordered Shao to lead a thousand elite cavalry from Jinyang; within five days they had crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still ordered Shao to take command of a thousand picked horsemen out of Jinyang; within five days they had crossed the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 遇周軍于大和谷，與諸將陣以待之。

translations.literal: They met Zhou troops at Dahe Valley and with the generals formed battle lines to await them.
translations.idiomatic: At Dahe Valley they encountered the Zhou army and, with the other generals, drew up in battle order to receive them.

sentences.zh: 韶為左軍，蘭陵王為中軍，斛律光為右軍。

translations.literal: Shao commanded the left wing, the Prince of Lanling the center, and Hulü Guang the right.
translations.idiomatic: Shao took the left wing, the Prince of Lanling the center, and Hulü Guang the right.

sentences.zh: 上山逆戰，韶且卻引，待其力弊，下馬擊之，周人大潰。

translations.literal: Ascending the hill to meet them in battle, Shao first withdrew to draw them on, waited until their strength was spent, then dismounted to strike—they routed the Zhou forces completely.
translations.idiomatic: Shao climbed the slope to give battle, then feigned retreat to pull the enemy forward; when their strength was spent he dismounted and closed with them, and the Zhou army broke in complete rout.

sentences.zh: 洛城圍亦即奔遁。

translations.literal: The siege of Luoyang then also broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The besiegers at Luoyang likewise broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 除太宰，封靈武縣公。

translations.literal: He was made Grand Mentor and enfeoffed as Duke of Lingwu County.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Mentor and enfeoffed as Duke of Lingwu County.

sentences.zh: 天統三年，除左丞相。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiantong he was made Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiantong he was appointed Left Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 四年，別封永昌郡公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was separately enfeoffed as Duke of Yongchang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he received a separate enfeoffment as Duke of Yongchang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 食滄州幹。

translations.literal: He drew sustenance revenue from Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His income fief was assigned in Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 武平二年，出晉州道，到定隴，築威敵、平寇二城而還。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wuping he marched out by the Jinzhou route, reached Dinglong, built the two fortresses Weidi and Pingkou, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wuping he led a force out along the Jinzhou road, reached Dinglong, built the fortresses Weidi and Pingkou, and returned.

sentences.zh: 二月，周師來寇，遣韶與右丞相斛律光、太尉蘭陵王長恭往。

translations.literal: In the second month, Zhou troops came raiding; Shao was dispatched together with Right Chancellor Hulü Guang and Grand Commandant Prince of Lanling Gao Changgong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, when Zhou armies invaded the frontier, Shao was sent out with Right Chancellor Hulü Guang and Grand Commandant Prince of Lanling Gao Changgong.

sentences.zh: 行達西境，有柏穀城者，敵之絕險，諸將莫肯攻圍。

translations.literal: Marching to the western frontier, there was a place called Baigu Fortress—the enemy's supreme stronghold—and none of the generals would besiege it.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the western border they came upon Baigu Fortress, an enemy stronghold of forbidding strength, and none of the generals would commit to besieging it.

sentences.zh: 韶曰：「汾北河東，勢為國家之有，若不去柏穀，事同痼疾。

translations.literal: Shao said: "North of the Fen and east of the Yellow River are by right the state's possession; if we do not take Baigu, the matter is like a chronic malady.
translations.idiomatic: Shao said, "The lands north of the Fen and east of the Yellow River ought by rights to be ours. If we leave Baigu untaken, it will fester like an old wound.

sentences.zh: 計彼會兵在南道。

translations.literal: I reckon they will muster troops on the southern route.
translations.idiomatic: I expect the enemy will gather reinforcements along the southern road.

sentences.zh: 今斷其要路，救不能來。

translations.literal: If we now cut their vital road, relief cannot come.
translations.idiomatic: Cut their lifeline now, and no relief can reach them.

sentences.zh: 城勢雖高，其中甚狹，火弩射之，一旦可盡。」

translations.literal: Though the fortress stands high, inside it is very narrow—fire-arrows shot into it can wipe them out in a day."
translations.idiomatic: The walls are high, but the space within is cramped; a barrage of fire-arrows can destroy them in a single day."

sentences.zh: 遂攻之，城潰。

translations.literal: They thereupon attacked it and the fortress collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked at once, and the fortress fell.

sentences.zh: 仍城華穀，置戍而還。

translations.literal: They then fortified Huagu, garrisoned it, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They then built up Huagu, left a garrison, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 封廣平郡公。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Guangping Commandery.
