translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Guangping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 是月，周又遣將攻邊，斛律光先率軍禦之，韶亦請行。

translations.literal: That month Zhou again sent generals to attack the frontier; Hulü Guang first led the army to resist, and Shao also requested to go.
translations.idiomatic: That same month the Zhou sent another force against the border. Hulü Guang marched out first to meet them, and Shao asked to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 五月，到服秦城。

translations.literal: In the fifth month they reached Fuqin Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month they arrived at Fuqin Fortress.

sentences.zh: 西人于姚襄城南更起城鎮，韶抽壯士從北襲之，使人潛度河告姚襄城中，內外相應，進戰大破之。

translations.literal: Westerners had built a new fortress south of Yao Xiang; Shao drew off crack troops to strike from the north, sent men secretly to cross the river and notify the city of Yao Xiang, coordinated inside and out, advanced to battle and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The Westerners had raised a new walled town south of Yao Xiang. Shao detached picked warriors to strike from the north, sent men secretly across the river to signal the garrison at Yao Xiang, and coordinated an attack from within and without that ended in a great victory.

sentences.zh: 諸將咸欲攻其新城，韶曰：「此城一面陰河，三面地險，不可攻。

translations.literal: All the generals wished to attack their new fortress; Shao said: "This fortress has the river on one side and dangerous ground on three—it cannot be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: The generals all wanted to storm the new fortress, but Shao said, "It lies against the river on one side and sheer ground on the other three; it cannot be taken by assault.

sentences.zh: 不如更作一城，壅其要道。

translations.literal: Better to build another fortress and block their vital route.
translations.idiomatic: Better to erect another fort and choke off their line of supply.

sentences.zh: 破服秦，並力圖之。」

translations.literal: Break Fuqin, then combine forces and take aim at it."
translations.idiomatic: Once Fuqin falls, we can concentrate our strength and deal with it then."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: They followed his plan.
translations.idiomatic: They accepted his plan.

sentences.zh: 六月，徙圍定陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth month they shifted the siege to Dingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month they moved the siege to Dingyang.

sentences.zh: 七月，屠其外城。

translations.literal: In the seventh month they slaughtered through the outer city.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month they stormed and overran the outer city.

sentences.zh: 時韶病在軍中，謂蘭陵王曰：「此城三面重澗，並無走路，唯慮東面一處耳。

translations.literal: At the time Shao was ill in camp; he said to the Prince of Lanling: "This city has deep ravines on three sides and no escape route anywhere—only the eastern side need worry us.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was then gravely ill in camp. He told the Prince of Lanling, "This city is hemmed in by deep gullies on three sides and has no way out anywhere save one opening to the east.

sentences.zh: 賊若突圍，必從此出。」

translations.literal: If the enemy breaks out, they will surely come this way."
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy tries to break out, they will surely take that route."

sentences.zh: 長恭乃設伏。

translations.literal: Changgong then set an ambush.
translations.idiomatic: Changgong accordingly laid an ambush.

sentences.zh: 其夜，果如策，伏兵擊之，大潰。

translations.literal: That night it happened exactly as he predicted; the ambush struck and the enemy was routed completely.
translations.idiomatic: That night events unfolded exactly as Shao had foreseen; the hidden troops fell upon the breakout force and put it to utter rout.

sentences.zh: 韶竟以病薨。

translations.literal: Shao ultimately died of his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Shao finally succumbed to his illness.

sentences.zh: 賜溫明秘器、轀輬車。

translations.literal: He was granted the warm-bright secret coffin and the imperial hearse.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted an imperial lacquered coffin and a state funeral carriage.

sentences.zh: 軍校之士，陣送至平恩墓所，發卒起塚。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers of the army lined up to escort him to the tomb site at Ping'en, and conscripts were raised to build the mound.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men of the army formed ranks to escort the body to the burial ground at Ping'en, and laborers were conscripted to raise the tomb mound.

sentences.zh: 贈假黃鉞、相國、太尉、錄尚書事，諡忠武。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted the ceremonial yellow battle-axe, Chancellor of State, Grand Commandant, and Recorder of the Department of State Affairs, with the posthumous title Zhongwu (Loyal and Martial).
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was honored with the yellow battle-axe, the titles Chancellor of State, Grand Commandant, and Recorder of the Department of State Affairs, and the posthumous name Loyal and Martial.

sentences.zh: 韶出總軍旅，入參幃幄，功既居高，重以婚媾之故，望傾朝野。

translations.literal: Shao went out to command armies and entered to share the inner counsel of the tent; his merit stood at the top, and compounded by ties of marriage, his prestige tilted court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Shao commanded armies in the field and sat in the inner councils of state; his achievements ranked among the highest, and with marriage ties to the throne his standing overshadowed court and realm alike.

sentences.zh: 而長於計略，善於禦眾，得將士之心。

translations.literal: Yet he excelled in stratagem, was skilled at commanding the multitude, and won the hearts of officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He was gifted in strategy, adept at handling troops, and held the deep loyalty of officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 又雅性溫慎，有宰相之風。

translations.literal: Moreover, by nature he was mild and cautious, with the bearing of a chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: By temperament he was gentle and careful, with the measured air of a true minister of state.

sentences.zh: 教訓子弟，閨門雍肅，事後母以孝聞。

translations.literal: He instructed his sons and younger kinsmen; his inner quarters were harmonious and solemn, and he was famed for filial duty toward his stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: He trained his sons and younger relatives with strict care; his household was orderly and dignified, and he was widely praised for the filial devotion he showed his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 齊代勳貴家，罕有及者。

translations.literal: Among the meritorious and noble houses of Qi, few could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Among the great families of merit in Northern Qi, few could equal him.

sentences.zh: 然僻于好色，雖居要重，微服間行。

translations.literal: Yet he was partial to lust; though he held weighty posts, he would go out in disguise by unmarked routes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was given to womanizing; even while holding the highest offices, he would slip out in plain dress by back ways.

sentences.zh: 魏黃門郎元瑀妻皇甫氏，緣瑀謀逆，沒官。

translations.literal: The wife of Wei Yellow Gate Attendant Yuan Yu, of the Huangfu clan, because Yu plotted rebellion, was confiscated into government service.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu, wife of Yuan Yu, Yellow Gate Attendant of Wei, had been seized for the state when Yu was implicated in a plot of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 韶美之，上啟固請，文襄賜之。

translations.literal: Shao admired her beauty, memorialized and firmly requested her, and Wenxiang bestowed her upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Struck by her beauty, Shao memorialized the throne and pressed his request until Wenxiang granted her to him.

sentences.zh: 別宅處之，禮同正嫡。

translations.literal: He housed her in a separate residence and treated her with the rites due a principal wife.
translations.idiomatic: He installed her in a separate mansion and honored her with the ceremony owed a lawful wife.

sentences.zh: 尤嗇于財，親戚故舊，略無施與。

translations.literal: He was especially miserly with wealth; to kin and old friends he gave next to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He was notoriously tight with money and scarcely gave anything even to relatives and old companions.

sentences.zh: 其子深尚公主，並省丞郎在家佐事十餘日，事畢辭還，人唯賜一杯酒。

translations.literal: When his son Shen married a princess, a combined provincial secretariat aide and directorate gentleman assisted with household affairs for more than ten days; when the matter was finished and he took leave to return, each person received only one cup of wine.
translations.idiomatic: When his son Shen married a princess, an aide and directorate gentleman from the Bing provincial secretariat spent more than ten days helping with the household arrangements; when the work was done and they came to take their leave, Shao rewarded each man with a single cup of wine.

sentences.zh: 元妃所生三子：懿、深、亮，皆宦達。

translations.literal: The three sons born by the Yuan consort—Yi, Shen, and Liang—all reached official success.
translations.idiomatic: The three sons borne by Lady Yuan—Yi, Shen, and Liang—all rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 懿字德猷，尚潁川長公主，拜駙馬都尉，襲封平原王。

translations.literal: Yi, style name Deyou, married the Long Princess of Yingchuan, was appointed Commandant of the Feathered Forest, and succeeded to the enfeoffment as Prince of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, styled Deyou, married the Long Princess of Yingchuan, became Commandant of the Feathered Forest, and inherited the title Prince of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 位行台右僕射，兼殿中尚書，卒。

translations.literal: He served as Right Vice Director of the Mobile Headquarters and concurrently Palace Secretary; he died.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of Right Vice Director of the Mobile Headquarters and Palace Secretary concurrently, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子寶鼎，尚中山長公主。

translations.literal: His son Baoding married the Long Princess of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baoding married the Long Princess of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Under Sui, in the Kaihuang era, he was Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes with an open office.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui, during Kaihuang, he served as Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes with an open office.

sentences.zh: 大業初，卒于饒州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye he died while serving as Inspector of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Daye reign he died while Inspector of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 深字德深，美容貌，寬謹有父風。

translations.literal: Shen, style name Deshen, had handsome looks; he was broad-minded and cautious, with his father's bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen, styled Deshen, was handsome in face and figure, open and careful in manner, and carried himself in his father's mold.

sentences.zh: 天保中，受父封姑臧縣公。

translations.literal: During Tianbao he received his father's enfeoffment as Duke of Guzang County.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao he inherited from his father the title Duke of Guzang County.

sentences.zh: 尚東安公主，位侍中。

translations.literal: He married the Princess of Dong'an and served as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Princess of Dong'an and rose to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 韶病篤，詔封深濟北王，以慰其意。

translations.literal: When Shao's illness was grave, an edict enfeoffed Shen as Prince of Jibei to comfort his mind.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao lay near death, an edict enfeoffed Shen as Prince of Jibei to ease his final days.

sentences.zh: 入周，拜大將軍、郡公，坐事死。

translations.literal: Entering Zhou, he was appointed Grand General and a commandery duke, but died by execution for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi fell and he entered Zhou service, he was made Grand General and a commandery duke, but was later executed for a crime.

sentences.zh: 亮字德堪。

translations.literal: Liang, style name Dekan.
translations.idiomatic: Liang, styled Dekan.

sentences.zh: 隋大業初，位汴州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sui Daye he served as Inspector of Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Sui Daye reign he served as Inspector of Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒于汝南郡守。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Administrator of Runan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as Administrator of Runan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 韶弟孝言，少警發，有風儀。

translations.literal: Shao's younger brother Xiaoyan from youth was quick-witted and had bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's younger brother Xiaoyan had been sharp and alert from boyhood and carried himself with natural dignity.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，其兄韶以別封霸城縣侯授之。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his elder brother Shao granted him a separate enfeoffment as Marquis of Bacheng County.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi was founded, his elder brother Shao gave him a separate enfeoffment as Marquis of Bacheng County.

sentences.zh: 曆中書黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Secretariat Yellow Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through service as Secretariat Yellow Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 典機密。

translations.literal: He managed confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw state secrets.

sentences.zh: 又曆秘書監、度支尚書、清都尹。

translations.literal: He also served in succession as Director of the Secretariat, Minister of Revenue, and Prefect of Qingdu.
translations.idiomatic: He later held in turn the posts of Director of the Secretariat, Minister of Revenue, and Prefect of the capital district of Qingdu.

sentences.zh: 孝言本以勳戚致位通顯，驕奢無憚。

translations.literal: Xiaoyan had originally attained eminent rank through merit and kinship, and was arrogant, extravagant, and without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyan had risen to prominence through battlefield merit and imperial connection, and once there he grew proud, lavish, and utterly without restraint.

sentences.zh: 曾夜過其客宋孝王家，呼坊人防援，不時赴，遂拷殺之。

translations.literal: Once at night he passed the home of his guest Song Xiaowang, summoned the ward warden Fang Yuan, who did not come in time, and had him beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: One night he stopped at the home of his guest Song Xiaowang and summoned the ward warden Fang Yuan. When Fang failed to come promptly, Xiaoyan had him tortured and killed.

sentences.zh: 又與諸淫婦密遊。

translations.literal: Again he secretly traveled with various debauched women.
translations.idiomatic: He also carried on secret liaisons with various loose women.

sentences.zh: 其夫覺，又拷掠而殞。

translations.literal: Their husbands discovered it; again he tortured and flogged, and they died.
translations.idiomatic: When their husbands found out, he tortured the women again until they died.

sentences.zh: 時苑內須果木，課人間及僧寺備輸，孝言悉分向其私宅種植。

translations.literal: At the time the park within the palace needed fruit trees; commoners and Buddhist temples were levied to supply them, and Xiaoyan entirely diverted them to plant at his private residences.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial park needed fruit trees, levies were imposed on commoners and monasteries to furnish them. Xiaoyan diverted the whole supply to plant at his own estates.

sentences.zh: 又殿內及園中須石，差車從漳河運載，復分車回取。

translations.literal: Again stone was needed for the palace halls and gardens; carts were dispatched to haul from the Zhang River, and he again diverted carts to haul back for himself.
translations.idiomatic: When stone was needed for the palace halls and gardens, carts were sent to haul it from the Zhang River. Xiaoyan again diverted carts to haul loads back for his own use.

sentences.zh: 事發，出為海州刺史。

translations.literal: When the matter came to light, he was sent out as governor of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was exposed, he was demoted and sent out as governor of Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 累遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 祖珽執政，將廢趙彥深，引孝言為助，加侍中。

translations.literal: Zu Ting held power and planned to depose Zhao Yanshen; he enlisted Xiaoyan's help and had him appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Zu Ting held the reins of government and set out to remove Zhao Yanshen, he brought Xiaoyan in as an ally and had him appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 孝言待物不平，抽擢非賄則舊。

translations.literal: Xiaoyan was partial in his dealings; promotions went only to those who bribed or were old associates.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyan showed favoritism in all he did. Advancement went only to men who paid bribes or were old cronies.

sentences.zh: 有將作丞崔成於眾中抗言：「尚書，天下尚書，豈獨段家尚書也！」

translations.literal: The Assistant Director of Palace Construction Cui Cheng protested openly in the assembly: "Minister! There are ministers throughout the realm—is the post of Minister the exclusive property of the Duan clan?"
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Director of Palace Construction Cui Cheng spoke up boldly before the assembly: "Minister! There are ministers throughout the empire—surely the office is not the Duan family's private preserve?

sentences.zh: 孝言元辭以對，唯厲色遣下。

translations.literal: Xiaoyan had no words with which to reply; he only glared and had him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyan could find no answer. He only scowled and had Cui removed.

sentences.zh: 尋除中書監，加特進。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Director of the Secretariat and granted Honorary Grand Counselor status.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Director of the Secretariat and granted the rank of Honorary Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 又托韓長鸞共構祖珽之短。

translations.literal: He also relied on Han Changluan jointly to fabricate charges against Zu Ting.
translations.idiomatic: He also enlisted Han Changluan to help fabricate accusations against Zu Ting.

sentences.zh: 及珽出後，孝言除尚書右僕射，仍掌選。

translations.literal: After Ting was removed, Xiaoyan was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and continued to control appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zu Ting had been driven out, Xiaoyan was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and retained control over official selection.

sentences.zh: 恣情用舍，請謁大行。

translations.literal: He promoted and dismissed at will; bribery flourished.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed and dismissed officials as he pleased, and solicitation of favors became rampant.

sentences.zh: 敕浚京城北隍，孝言監作。

translations.literal: An edict ordered dredging the northern moat of the capital; Xiaoyan supervised the work.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered the northern moat of the capital dredged, Xiaoyan was put in charge of the project.

sentences.zh: 儀同三司崔士順、將作大匠元士將、太府少卿酈孝裕、尚書左戶郎中薛叔昭、司州中從事崔龍子、清都尹丞李道隆、鄴縣令尉長卿、臨漳令崔象、成安令高子徹等，並在孝言部下典作。

translations.literal: Supervising General of the Third Rank Cui Shishun, Grand Master of Palace Construction Yuan Shijiang, Vice Director of the Imperial Storehouse Li Xiaoyu, Left Household Section Director of the Ministry of State Affairs Xue Shuzhao, Middle Staff Officer of Sizhou Cui Longzi, Assistant Magistrate of Qingdu Prefecture Li Daolong, Magistrate of Ye County Wei Zhangqing, Magistrate of Linzhang County Cui Xiang, Magistrate of Cheng'an County Gao Ziche, and others were all under Xiaoyan's command overseeing the work.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising General of the Third Rank Cui Shishun, Grand Master of Palace Construction Yuan Shijiang, Vice Director of the Imperial Storehouse Li Xiaoyu, Left Household Section Director Xue Shuzhao, Middle Staff Officer of Sizhou Cui Longzi, Assistant Magistrate of Qingdu Li Daolong, Magistrate of Ye County Wei Zhangqing, Magistrate of Linzhang Cui Xiang, Magistrate of Cheng'an Gao Ziche, and others all served under Xiaoyan as overseers of the project.

sentences.zh: 日別置酒高會，諸人膝行跪伏，稱觴上壽，或自陳屈滯，更請轉官。

translations.literal: Each day they set out wine for grand feasts; the men crawled on their knees and prostrated themselves, offered cups to toast his longevity, or pleaded their grievances and asked for transfer of office.
translations.idiomatic: Every day they laid out wine for lavish banquets. The men crawled forward on their knees, offered cups to wish him long life, or pleaded their grievances and begged for new appointments.

sentences.zh: 孝言意色揚揚，以為己任，皆隨事報答，許有加授。

translations.literal: Xiaoyan looked pleased, taking it as his duty; he answered each according to the case and promised promotions.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyan looked thoroughly pleased, as though it were his rightful duty. He answered each man according to the occasion and promised promotions.

sentences.zh: 富商大賈，多被銓擢，所進用人士，咸是險縱之流。

translations.literal: Rich merchants were often selected and promoted; the people he advanced were all reckless and dissolute.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy merchants were often chosen and promoted. The men he put in office were all reckless and dissolute.

sentences.zh: 尋遷左僕射，特進、侍中如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Left Vice Director; Honorary Grand Counselor and Palace Attendant remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Left Vice Director, while retaining his posts as Honorary Grand Counselor and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 孝言富貴豪侈，尤好女色。

translations.literal: Xiaoyan was wealthy, noble, and extravagant, especially fond of women.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyan lived in wealth and splendor, and above all he loved women.

sentences.zh: 後取婁定遠妾董氏，大耽愛之。

translations.literal: Later he took Lou Dingyuan's concubine Lady Dong and indulged in her greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Later he took Lou Dingyuan's concubine, Lady Dong, and became utterly infatuated with her.

sentences.zh: 為此內外不和，更相糾列。

translations.literal: Because of this, relations within and without were not harmonious, and they denounced each other.
translations.idiomatic: This brought discord inside and out, and the parties began denouncing one another.

sentences.zh: 又于晉陽監作，坐事除名，徙光州。

translations.literal: Again, while supervising construction at Jinyang, due to an offense he was dismissed from office and banished to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while supervising construction at Jinyang, he was stripped of office for misconduct and exiled to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 隆化主敗後，有敕追還。

translations.literal: After the defeat of the Lord of Longhua, an edict recalled him.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Lord of Longhua, an edict ordered him recalled.

sentences.zh: 孝言雖黷貨無厭，恣情酒色，然舉止風流。

translations.literal: Although Xiaoyan was insatiable in graft and indulged in wine and women, his bearing was elegant.
translations.idiomatic: For all his insatiable greed and his indulgence in wine and women, Xiaoyan's manner remained elegant.

sentences.zh: 招致名士。

translations.literal: He summoned famous men of letters.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered celebrated men of letters to him.

sentences.zh: 美景良辰，未嘗虛棄；

translations.literal: On fine days in beautiful seasons, he never let them pass unused;
translations.idiomatic: On fine days in beautiful seasons, he never let a moment go to waste;

sentences.zh: 賦詩奏伎，以盡歡洽。

translations.literal: composing poetry and presenting entertainments to exhaust the joy of conviviality.
translations.idiomatic: he composed poetry and staged performances until the pleasure of the gathering was fully spent.

sentences.zh: 雖草萊之士，粗關文藝，多引入賓館，與同興賞。

translations.literal: Even men of humble origin who had some connection with literature, he often brought into his guest house to enjoy together.
translations.idiomatic: Even humble men with some modest literary talent he often invited into his guest house to share in his pleasures.

sentences.zh: 其貧躓者，亦時乞遺。

translations.literal: Those in poverty and distress, he also occasionally gave alms to.
translations.idiomatic: Those who were poor and in distress he also sometimes gave handouts.

sentences.zh: 時論復以此多之。

translations.literal: Public opinion again praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion again spoke well of him for this.

sentences.zh: 齊亡入周，位上開府。

translations.literal: When Qi fell he entered Zhou, attaining the rank of Upper Supervising General.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Qi he entered Zhou territory and rose to the rank of Upper Supervising General.

sentences.zh: 斛律金，字阿六敦，朔州敕勒部人也。

translations.literal: Hulü Jin, styled Aluodun, was a man of the Chile tribe of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hulü Jin, styled Aluodun, came from the Chile tribe of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖倍侯利，魏道武時內附，位大羽真，賜爵孟都公。

translations.literal: His ancestor Beihouli submitted to inner allegiance during Emperor Daowu of Wei, held the rank of Dayuzhen, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Mengdu.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Beihouli submitted to Wei allegiance under Emperor Daowu, rose to the rank of Dayuzhen, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Mengdu.

sentences.zh: 祖幡地斤，殿中尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fandijin was Director of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fandijin served as Director of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 父那瑰，光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His father Nagui was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His father Nagui held the post of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 贈司空。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 金性敦直，善騎射，行兵用匈奴法，望塵知馬步多少，嗅地知軍度遠近。

translations.literal: Jin's nature was honest and upright; he was skilled in mounted archery. In campaigning he used Xiongnu methods—gazing at dust he could tell how many horse and foot soldiers there were; smelling the ground he could tell how far an army's camp lay.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was plainspoken and upright, and skilled in mounted archery. On campaign he used Xiongnu methods: from the dust he could tell how many horse and foot soldiers were moving; from the scent of the ground he could judge how far off an army lay.

sentences.zh: 初為軍主，與懷朔鎮將楊鈞送蠕蠕主阿那環。

translations.literal: Initially he was a military commander; with the Huaiyuan garrison commander Yang Jun he escorted the Rouran ruler Anahuan.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as a military commander. Together with Huaiyuan garrison commander Yang Jun, he escorted the Rouran ruler Anahuan.

sentences.zh: 環見金獵射，歎其工。

translations.literal: When Anahuan saw Jin hunting and shooting, he sighed at his skill.
translations.idiomatic: When Anahuan watched Jin hunt and shoot, he marveled at his skill.

sentences.zh: 及破六韓拔陵構逆，金擁眾屬焉，署金為王。

translations.literal: When Bohai Ba Ling raised rebellion, Jin led his followers to submit to him; Ling appointed Jin as king.
translations.idiomatic: When Bohai Ba Ling rebelled, Jin brought his followers over to him, and Ling made Jin a king.

sentences.zh: 金度陵終敗，乃統所部叛陵，詣雲州。

translations.literal: When Jin saw that Ling would ultimately be defeated, he took command of his troops, rebelled against Ling, and went to Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Ling was bound to fail, Jin rallied his own troops, broke with Ling, and went to Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 魏除為第二領人酋長，秋朝京師，春還部落，號曰雁臣。

translations.literal: Wei appointed him second-rank tribal chieftain; in autumn he attended court in the capital, in spring he returned to the tribes—he was called a "wild-goose minister."
translations.idiomatic: Wei appointed him second-rank tribal chieftain. Each autumn he came to court in the capital; each spring he returned to his tribes. He was called a "wild-goose minister."

sentences.zh: 仍稍引南出黃瓜堆，為杜洛周所破。

translations.literal: Still he gradually led them south to Huangguadui and was defeated by Du Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then gradually led his people south to Huangguadui, where Du Luozhou defeated him.

sentences.zh: 與兄平二人脫身歸爾硃榮，為別將。

translations.literal: He and his elder brother Ping, two men, escaped and submitted to Erzhu Rong, serving as a separate commander.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Ping escaped together and submitted to Erzhu Rong, serving as a separate commander.

sentences.zh: 孝莊立，賜爵阜城男。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang was enthroned, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang took the throne, Jin was enfeoffed as Baron of Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 位金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He held the rank of Grand Master of Golden Radiance and Purple Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the rank of Grand Master of Golden Radiance and Purple Splendor.

sentences.zh: 神武密懷匡復，金贊成大謀。

translations.literal: Gao Huan secretly nurtured plans to restore the dynasty; Jin supported him in completing the great design.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan secretly harbored plans to restore order to the realm, and Jin helped him carry the great design through.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，為汾州刺史，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he became governor of Fenzhou and was promoted to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taichang era he became governor of Fenzhou and was promoted to Marquis.

sentences.zh: 從神武破紇豆陵於河西。

translations.literal: He followed Divine Wu in defeating Gedouling west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Divine Wu in defeating Gedouling west of the river.

sentences.zh: 沙苑之役，神武以地厄少卻，軍為西師所乘，遂亂。

translations.literal: At the Battle of Shazha, Divine Wu because the terrain was narrow retreated slightly; the army was exploited by the Western army and fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Shazha, Divine Wu withdrew slightly because the ground was cramped. The Western army seized the moment, and the formation broke apart.

sentences.zh: 張華原以簿帳曆營點兵，莫有應者。

translations.literal: Zhang Huayuan went through the roster and camp calling for troops; there were none who responded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huayuan went through the registers and called out through the camps for troops, but no one answered.

sentences.zh: 神武將集兵便戰，金曰：「眾散將離，其勢不可復用，宜急向河東。」

translations.literal: Divine Wu was about to gather troops and give battle at once; Jin said: "The masses are scattered and the generals are separating—the momentum cannot be reused. We should quickly turn toward Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Divine Wu was about to rally the men and fight at once. Jin said, "The troops are scattered and the generals are pulling away. This force cannot be used again. We must turn quickly toward Hedong.

sentences.zh: 神武據鞍未動，金以鞭拂馬，神武乃還。

translations.literal: Divine Wu held the saddle and did not move; Jin whipped his horse with a whip, and only then did Divine Wu return.
translations.idiomatic: Divine Wu sat in his saddle and did not move. Jin struck his horse with a whip, and only then did Divine Wu turn back.

sentences.zh: 於是大崩，喪甲士八萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon came the great rout; eighty thousand armored soldiers were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Then came the great collapse. Eighty thousand armored soldiers were lost.

sentences.zh: 侯景斂。

translations.literal: Hou Jing gathered them in.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing gathered in the dead.

sentences.zh: 西魏力人持大棒守河橋，衣甲厚，射之不入。

translations.literal: Western Wei strongmen held great clubs guarding the river bridge; their armor was thick and arrows could not pierce it.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei strongmen with great clubs guarded the river bridge. Their armor was so thick that arrows could not penetrate it.

sentences.zh: 賀拔仁候其轉面，射，一發斃之。

translations.literal: Heba Ren waited for one to turn his face, shot, and felled him with a single arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Ren waited until one of them turned his face, shot, and dropped him with a single arrow.

sentences.zh: 是役也，無金先請還，幾至危矣。

translations.literal: In this battle, had Jin not first urged retreat, they would nearly have been in peril.
translations.idiomatic: In that battle, had Jin not been the first to urge retreat, disaster would have been close at hand.

sentences.zh: 及高仲密西叛，周文攻洛陽，從神武破之。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhongmi defected west, Zhou Wen attacked Luoyang; he followed Divine Wu and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi defected to the west and Zhou Wen attacked Luoyang, Jin followed Divine Wu and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 還，除大司馬，改封石城郡公。

translations.literal: Upon return, he was appointed Grand Marshal; enfeoffed as Duke of Shicheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Grand Marshal and enfeoffed as Duke of Shicheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 金性質直，不識文字。

translations.literal: Jin's nature was straightforward and he did not know written characters.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was plain and direct by nature and could not read.

sentences.zh: 本名敦，苦其難署，改名為金，從其便易，猶以為難。

translations.literal: His original name was Dun; finding it hard to sign, he changed his name to Jin for convenience, yet still found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Dun. Because the character was hard to write when signing documents, he changed his name to Jin for convenience, yet even that he still found difficult.

sentences.zh: 司馬子如教為金字，作屋況之，其字乃就。

translations.literal: Sima Ziru taught him to write the character for jin, building a pavilion to practice it; only then did he manage the character.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ziru taught him to write the character jin, built a pavilion for him to practice in, and only then did he learn to form the character.

sentences.zh: 神武重其古質，每誡文襄曰：「爾所使多漢，有讒此人者，勿信之。」

translations.literal: Divine Wu valued his ancient simplicity and often admonished Wenxiang: "Those you employ are mostly Han Chinese; if any slander this man, do not believe them.
translations.idiomatic: Divine Wu prized his rough honesty and often warned Wenxiang, "Most of those you employ are Han Chinese. If anyone slanders this man, do not believe them.

sentences.zh: 及文襄嗣事，為肆州刺史。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang succeeded to affairs, he became governor of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxiang took over affairs of state, Jin became governor of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 文宣受禪，封咸陽郡王。

translations.literal: When Wenxuan received the abdication, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xianyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxuan accepted the abdication, Jin was enfeoffed as Prince of Xianyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 天保三年，就除太師。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianbao, he was appointed Grand Preceptor in situ.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianbao he was appointed Grand Preceptor while remaining in office.

sentences.zh: 四年，解州，乙太師還晉陽。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, relieved of the governorship, he returned to Jinyang as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was relieved of his provincial post and returned to Jinyang as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸其第，六宮及諸王盡從，置酒極夜方罷。

translations.literal: The emperor visited his residence; the six palaces and all the princes followed entirely; wine was set and only at the end of the night did they finish.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited his home. The six palaces and all the princes came with him. Wine was poured, and the feast did not end until deep into the night.

sentences.zh: 帝欣甚，詔金第二子豐樂為武衛大將軍，賜帛五千匹。

translations.literal: The emperor was exceedingly pleased; an edict made Jin's second son Fengle General of the Military Guard and granted five thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted. By edict he made Jin's second son Fengle General of the Military Guard and granted five thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「公元勳佐命，父子忠誠，朕當結以婚姻，永為籓衛。」

translations.literal: He said: "You, Duke, have meritoriously assisted our founding; father and sons are loyal. I shall bind you by marriage and forever make you a frontier bulwark.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "You, Duke, have served the founding of the dynasty with great merit, and your house is loyal through father and son. I shall bind our houses by marriage and make you a bulwark of the realm forever.

sentences.zh: 仍詔金孫武都尚義甯公主。

translations.literal: Still an edict ordered that Jin's grandson Wudu marry Princess Yining.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also arranged the marriage of Jin's grandson Wudu to Princess Yining.

sentences.zh: 成禮之日，帝從皇太后幸金宅，皇后、太子、諸王皆從。

translations.literal: On the day the rites were completed, the emperor accompanied the empress dowager to Jin's residence; the empress, crown prince, and all princes followed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the wedding rites were completed, the emperor came with the empress dowager to Jin's residence. The empress, crown prince, and all the princes followed.

sentences.zh: 其見待如此。

translations.literal: Such was the favor shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the honor in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 後蠕蠕為突厥破散，慮其犯塞，詔金屯兵白道以備之。

translations.literal: Later, when the Rouran were shattered and dispersed by the Turks, fearing they would raid the border, an edict ordered Jin to station troops on the White Road to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Rouran were broken and scattered by the Turks, the court feared they would raid the frontier. An edict ordered Jin to station troops on the White Road to guard against them.

sentences.zh: 多所俘獲，並表陳虜可取狀。

translations.literal: Many captives were taken; he repeatedly submitted memorials stating the situation for taking the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Many captives were taken, and he repeatedly memorialized the throne with reports on how the enemy might be seized.

sentences.zh: 文宣乃與金共討之。

translations.literal: Wenxuan then jointly campaigned against them with Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan then marched against them together with Jin.

sentences.zh: 進位右丞相，食齊州幹。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Chancellor, with income from Qi province revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Chancellor and granted income from the revenues of Qi province.

sentences.zh: 遷左丞相。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Left Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 帝晚年敗德，嘗持槊走馬以擬金胸者三，金立不動，於是賜物千段。

translations.literal: In his later years the emperor's virtue failed; he once galloped with spear levelled thrice at Jin's chest; Jin stood unmoved—thereupon granted a thousand rolls of goods.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the emperor's conduct deteriorated. Once he galloped up and thrice levelled his spear at Jin's chest. Jin did not stir. The emperor then granted him a thousand rolls of goods.

sentences.zh: 孝昭踐阼，納其孫女為皇太子妃。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhao took the throne, he took Jin's granddaughter as crown prince consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhao ascended the throne, he took Jin's granddaughter as crown prince consort.

sentences.zh: 詔金朝見，聽乘步挽車至階。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jin to attend court; he was permitted to ride a drawn carriage to the steps.
translations.idiomatic: By edict Jin was summoned to court and permitted to ride a hand-drawn carriage right to the steps.

sentences.zh: 武成即位，禮遇彌重，又納其孫女為太子妃。

translations.literal: When Wucheng acceded, honors were even heavier; again his granddaughter was taken as crown prince consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Wucheng came to the throne, the honors grew even greater, and again Jin's granddaughter was made crown prince consort.

sentences.zh: 金曾遣人獻食，中書舍人李若誤奏，雲金自來。

translations.literal: Jin once sent someone to present food; Secretariat Reviser Li Ruo mistakenly memorialized that Jin had come in person.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jin sent a man to present food. Secretariat Reviser Li Ruo mistakenly reported that Jin himself had come.

sentences.zh: 武成出昭陽殿，敕侍中高文遙將羊車引之。

translations.literal: Wucheng came out of Zhaoyang Hall and ordered Attendant-in-chief Gao Wenyao to take a sheep-drawn cart to fetch him.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng came out of Zhaoyang Hall and ordered Attendant-in-chief Gao Wenyao to bring a sheep-drawn cart to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 若知事誤，更不敢出映廊下。

translations.literal: When Ruo knew the matter was wrong, he dared not come out from beneath the corridor.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruo realized the mistake, he did not dare come out from beneath the corridor.

sentences.zh: 文遙還覆奏，帝罵若云：「空頭漢，合殺！」

translations.literal: Wenyao returned and reported again; the emperor cursed Ruo: "Empty-headed Han—ought to be killed!
translations.idiomatic: Wenyao returned and reported again. The emperor cursed Ruo, saying, "Empty-headed Han—you ought to be killed!

sentences.zh: 亦不加罪。

translations.literal: Yet he did not add punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet no punishment followed.

sentences.zh: 金長子光，大將軍。

translations.literal: Jin's eldest son Guang was a grand general.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's eldest son Guang was a grand general.

sentences.zh: 次子羨及孫武都，並開府儀同三司，出鎮方嶽。

translations.literal: Second son Xian and grandson Wudu were both Supervising General of the First Rank, defending frontier commands.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Xian and his grandson Wudu were both Supervising Generals of the First Rank, holding frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 其餘子孫，皆封侯貴達。

translations.literal: The rest of his sons and grandsons were all enfeoffed as marquises and attained high rank.
translations.idiomatic: The rest of his sons and grandsons were all enfeoffed as marquises and rose to high rank.

sentences.zh: 一門一皇后，二太子妃，三公主，尊寵當時莫比。

translations.literal: In one clan one empress, two crown prince consorts, three princesses—honor and favor unmatched in the age.
translations.idiomatic: One house produced one empress, two crown prince consorts, and three princesses. No family of the age knew such honor.

sentences.zh: 金嘗謂光曰：「我雖不讀書，聞古來外戚梁冀等，無不傾滅。

translations.literal: Jin once told Guang: "Though I do not read books, I have heard that in antiquity maternal kinsmen such as Liang Ji were without exception overthrown and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin once said to Guang, "I may not read books, but I have heard that in old times maternal kinsmen such as Liang Ji were invariably overthrown and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 女若有寵，諸貴人妒；

translations.literal: If your daughter has favor, the nobles are jealous;
translations.idiomatic: If your daughter wins favor, the great families grow jealous;

sentences.zh: 女若無寵，天子嫌之。

translations.literal: if your daughter has no favor, the Son of Heaven despises her.
translations.idiomatic: if she wins no favor, the Son of Heaven turns against her.

sentences.zh: 我家直以立勳抱忠致富貴，豈藉女也？」

translations.literal: Our house has become rich and noble purely by establishing merit and holding loyalty—why rely on daughters?
translations.idiomatic: Our house has grown rich and noble by merit and loyalty alone. Why should we depend on daughters?

sentences.zh: 辭不獲免，常以為憂。

translations.literal: Unable to refuse the appointments, he always took it as a worry.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to refuse the imperial matches, he always took them as a source of dread.

sentences.zh: 天統三年薨，年八十，贈假黃鉞、相國、太尉公，贈錢百萬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiantong he died, age eighty; posthumously granted ceremonial Yellow Ax, Grand Mentor of state, Duke of Grand Commandant; granted one million in money.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiantong he died at the age of eighty. Posthumously he was granted the Ceremonial Yellow Ax, the title Grand Mentor of State and Duke of Grand Commandant, and one million in cash.

sentences.zh: 諡曰武。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Martial.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Martial.

sentences.zh: 子光嗣。

translations.literal: Son Guang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 光字明月，馬面彪身，神爽雄傑，少言笑，工騎射。

translations.literal: Guang, styled Mingyue, had a horse-like face and tiger-like build, spirited and heroic, spoke little and laughed little, skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Guang, styled Mingyue, had a long face like a horse and a body like a tiger's. He was spirited and heroic, spoke little and laughed little, and was skilled in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 初為侯景部下，彭樂謂高敖曹曰：「斛律家小兒，不可三度將行，後奪人名。」

translations.literal: Initially under Hou Jing's command; Peng Yue said to Gao Aocao: "That boy of the Hulü family—do not let him lead troops three times; afterward he will steal men's reputations.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served under Hou Jing. Peng Yue said to Gao Aocao, "That boy of the Hulü house—do not let him lead troops three times. After that he will take credit that belongs to others.

sentences.zh: 以庫直事文襄。

translations.literal: He served as palace attendant under Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He served Wenxiang as a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 從出野，見雁雙飛來，文襄使光馳射之，以二矢俱落焉。

translations.literal: Once on an outing to the wilds, a pair of wild geese flew by; Wenxiang had Guang gallop and shoot; both fell with two arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Once on an outing to the wilds, a pair of geese flew past. Wenxiang had Guang gallop after them and shoot. Both birds fell to two arrows.

sentences.zh: 後從金西征，周文帝長史莫孝暉在行間，光年十七，馳馬射中之，因禽於陣。

translations.literal: Later, following Jin on the western campaign, Zhou Wendi's chief clerk Mo Xiaohui was in the ranks; Guang at seventeen galloped and shot him, capturing him in the formation.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on a western campaign with Jin, Zhou Wendi's chief clerk Mo Xiaohui was in the enemy ranks. Guang, seventeen years old, galloped forward, shot him, and took him captive on the field.

sentences.zh: 神武即擢授都督，封永樂子。

translations.literal: Divine Wu immediately promoted him to commander and enfeoffed him as Viscount of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: Divine Wu at once promoted him to commander and enfeoffed him as Viscount of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 雙嘗從文襄於洹橋校獵。

translations.literal: Shuang once followed Wenxiang on a hunting expedition at the Huan Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Guang once accompanied Wenxiang on a hunting expedition at the Huan Bridge.

sentences.zh: 雲表見一大鳥，射之正中其頸，形如車輪，旋轉而下，乃雕也。

translations.literal: In the clouds appeared a great bird; he shot it square in the neck; shaped like a carriage wheel, it spiraled down—it was an eagle.
translations.idiomatic: A great bird appeared above the clouds. He shot it square in the neck. Shaped like a carriage wheel, it spun down—it was an eagle.

sentences.zh: 丞相屬邢子高歎曰：「此射雕手也。」

translations.literal: Chancellery Aide Xing Zigao sighed: "This is an eagle-shooter.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellery Aide Xing Zigao sighed and said, "This is a true eagle-shooter.

sentences.zh: 當時號落雕都督。

translations.literal: At the time he was called the Eagle-Felling Commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the time men called him the Eagle-Felling Commander.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，別封西安縣子。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, he was separately enfeoffed as Viscount of Xi'an county.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, he was separately enfeoffed as Viscount of Xi'an county.

sentences.zh: 皇建元年，進爵钜鹿郡公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangjian, he was promoted to Duke of Julu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangjian he was promoted to Duke of Julu commandery.

sentences.zh: 時樂陵王百年為皇太子，求妃。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Leiling Wang Bainen was crown prince and sought a consort.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince of Leiling Wang Bainen was crown prince and sought a consort.

sentences.zh: 孝昭以光世載醇謹，納其長女為太子妃。

translations.literal: Xiaozhao, because the Guang family for generations had been pure and careful, took his eldest daughter as crown prince consort.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhao, considering the Guang family pure and careful through generations, took Guang's eldest daughter as crown prince consort.

sentences.zh: 歷位太子太保、尚書令、司空、司徒。

translations.literal: He held the posts in succession of Crown Prince Grand Tutor, Minister of the Department of State Affairs, Minister of Works, and Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Crown Prince Grand Tutor, Minister of the Department of State Affairs, Minister of Works, and Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 河清三年，周大司馬尉遲迥、齊公憲、庸公王雄等眾十萬攻洛陽。

translations.literal: In the third year of Heqing, Zhou Grand Marshal Yuchi Jiong, Duke of Qi Xian, Duke of Yong Wang Xiong, and others with a host of one hundred thousand attacked Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Heqing, Zhou Grand Marshal Yuchi Jiong, Duke of Qi Xian, Duke of Yong Wang Xiong, and others led a force of one hundred thousand against Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 光率騎五萬馳往，戰於芒山，迥等大敗。

translations.literal: Guang led fifty thousand cavalry in a rush to the scene and fought at Mangshan; Jiong and the others were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Guang led fifty thousand cavalry in haste to the scene and fought at Mangshan. Jiong and his allies were routed.

sentences.zh: 光親射雄殺之，迥、憲僅而獲免。

translations.literal: Guang personally shot and killed Xiong; Jiong and Xian barely escaped with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Guang himself shot Xiong dead. Jiong and Xian barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 仍築京觀。

translations.literal: He then built a victory mound.
translations.idiomatic: He then erected a victory mound from the enemy dead.

sentences.zh: 武成幸洛陽策勳，遷太尉。

translations.literal: Wucheng came to Luoyang to record merit and reward service; Guang was promoted to Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng came to Luoyang to record merit and distribute rewards. Guang was promoted to Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 初，文宣時，周人常懼齊兵之西度，恆以冬月，守河椎冰。

translations.literal: Initially, in Wenxuan's time, the Zhou people always feared Qi troops crossing west and constantly in winter months guarded the river by breaking ice.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Wenxuan's day, the Zhou people had always feared that Qi armies would cross westward and every winter broke the river ice to block them.

sentences.zh: 及帝即位，朝政漸紊，齊人椎冰，懼周兵之逼。

translations.literal: When the emperor acceded, court affairs gradually fell into disorder; the Qi people broke the ice, fearing Zhou troops pressing close.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor came to the throne, court affairs gradually fell into disorder. Now it was the Qi who broke the ice, fearing that Zhou armies would press in.

sentences.zh: 光憂曰：「國家常有吞關、隴之志，今日至此，而唯玩聲色！」

translations.literal: Guang said in worry: "The state has always harbored the ambition to swallow Guan and Long; today it has come to this, and yet we only indulge in music and women!
translations.idiomatic: Guang said in distress, "The state has always meant to swallow Guan and Long. Now matters have come to this, and all we do is indulge in music and women!

sentences.zh: 先是，武成納光第二女為太子妃，天統元年，拜皇后，光轉大將軍。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wucheng had taken Guang's second daughter as crown prince consort; in the first year of Tiantong she was made empress, and Guang was transferred to grand general.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wucheng had taken Guang's second daughter as crown prince consort. In the first year of Tiantong she became empress, and Guang was transferred to grand general.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，父喪去官。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year, on his father's death he left office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year, upon his father's death he left office.

sentences.zh: 其月，詔起光及弟羨，並復位。

translations.literal: That same month, an edict recalled Guang and his brother Xian, and both resumed their posts.
translations.idiomatic: That same month an edict recalled Guang and his brother Xian, and both returned to their posts.

sentences.zh: 秋，除太保，襲爵咸陽王，遷太傅。

translations.literal: In autumn he was appointed Grand Tutor, inherited the title Prince of Xianyang, and was transferred to Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn he was appointed Grand Tutor, inherited the title Prince of Xianyang, and was transferred to Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 十二月，周軍圍洛陽，壅絕糧道。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Zhou armies besieged Luoyang and cut off the grain route.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Zhou armies besieged Luoyang and severed the supply lines.

sentences.zh: 武平元年正月，詔光率步騎三萬禦之，鋒刃纏交，周將宇文桀眾大潰，直到宜陽。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Wuping, an edict ordered Guang to lead thirty thousand foot and horse to resist them; blades crossed in close combat, Zhou commander Yuwen Jie and his host were greatly routed, and they pressed on to Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Wuping, an edict ordered Guang to lead thirty thousand foot and horse against them. Blades locked in fierce combat, Zhou commander Yuwen Jie and his force were routed, and Guang pressed on to Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 軍還，擊周齊王憲等眾大潰。

translations.literal: When the army returned, it struck Duke of Qi Xian and the others and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march the army struck Duke of Qi Xian and his allies and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 詔加右丞相、并州刺史。

translations.literal: By edict he was given the additional post of Right Chancellor and governor of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he was additionally appointed Right Chancellor and governor of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，光又率步騎五萬於玉壁築華谷、龍門二城，與憲相持，憲不敢動。

translations.literal: That winter Guang again led fifty thousand foot and horse to build the two fortresses of Huagu and Longmen at Yubi, holding Xian at bay; Xian did not dare move.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Guang again led fifty thousand foot and horse to build the fortresses of Huagu and Longmen at Yubi and held Xian in check. Xian did not dare stir.

sentences.zh: 二年，率眾築平隴等鎮戍十三所。

translations.literal: In the second year he led the host to build thirteen garrison posts including Pinglong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he led his forces in building thirteen garrison posts, including Pinglong.

sentences.zh: 周柱國枹罕公普屯威、柱國韋孝寬等來逼平隴，光與戰于汾水，大破之。

translations.literal: Zhou Pillar of State Duke of Baohan Putun Wei, Pillar of State Wei Xiaokuan, and others pressed Pinglong; Guang fought them on the Fen River and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Pillar of State Duke of Baohan Putun Wei, Pillar of State Wei Xiaokuan, and others pressed Pinglong. Guang fought them on the Fen River and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 周遣其柱國紇幹廣略圍宜陽，光率步騎五萬赴之，戰於城下。

translations.literal: Zhou sent its Pillar of State Qigan Guanglue to besiege Yiyang; Guang led fifty thousand foot and horse to the relief and fought below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou sent its Pillar of State Qigan Guanglue to besiege Yiyang. Guang led fifty thousand foot and horse to the relief and fought below the walls.

sentences.zh: 取周建安等四戍，捕千餘人而還。

translations.literal: He took the four Zhou garrisons of Jian'an and the rest, captured more than a thousand men, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He took four Zhou garrisons including Jian'an, captured more than a thousand men, and returned.

sentences.zh: 軍未至鄴，敕令便放兵散。

translations.literal: Before the army reached Ye, an edict ordered the troops dismissed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army reached Ye, an edict ordered the troops dismissed immediately.

sentences.zh: 光以功勳者未得慰勞，若散，恩澤不施。

translations.literal: Guang said that those who had achieved merit had not yet received consolation and reward; if they were dismissed, favor would not be shown.
translations.idiomatic: Guang said that men who had won merit had not yet been rewarded. If the army were dismissed now, no grace would reach them.

sentences.zh: 乃密表，請使宣旨，軍仍且進。

translations.literal: He then submitted a secret memorial asking that an envoy be sent to proclaim the edict while the army continued to advance for the time being.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent a secret memorial asking that an envoy be dispatched to proclaim the imperial message while the army continued to advance for the moment.

sentences.zh: 朝廷發使遲留，軍還將至紫陌，光駐營待使。

translations.literal: The court's envoy was delayed; when the army was returning and nearing Zimo, Guang halted camp to await the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The court's envoy was slow in coming. As the army was returning and nearing Zimo, Guang halted camp to wait for him.

sentences.zh: 帝聞光軍營已逼，心甚惡之，急令舍人追光入見，然後宣勞散兵。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard that Guang's army camp was already pressing close, he was greatly displeased and urgently ordered a palace attendant to summon Guang to audience; only then did he proclaim rewards and dismiss the troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned that Guang's camp was already pressing close to the capital, he was deeply displeased. He urgently ordered a palace attendant to summon Guang to audience, and only then proclaimed rewards and dismissed the troops.

sentences.zh: 拜左丞相，別封清河郡公。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Chancellor and separately enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was appointed Left Chancellor and separately enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe commandery.

sentences.zh: 光嘗在朝堂，垂簾而坐。

translations.literal: Guang was once in the court hall, sitting behind the lowered curtain.
translations.idiomatic: Once Guang was in the court hall, seated behind the lowered curtain.

sentences.zh: 祖珽不知，乘馬過其前。

translations.literal: Zu Ting did not know and rode past before him.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ting did not know and rode past in front of him.

sentences.zh: 光怒，謂人曰：「此人乃敢爾！」

translations.literal: Guang was angry and said to others: "This man actually dares to behave like this!"
translations.idiomatic: Guang was furious and said to others, "This man actually dares to behave like this!

sentences.zh: 後珽在內省，言聲高慢，光過聞之，又怒。

translations.literal: Later Ting was in the inner secretariat, speaking in a loud and insolent voice; Guang passed by, heard it, and was angry again.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Ting was in the inner secretariat speaking in a loud and insolent voice, Guang passed by, heard him, and grew angry again.

sentences.zh: 珽知光忿，賂其從奴搕頭。

translations.literal: Ting knew Guang was angry and bribed his attendant Yaotou.
translations.idiomatic: Ting knew Guang was enraged and bribed his attendant Yaotou.

sentences.zh: 曰：「自公用事，相王每夜抱膝歎曰：'盲人用權，國必破矣」珽省事褚士達夢人倚戶授其詩曰：「九升八合粟，角鬥定非真，堰卻津中水，將留何處人。」

translations.literal: He said: "Since you took power, the Prince every night sighs holding his knees and says, 'A blind man wielding power—the state will surely fall.'" Zu Ting's secretariat clerk Chu Shida dreamed of a man leaning on the door giving him a poem: "Nine sheng eight he of grain, horn and dou surely not true, dam the water in the ford, what person will remain."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Since you took power, the Prince every night sits with his knees drawn up and sighs, 'A blind man wielding power—the state will surely fall.'" Zu Ting's secretariat clerk Chu Shida dreamed of a man leaning against the door and giving him a poem: "Nine sheng eight he of grain, horn and dou surely not true, dam the water in the ford, what person will remain."

sentences.zh: 以告珽。

translations.literal: He reported it to Ting.
translations.idiomatic: He reported the dream to Ting.

sentences.zh: 珽占之曰：「角鬥，斛字；

translations.literal: Ting divined it and said: "'Horn and dou' is the character hu;
translations.idiomatic: Ting interpreted it and said, "'Horn and dou' forms the character hu;

sentences.zh: 津卻水，何留人，合成律字；

translations.literal: 'dam the ford's water, what person will remain' together forms the character lü;
translations.idiomatic: dam the ford's water, what person will remain' together forms the character lü;

sentences.zh: 非真者，解斛律於我不實。」

translations.literal: not true' means to remove Hulü, who is not genuine toward me.
translations.idiomatic: not true' means to remove Hulü, who is false toward me.

sentences.zh: 士達又言所夢狀，乃其父形也。

translations.literal: Shida again spoke of the form in the dream—it was the shape of his father.
translations.idiomatic: Shida also said that the figure in the dream had taken the form of his father.

sentences.zh: 珽由是懼。

translations.literal: Ting therefore grew afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Ting was therefore afraid.

sentences.zh: 又穆提婆求娶光庶女，不許。

translations.literal: Again Mutipo asked to marry Guang's concubine-born daughter; he did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Mutipo also asked to marry Guang's daughter by a concubine, and Guang refused.

sentences.zh: 帝賜提婆晉陽之田，光言於朝曰：「此田，神武以來，常種禾飼馬，以擬寇難。

translations.literal: The emperor granted Mutipo fields at Jinyang; Guang said at court: "These fields, since Divine Wu's time, have always been sown with grain to feed horses, in preparation for enemy trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted Mutipo fields at Jinyang. Guang said at court, "Since Divine Wu's day these fields have always been sown with grain to feed horses against enemy raids.

sentences.zh: 今賜，無乃闕軍務也？」

translations.literal: Now to grant them—will this not leave military affairs short?
translations.idiomatic: To grant them now—will that not cripple military readiness?

sentences.zh: 帝又以鄴清風園賜提婆租賃之。

translations.literal: The emperor also granted Mutipo the rental income of Qingfeng Garden in Ye.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also granted Mutipo the rental income of Qingfeng Garden in Ye.

sentences.zh: 於是官無菜，賒買於人，負錢三百萬，其人訴焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the government had no vegetables and bought on credit from others; it owed three million in cash, and the creditor sued.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the government had no vegetables and bought on credit from private suppliers. It owed three million in cash, and the creditor brought suit.

sentences.zh: 光曰：「此菜園賜提婆，是一家足；

translations.literal: Guang said: "This vegetable garden granted to Mutipo suffices for one household;
translations.idiomatic: Guang said, "This vegetable garden granted to Mutipo is enough for one household;

sentences.zh: 若不賜提婆，便百官足」。

translations.literal: if not granted to Mutipo, then all the officials would have enough."
translations.idiomatic: if it were not granted to Mutipo, all the officials would have enough."

sentences.zh: 由是祖、穆積怨。

translations.literal: Because of this Zu and Mu accumulated resentment.
translations.idiomatic: From this Zu and Mu nursed deep grievances against him.

sentences.zh: 周將韋孝寬懼光，乃作謠言，令間諜漏之于鄴曰：「百斗飛上天，明月照長安。」

translations.literal: Zhou commander Wei Xiaokuan feared Guang and therefore composed a song and had spies leak it in Ye, saying: "A hundred dou fly up to heaven; Bright Moon shines on Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou commander Wei Xiaokuan feared Guang. He composed a song and had spies leak it in Ye: "A hundred dou fly up to heaven; Bright Moon shines on Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「高山不推自崩，槲樹不扶自豎。」

translations.literal: Again: "A high mountain collapses without being pushed; an oak tree stands upright without being braced."
translations.idiomatic: And again: "A high mountain collapses without being pushed; an oak tree stands upright without being braced."

sentences.zh: 珽讀之曰：「盲老公背上下大斧，饒舌老母不得語。」

translations.literal: Ting read it and said: "The blind old man carries a great axe on his back; the glib old woman may not speak."
translations.idiomatic: Ting read it and said, "The blind old man carries a great axe on his back; the glib old woman may not speak."

sentences.zh: 令小兒歌之于路。

translations.literal: He had little children sing it in the streets.
translations.idiomatic: He had small children sing it in the streets.

sentences.zh: 提婆聞，以告其母。

translations.literal: Mutipo heard it and told his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Mutipo heard it and told his mother.

sentences.zh: 令萱以饒舌為斥己，盲老公謂祖珽也，遂協謀，以謠言啟帝曰：「斛律累世大將，明月聲震關西，豐樂威行突厥，女為皇后，男尚公主，謠言可畏」帝以問韓長鸞。

translations.literal: Lingxuan took "glib tongue" as a rebuke of herself; "blind old man" referred to Zu Ting. They therefore conspired and reported the song to the emperor, saying: "The Hulü for generations have been great generals. Mingyue's fame shakes the passes west; Fengle's authority extends among the Turks. His daughter is empress; his sons marry princesses. The song is to be feared." The emperor asked Han Changluan.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxuan took "glib tongue" as an attack on herself and "blind old man" as a reference to Zu Ting. They therefore plotted together and reported the song to the emperor, saying, "The Hulü for generations have been great generals. Mingyue's fame shakes the western passes; Fengle's authority extends among the Turks. His daughter is empress; his sons marry princesses. The song is terrifying." The emperor asked Han Changluan.

sentences.zh: 鸞以為不可，事寢。

translations.literal: Changluan said it could not be; the matter rested.
translations.idiomatic: Changluan said it could not be so, and the matter rested.

sentences.zh: 光又嘗謂人曰：「今軍人皆無褌袴，後宮內參，一賜數萬匹，府藏稍空，此是何理？」

translations.literal: Guang also once said to others: "Today the soldiers all lack trousers; the inner attendants of the rear palaces, one grant gives them tens of thousands of bolts—the treasury is gradually emptied. What kind of principle is this?
translations.idiomatic: Guang also once said to others, "Today the soldiers lack even trousers, while inner attendants of the rear palaces receive tens of thousands of bolts in a single grant. The treasury is being drained. What principle is this?

sentences.zh: 受賜者聞之，皆曰：「天子自賜我，關相王何事？」

translations.literal: Those who received grants heard it and all said: "The Son of Heaven granted it to us himself—what business is it of the Prince?"
translations.idiomatic: Those who had received grants heard this and all said, "The Son of Heaven granted it to us himself—what business is it of the Prince?"

sentences.zh: 珽又通啟求見，帝使以庫車載入，珽因請間，唯何洪珍在側。

translations.literal: Ting again submitted a memorial requesting audience; the emperor had him brought in on a treasury cart; Ting therefore requested a private meeting—only He Hongzhen was at the side.
translations.idiomatic: Ting again submitted a memorial requesting audience. The emperor had him brought in on a treasury cart. Ting then asked for a private meeting. Only He Hongzhen was present.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「前得公啟，即欲施行，長鸞以為無此理，未可。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Earlier I received your memorial and intended to carry it out; Changluan said there was no such principle and it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When I received your earlier memorial I meant to act on it, but Changluan said there was no such principle and it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 珽未對。

translations.literal: Ting did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Ting did not answer.

sentences.zh: 洪珍進曰：「若本無意，則可；

translations.literal: Hongzhen stepped forward and said: "If there had been no such intent, that would be one thing;
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhen stepped forward and said, "If there had never been such intent, that would be one thing;

sentences.zh: 既有此意，不決行，萬一事泄，如何！」

translations.literal: but since there has been such intent, if you do not decide and act, should the matter leak out, what then!
translations.idiomatic: but since there has been such intent, if you do not decide and act, and the matter leaks out, what then!

sentences.zh: 帝然洪珍言，而猶預未決。

translations.literal: The emperor approved Hongzhen's words, yet still hesitated and had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed with Hongzhen, yet still hesitated and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 珽令武都妾兄顏玄，告光謀為不軌；

translations.literal: Ting had Wudu's concubine-born elder brother Yan Xuan report that Guang was plotting rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: Ting had Wudu's concubine-born elder brother Yan Xuan accuse Guang of plotting rebellion;

sentences.zh: 又令曹魏祖奏，言上將星盛，不誅，恐有災禍。

translations.literal: he also had Cao Weizu memorialize, saying the general's star was flourishing; if Guang were not executed, he feared disaster.
translations.idiomatic: he also had Cao Weizu submit a memorial saying the general's star was blazing bright; if Guang were not executed, he feared calamity would follow.

sentences.zh: 先是天狗西流，占曰秦地。

translations.literal: Earlier the celestial dog had flowed west; divination said it pointed to the Qin region.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the celestial dog had moved westward. Divination said it pointed to the Qin region.

sentences.zh: 案秦即咸陽也。

translations.literal: Investigation showed that Qin meant Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation showed that Qin meant Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 自太廟及光宅，並見血。

translations.literal: From the imperial temple and Guang's residence, blood was seen.
translations.idiomatic: Blood appeared both at the imperial temple and at Guang's residence.

sentences.zh: 先是三日，鼠常晝見光寢室，常投食與之，一朝三鼠俱死。

translations.literal: Three days earlier, rats had often been seen in daylight in Guang's bedchamber; he regularly threw food to them, and one morning all three rats died together.
translations.idiomatic: Three days earlier rats had often been seen in daylight in Guang's bedchamber. He regularly threw food to them, and one morning all three died at once.

sentences.zh: 又床下有二物如黑豬，從地出走，其穴膩滑。

translations.literal: Again beneath the bed were two things like black pigs that ran out from the ground; their burrow was greasy and slick.
translations.idiomatic: Again, beneath the bed were two creatures like black pigs that burst out of the ground. Their burrow was greasy and slick.

sentences.zh: 大蛇屢見。

translations.literal: Great serpents were repeatedly seen.
translations.idiomatic: Great serpents were seen again and again.

sentences.zh: 屋脊有聲，如彈丸落。

translations.literal: On the roof ridge there were sounds like falling pellets.
translations.idiomatic: On the roof ridge came sounds like pellets falling.

sentences.zh: 又大門橫木自焚。

translations.literal: Again the horizontal beam of the great gate burned by itself.
translations.idiomatic: Again the crossbeam of the great gate burst into flame by itself.

sentences.zh: 擣衣石自移。

translations.literal: The clothes-beating stone moved by itself.
translations.idiomatic: The stone used for beating clothes moved by itself.

sentences.zh: 既而丞相府佐封士讓密啟云：「光前西討還，敕令便放兵散，光令軍逼帝京，將為不軌，不果而止。

translations.literal: Before long, Chancellor's Office aide Feng Shirang submitted a secret memorial saying: "When Guang earlier returned from the western campaign, an edict ordered the troops dismissed at once. Guang made the army press close to the imperial capital, intending rebellion; he stopped only because he did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Chancellor's Office aide Feng Shirang submitted a secret memorial saying, "When Guang earlier returned from the western campaign, an edict ordered the troops dismissed at once. Guang made the army press toward the capital, intending rebellion, and stopped only because he failed.

sentences.zh: 家藏弩甲，奴僮千數，每使豐樂、武都處，陰謀往來。

translations.literal: In the house were stored crossbows and armor; slaves and retainers numbered in the thousands. He often sent Fengle and Wudu back and forth in secret plotting.
translations.idiomatic: Crossbows and armor were stored in the house, and slaves and retainers numbered in the thousands. He often sent Fengle and Wudu back and forth in secret plotting.

sentences.zh: 若不早圖，恐事不可測。」

translations.literal: If he is not dealt with early, I fear the outcome cannot be foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: If he is not dealt with soon, I fear the outcome cannot be foreseen.

sentences.zh: 帝謂何洪珍曰：「人心亦大聖，我前疑其欲反，果然。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to He Hongzhen: "Human hearts are also great sages. I earlier suspected he meant to rebel, and indeed it is so."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to He Hongzhen, "Human hearts are great sages too. I earlier suspected he meant to rebel, and indeed it is so."

sentences.zh: 帝性怯，恐即有變，令洪珍馳召祖珽告之。

translations.literal: The emperor was timid by nature and feared there would be sudden change; he ordered Hongzhen to gallop and summon Zu Ting to tell him.
translations.idiomatic: Timid by nature, the emperor feared sudden upheaval and ordered Hongzhen to gallop off and summon Zu Ting to tell him.

sentences.zh: 又恐追光不從命。

translations.literal: Again he feared that if Guang were summoned he would not obey the order.
translations.idiomatic: He also feared that if Guang were summoned he would refuse to obey.

sentences.zh: 珽因請賜其一駿馬，令明日乘至東山遊觀，須其來謝，因執之。

translations.literal: Ting therefore requested that one fine horse be granted him, so that the next day he would ride to Dongshan for an outing; when Guang came to give thanks, they would seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Ting therefore asked that a fine horse be granted Guang, so that the next day he would ride to Dongshan on an outing. When Guang came to give thanks, they would seize him.

sentences.zh: 帝如其言。

translations.literal: The emperor did as he said.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did as he proposed.

sentences.zh: 光將上馬，頭眩。

translations.literal: When Guang was about to mount his horse, he grew dizzy.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Guang was about to mount his horse, his head swam.

sentences.zh: 及至，引入涼風堂，劉桃枝自後撲 之，不倒。

translations.literal: When he arrived, they led him into the Cool Breeze Hall. Liu Taozhi struck him from behind, but he did not fall.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, they ushered him into the Cool Breeze Hall. Liu Taozhi struck him from behind, yet he did not fall.

sentences.zh: 光曰：「桃枝常作如此事，我不負國家。」

translations.literal: Guang said, "Taozhi often does such things. I have not failed the state."
translations.idiomatic: Guang said, "Taozhi often does such things. I have not betrayed the state.

sentences.zh: 桃枝與力士三人，以弓弦肙其頸，遂拉殺之，年五十八。

translations.literal: Taozhi and three strongmen wrapped a bowstring around his neck and pulled until they killed him. He was fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Taozhi and three strongmen looped a bowstring around his neck and strangled him to death. He was fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 血流於地，剗之跡終不滅。

translations.literal: Blood flowed on the ground; no matter how it was scraped away, the marks never disappeared.
translations.idiomatic: Blood pooled on the floor, and no matter how it was scraped clean, the stains never vanished.

sentences.zh: 於是下詔稱其反，族滅之。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued declaring him a rebel, and his clan was annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued declaring him a rebel, and his entire clan was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 使二千石郎邢祖信掌簿籍其家。

translations.literal: Xing Zuxin, a gentleman of the Two-Thousand-Bushel rank, was assigned to take inventory of his household registers.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Zuxin, a gentleman of the Two-Thousand-Bushel rank, was ordered to inventory the family's property and records.

sentences.zh: 珽於都省問所得物，祖信曰：「得弓十五張，宴射箭一百，貝刀七口，賜槊二張。」

translations.literal: At the ministry headquarters Zu Ting asked what had been confiscated. Zuxin said, "Fifteen bows, one hundred banquet arrows, seven shell knives, and two granted spears were found."
translations.idiomatic: At the ministry headquarters Zu Ting asked what had been seized. Zuxin replied, "Fifteen bows, one hundred banquet arrows, seven shell knives, and two imperial spears.

sentences.zh: 珽又厲聲曰：「更得何物？」

translations.literal: Zu Ting again said in a sharp voice, "What else was found?"
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ting demanded again in a harsh voice, "What else did you find?

sentences.zh: 曰：「得棗子枝二十束，擬奴僕與人鬥者，不問曲直，即以杖之一百。」

translations.literal: He said, "Twenty bundles of jujube switches were found. They were intended for when slaves and servants fought with others—without asking right or wrong, they were to be beaten a hundred strokes with them."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Twenty bundles of jujube switches. They were meant for when slaves and servants brawled with others: without inquiring who was right or wrong, Guang would have them beaten a hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 珽大慚，乃下聲曰：「朝廷已加重刑，郎中何可分雪？」

translations.literal: Zu Ting was greatly shamed and lowered his voice: "The court has already imposed heavy punishment—how could a gentleman make excuses for him?"
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ting was deeply shamed and softened his tone: "The court has already inflicted severe punishment—how could a gentleman speak in his defense?

sentences.zh: 及出，人尤其抗直。

translations.literal: When he left, people especially praised his bold integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When he left, everyone praised his fearless honesty.

sentences.zh: 祖信慨然曰：「好宰相尚死，我何惜餘生！」

translations.literal: Zuxin said with emotion, "Even a good chancellor still died—why should I spare the rest of my life!"
translations.idiomatic: Zuxin said with feeling, "Even a fine chancellor was put to death—why should I cling to what life remains?

sentences.zh: 祖信少年時，父遜為李庶所卿，因詣庶，謂庶曰：「暫來見卿，還辭卿去。」

translations.literal: When Zuxin was young, his father Xun had been respected by Li Shu, so he went to call on Li Shu and said to him, "I have come for a brief visit to see you and will take my leave when I go."
translations.idiomatic: When Zuxin was young, his father Xun had been favored by Li Shu, so he went to visit Li Shu and said, "I have come only for a brief call and will take my leave when I go.

sentences.zh: 庶父諧杖庶而謝焉。

translations.literal: Li Shu's father Xie beat Li Shu with a staff and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shu's father Xie thrashed Li Shu with a staff and offered an apology.

sentences.zh: 光居家嚴肅，見子弟若君臣。

translations.literal: In his household Guang was grave and austere; he treated sons and younger kinsmen as if they were sovereign and subject.
translations.idiomatic: At home Guang was stern and solemn, treating sons and younger kinsmen with the formality of sovereign and subject.

sentences.zh: 雖極貴盛，性節儉，簡聲色，不營財利，杜絕饋餉。

translations.literal: Though he reached the utmost rank and glory, by nature he was frugal. He kept music and women at a distance, did not pursue wealth, and cut off all gift-giving.
translations.idiomatic: Though he rose to the highest rank and splendor, he was frugal by nature, kept music and women at arm's length, sought no profit, and refused all gifts.

sentences.zh: 門無賓客，罕與朝士交言，不肯預政事。

translations.literal: No guests came to his gate; he rarely exchanged words with court officials and refused to take part in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: No guests passed his gate; he seldom spoke with court officials and would not involve himself in politics.

sentences.zh: 每會議，常獨後言，言輒合理。

translations.literal: Whenever councils met, he usually spoke last, and what he said was always reasonable.
translations.idiomatic: In every council he usually spoke last, and his words were always sound.

sentences.zh: 將有表疏，令人執筆，口占之，務從省實。

translations.literal: When he was to have a memorial or formal submission, he had someone hold the brush while he dictated, always striving for brevity and fact.
translations.idiomatic: When a memorial or report was needed, he had someone hold the brush while he dictated, always aiming for brevity and plain truth.

sentences.zh: 行兵用匈奴卜法，吉凶無不中。

translations.literal: When campaigning he used Xiongnu divination methods; good and ill fortune were never misjudged.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign he used Xiongnu divination, and his readings of fortune and misfortune never missed.

sentences.zh: 軍營未定，終不入幕，或竟日不坐。

translations.literal: If the camp was not yet settled, he would never enter his tent; sometimes he would not sit down all day.
translations.idiomatic: If the camp was not yet in order, he would not enter his tent; sometimes he went the whole day without sitting.

sentences.zh: 身不脫介胄，常為士卒先。

translations.literal: He never removed his armor and was always ahead of the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He never doffed his armor and always marched at the head of his men.
