sentences.zh: 有罪者，唯大杖撾背，未嘗妄殺。

translations.literal: Those who were guilty received only heavy staff blows on the back; he never killed recklessly.
translations.idiomatic: Offenders received only heavy blows on the back with a staff; he never killed without cause.

sentences.zh: 眾皆爭為之死。

translations.literal: All vied to die for him.
translations.idiomatic: Every man under him would have died for him.

sentences.zh: 宜陽之役，謂周人曰：「歸我七年人，不然取爾十倍。」

translations.literal: At the battle of Yiyang he told the Zhou men, "Return my men of seven years' standing, or I shall take ten times as many of yours."
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Yiyang he told the Zhou forces, "Return the men I have held for seven years, or I will take ten times as many of yours.

sentences.zh: 周人即歸之。

translations.literal: The Zhou men returned them at once.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou men returned them immediately.

sentences.zh: 在西境築定誇諸城，馬上以鞭指畫，所取地皆如其言，拓地五百里而未嘗伐功。

translations.literal: On the western frontier he built cities at Ding, Kua, and elsewhere. From horseback he traced boundaries with his whip; the land taken was always as he said. He extended the territory five hundred li yet never claimed credit for the achievement.
translations.idiomatic: On the western frontier he built the cities of Ding, Kua, and others. From horseback he traced boundaries with his whip, and the land seized matched his word. He expanded the realm by five hundred li yet never boasted of the feat.

sentences.zh: 板築之役，鞭撻人士，頗稱其嚴。

translations.literal: In corvée labor for rammed-earth walls, he beat officials and commoners with whips; many praised his severity.
translations.idiomatic: During corvée work on rammed-earth walls he flogged officials and commoners alike, and many spoke of his strictness.

sentences.zh: 自結髮從戎，未嘗失律，深為鄰敵懾憚。

translations.literal: From the time he first bound his hair and took up arms, he never failed in discipline, and neighboring enemies deeply feared him.
translations.idiomatic: From the day he first bound his hair and entered the army, he never broke discipline, and neighboring foes feared him deeply.

sentences.zh: 罪既不彰，一旦屠滅，朝野惜之。

translations.literal: Since his guilt was never clearly shown, when he was slaughtered in a single day, court and countryside alike mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: His guilt had never been made clear, yet he was butchered in a single day; court and countryside alike grieved for him.

sentences.zh: 周武帝聞光死，赦其境內。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou heard that Guang was dead, he granted an amnesty within his realm.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou learned of Guang's death, he proclaimed an amnesty throughout his realm.

sentences.zh: 後入鄴，追贈上柱國、崇國公。

translations.literal: Later, when he entered Ye, he posthumously enfeoffed Guang as Supreme Pillar of State and Duke of Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Later, upon entering Ye, he posthumously enfeoffed Guang as Supreme Pillar of State and Duke of Chong.

sentences.zh: 指詔書曰：「此人若在，朕豈得至鄴？」

translations.literal: Pointing at the edict, he said, "If this man had still been alive, how could I have reached Ye?"
translations.idiomatic: Pointing at the edict, he said, "If this man had still lived, how could I ever have taken Ye?"

sentences.zh: 長子武都，位特進、開府儀同三司、梁、袞二州刺史，所在唯事聚斂。

translations.literal: His eldest son Wudu held the posts of Supereminent Grandee, General of the Palace Gate with Equipage Equal to the Three Ministers, and Inspector of the Liang and Yan provinces; wherever he served he did nothing but amass wealth.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Wudu held the ranks of Supereminent Grandee, General of the Palace Gate with Equipage Equal to the Three Ministers, and Inspector of Liang and Yan provinces; wherever he was posted he did nothing but hoard wealth.

sentences.zh: 光死，遣使於州斬之。

translations.literal: When Guang died, an envoy was sent to the province to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: After Guang's death, an envoy was dispatched to the province to behead him.

sentences.zh: 小子鐘，年甫數歲，獲免。

translations.literal: The youngest son Zhong, only a few years old, was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest son Zhong, only a few years old, was spared.

sentences.zh: 周朝襲封崇國公。

translations.literal: Under the Zhou dynasty he inherited the enfeoffment as Duke of Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou dynasty he inherited the title of Duke of Chong.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，卒于車騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he died while serving as General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang era of Sui he died in office as General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 羨曆事數帝，以謹直稱，雖極榮寵，不自矜尚。

translations.literal: Xian served several emperors in succession and was known for prudent integrity. Though he received the highest honors, he did not pride himself on them.
translations.idiomatic: Xian served several emperors in turn and was known for cautious honesty. Though he enjoyed the greatest honors, he never prided himself on them.

sentences.zh: 以合門貴盛，深以為憂。

translations.literal: Because the whole household was noble and powerful, he was deeply troubled.
translations.idiomatic: The entire family's rank and power weighed on him, and he was deeply anxious.

sentences.zh: 武平元年，乃上書推讓，乞解所職。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wuping he submitted a memorial resigning and requesting to be relieved of his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wuping he submitted a memorial yielding his honors and asking to be relieved of office.

sentences.zh: 詔不許。

translations.literal: An edict refused permission.
translations.idiomatic: An edict denied his request.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，進爵荊山郡王。

translations.literal: That autumn he was advanced in rank to Prince of Jingshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was promoted to Prince of Jingshan commandery.

sentences.zh: 羨慮禍，使人騎快騾迎至鄴，無日不得音問。

translations.literal: Xian, fearing disaster, sent men on fast mules daily to Ye for reports; not a day passed without word arriving.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing calamity, Xian sent riders on swift mules to Ye every day for news; not a single day passed without a report.

sentences.zh: 後二日鄴使不至，家人乞養憂之。

translations.literal: Two days later no messenger from Ye arrived, and his family and dependents grew anxious.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later no courier from Ye came, and his family and household dependents were filled with dread.

sentences.zh: 又夢著枷鎖，勸豐樂速奔突厥，羨不從。

translations.literal: He also dreamed he wore cangue and fetters. Someone urged Fengle to flee quickly to the Turks, but Xian would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: He also dreamed that he wore cangue and fetters. Someone urged Fengle to flee at once to the Turks, but Xian refused.

sentences.zh: 占其夢曰：「枷者加官，鎖者鎖鎖吉利。」

translations.literal: One who interpreted the dream said, "The cangue means added rank; the fetters mean 'locks'—'locks' is auspicious."
translations.idiomatic: One who read the dream said, "The cangue means added rank; the fetters mean 'locks'—and 'locks' is lucky.

sentences.zh: 及光誅，敕中領軍賀拔伏恩等十餘人馳驛捕之，遣領軍大將軍鮮于桃枝、洛州行台僕射獨孤永業便發定州騎卒續進。

translations.literal: When Guang was executed, an edict ordered more than ten men including Central Army Commander Helaba Fu'en to ride post-horses in pursuit and arrest him; the Border Array Grand General Xianyu Taozhi and Luozhou Executive Commander Dugu Yongye were dispatched at once to send cavalry from Dingzhou to follow up.
translations.idiomatic: When Guang was executed, an edict ordered Helaba Fu'en and more than ten others, as Central Army Commander, to ride post relays in pursuit and seize him; Border Array Grand General Xianyu Taozhi and Luozhou Executive Commander Dugu Yongye were sent at once to mobilize cavalry from Dingzhou in support.

sentences.zh: 伏恩等既至，門者白羨曰：「使人衷甲馬汗，宜閉城門。」

translations.literal: When Fu'en and the others arrived, the gatekeeper reported to Xian, "The envoys wear armor under their robes and their horses are sweated—you should shut the city gates."
translations.idiomatic: When Fu'en and his party arrived, the gatekeeper reported to Xian, "The envoys are armored beneath their robes and their horses are lathered—you should close the city gates.

sentences.zh: 羨曰：「敕使豈可疑拒！」

translations.literal: Xian said, "How could one suspect and refuse an imperial envoy!"
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "How could I suspect and turn away an imperial envoy!

sentences.zh: 出迎之，遂見執，死于長史査事。

translations.literal: He went out to meet them and was then seized, dying in the Chief Clerk's investigation office.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to receive them and was seized on the spot, dying in the Chief Clerk's custody while the case was being handled.

sentences.zh: 謂其妻曰：「啟太后，臣兄弟死自當知。」

translations.literal: He said to his wife, "Inform the Empress Dowager: we brothers know we must die when the time comes."
translations.idiomatic: He told his wife, "Report to the Empress Dowager: as brothers, we know we must die when our time comes.

sentences.zh: 臨刑歎曰：「富貴如此，女為皇后，公主滿家，常使三百兵，何得不敗？」

translations.literal: Facing execution he sighed and said, "With wealth and glory like this—a daughter as empress, princesses filling the house, always commanding three hundred soldiers—how could we not be destroyed?"
translations.idiomatic: At the moment of execution he sighed and said, "With fortune like this—a daughter as empress, princesses throughout the house, three hundred soldiers always at our call—how could we not be ruined?

sentences.zh: 並害五子，年十五已下者宥之。

translations.literal: Five sons were killed along with him; those fifteen and under were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Five sons were killed with him; those fifteen and younger were spared.

sentences.zh: 羨未誅前，忽令其在州諸子五六人，鎖頸乘驢出城，闔家泣送之至閣，日晚而歸。

translations.literal: Before Xian was executed, he suddenly had five or six of his sons at the prefecture led out of the city with locked necks, riding donkeys. The whole family wept as they escorted them to the gate, then returned in the evening.
translations.idiomatic: Before Xian was executed, he suddenly had five or six sons then at the prefecture led out of the city with iron collars, mounted on donkeys. The whole family wept as they escorted them to the yamen gate and returned only at nightfall.

sentences.zh: 吏人莫不驚異。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners were all astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners alike were stunned.

sentences.zh: 行燕郡守馬嗣明，道術之士也，為羨所欽，竊問之，答云：「須有衤襄厭。」

translations.literal: Ma Siming, Administrator of Xingyan commandery, was a practitioner of occult arts whom Xian admired; Xian questioned him in private, and he answered, "There must be a ritual of exorcism to avert ill fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Siming, Administrator of Xingyan commandery, was a practitioner of occult arts whom Xian admired; Xian questioned him in private, and he answered, "There must be a ritual of exorcism to avert ill fortune.

sentences.zh: 數日而有此變。

translations.literal: Within days this disaster came to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Within days the calamity arrived.

sentences.zh: 羨及光並工騎射。

translations.literal: Xian and Guang were both skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Xian and Guang were both masters of mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 少時獵，父金命子孫會射而觀之，泣曰：「明月、豐樂用弓不及我，諸孫又不及明月、豐樂，世衰矣。」

translations.literal: When they were young and hunting, their father Jin summoned the descendants to an archery contest and watched. Weeping, he said, "Mingyue and Fengle cannot handle the bow as well as I; the grandchildren are again inferior to Mingyue and Fengle—the age is in decline."
translations.idiomatic: When they were young and out hunting, their father Jin gathered the descendants for an archery contest and watched. In tears he said, "Mingyue and Fengle cannot draw the bow as well as I, and the grandchildren fall short of Mingyue and Fengle—the line is fading.

sentences.zh: 每日令出田，還即效所獲。

translations.literal: Every day he had them go out to the fields; on return they would show what they had taken.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he sent them into the field, and on return they had to display what they had taken.

sentences.zh: 光獲少，必麗龜達腋；

translations.literal: When Guang took little, he always pierced the turtle shell and reached the armpit;
translations.idiomatic: When Guang's bag was light, every shot pierced the turtle mark and drove the arrow to the armpit;

sentences.zh: 羨獲雖多，非要害之所。

translations.literal: though Xian took much, it was never at a vital spot.
translations.idiomatic: though Xian's bag was heavy, none of his shots struck a vital spot.

sentences.zh: 光恆蒙賞，羨或被捶。

translations.literal: Guang always received reward; Xian sometimes was beaten.
translations.idiomatic: Guang always won praise; Xian was sometimes thrashed.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，云：「明月必背上著箭，豐樂隨處即下手，數雖多，去兄遠矣。」

translations.literal: When people asked the reason, Jin said, "Mingyue always plants his arrow in the back; Fengle strikes wherever he can. Though the count is high, he is far behind his elder brother."
translations.idiomatic: When people asked why, Jin said, "Mingyue always drives his arrow into the back; Fengle shoots wherever he can. However high the count, he is far behind his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 聞者服其言。

translations.literal: Those who heard accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard it accepted his judgment.

sentences.zh: 金兄平，少便弓馬。

translations.literal: Jin's older brother Ping was skilled with bow and horse from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's elder brother Ping was adept with bow and horse from boyhood.

sentences.zh: 神武起，以都督從。

translations.literal: When Divine Martial rose, he followed as a commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Divine Martial rose to power, Ping followed him as a commander.

sentences.zh: 皇建初，封定陽郡公。

translations.literal: At the start of Huangjian he was enfeoffed as Duke of Dingyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Huangjian he was enfeoffed as Duke of Dingyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 後為青州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he served as Inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太尉。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 論曰：齊神武以晉陽戎馬之地，霸圖攸屬，練兵訓旅，遙制朝權，鄴都機務，情寄深遠。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Qi Divine Martial, holding the martial land of Jinyang where hegemony was bound to attach, drilled troops and trained armies, controlled court power from afar, and entrusted the urgent affairs of Ye with profound reliance.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: With Jinyang, a land of warhorses, as the seat of his hegemonic design, Qi Divine Martial drilled armies, held court power from afar, and placed the weight of Ye's urgent affairs in hands he trusted deeply.

sentences.zh: 孫騰、高隆之、司馬子如等俱不能清貞守道，以康亂為懷，而厚斂貨財，填彼溪壑。

translations.literal: Sun Teng, Gao Longzhi, Sima Ziru, and the rest could none of them keep to purity and rectitude or take easing disorder to heart; instead they heavily amassed goods and wealth to fill their ravines and gullies.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng, Gao Longzhi, Sima Ziru, and the rest could none of them remain pure and upright or make restoring order their concern; instead they amassed wealth until ravines and gullies overflowed.

sentences.zh: 昔蕭何之鎮關中，荀彧之居許下，不亦異於是乎！

translations.literal: In old times Xiao He guarded Guanzhong and Xun Yu dwelt at Xuchang—were they not utterly different from this!
translations.idiomatic: In earlier ages Xiao He held Guanzhong and Xun Yu held Xuchang—were they not worlds apart from this!

sentences.zh: 賴文襄入輔，責以驕縱，厚遇崔暹，奮其霜簡；

translations.literal: It was thanks to Wenxiang's entering as regent, rebuking their arrogance and indulgence, treating Cui Xian generously, and deploying his frost-cold censorial rod;
translations.idiomatic: Only when Wenxiang entered as regent, rebuking their arrogance and excess, honoring Cui Xian, and wielding his icy censor's rod,

sentences.zh: 不然則君子屬厭，豈易聞焉。

translations.literal: otherwise worthy men would have met ruin to repletion—could such a thing easily have gone unspoken?
translations.idiomatic: was disaster avoided; otherwise worthy men would have been destroyed to the last—would that have been anything rare?

sentences.zh: 子如徒以少相親重，情深昵狎，義非草昧，恩結寵私，勳德莫聞，坐致台輔。

translations.literal: Ziru rose only because as a youth he was personally close and esteemed; affection ran deep and intimacy was familiar. His righteousness did not spring from the founding struggle—favor bound him in private loyalty; neither achievement nor virtue was heard of, yet he reached the highest ministerial posts sitting idle.
translations.idiomatic: Ziru owed his rise solely to youthful intimacy and personal favor; affection ran deep and familiarity bred indulgence. His loyalty did not come from shared hardship in founding the state—private favor bound him instead. No merit or virtue was ever heard of, yet he sat idle until he reached the highest ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 消難去齊歸周，義非殉國，向背不已；

translations.literal: Xiaonan's leaving Qi for Zhou was not righteousness dying for the state; his turning this way and that did not cease;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaonan's desertion of Qi for Zhou was no martyrdom for the state; his shifting allegiances never stopped;

sentences.zh: 晚又奔陳，一之謂甚，胡可而再。

translations.literal: late in life he fled again to Chen—once is already too much; how could it be allowed a second time!
translations.idiomatic: and in his later years he fled again to Chen—once was already too much; how could it be tolerated twice!

sentences.zh: 膺之風素可重，幼之清簡自立，有足稱者。

translations.literal: Yingzhi's character and conduct were worthy of respect; Youzhi's purity, simplicity, and self-reliance also deserve praise.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhi's integrity deserves respect, and Youzhi's purity, restraint, and self-reliance are also worthy of note.

sentences.zh: 竇泰、尉景、婁昭、厙狄幹、韓軌等，並以外戚近親，屬雲雷之舉，位非寵進，功籍勢成，附翼攀鱗，鬱為佐命之首；

translations.literal: Dou Tai, Wei Jing, Lou Zhao, Kudigan, Han Gui, and the rest were all close kin by marriage. They joined the enterprise when clouds and thunder gathered; their posts were not merely favor promotions—their merit rode on momentum already formed. Clinging to wings and scaling dragons' scales, they flourished as foremost helpers in founding the dynasty;
translations.idiomatic: Dou Tai, Wei Jing, Lou Zhao, Kudigan, Han Gui, and the rest were all close affinal kin. They joined when the thunderclouds of revolution gathered; their offices were not mere favor—they rode the momentum of power already made. Clinging to wings and climbing dragon scales, they rose to become the foremost founders of the dynasty;

sentences.zh: 定遠以常人之才，而因趙郡忠正，將以志除朝蠹，謀逐佞臣，而信納奸凶，反受其亂。

translations.literal: Dingyuan had only ordinary talent, yet relying on the loyalty and rectitude of the Prince of Zhao commandery, he intended through this resolve to purge court parasites and plot to drive out flatterers—but by trusting and accepting treacherous villains he instead suffered their disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Dingyuan had only ordinary ability, yet leaning on the Prince of Zhao commandery's loyalty and rectitude, he meant to purge the court's parasites and drive out sycophants—only to trust wicked men and be ruined by them in turn.

sentences.zh: 遂使庸豎肆毒，賢戚見誅，敗政害時，莫大於此。

translations.literal: Thus petty upstarts ran rampant with poison, worthy kinsmen were executed, and nothing harmed governance and the age more than this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus base men ran amok with malice, worthy kinsmen were put to death, and nothing did more harm to government and the age than this.

sentences.zh: 鄙語曰：「利以昏智」，況定遠非智者乎。

translations.literal: A vulgar saying runs, "Gain blinds the wise"—all the more so when Dingyuan was no sage!
translations.idiomatic: A common saying has it, "Profit clouds the mind"—and Dingyuan was no sage.

sentences.zh: 段榮以姻戚之重，遇時來之會，功伐之地，亦足稱焉。

translations.literal: Duan Rong, by the weight of marriage alliance, met the moment fortune arrived; in territory gained by military achievement, he too is worth naming.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Rong, through the weight of marriage ties, seized the moment when fortune turned; in lands won by force of arms, he too deserves mention.

sentences.zh: 韶光輔七君，克隆門業，每出當閫外，或任處留台。

translations.literal: Shao and Guang assisted seven rulers and multiplied the family's enterprise. Whenever one went out to hold the outer command, the other would remain at the capital on duty.
translations.idiomatic: Shao and Guang served seven sovereigns and enlarged the family estate. Whenever one marched out to hold the frontier command, the other remained at the capital on duty.

sentences.zh: 以猜忌之朝，終其眉壽；

translations.literal: In a court rife with suspicion, they lived out their full span of years to old age;
translations.idiomatic: In an age of suspicion they lived out their full span to old age;

sentences.zh: 屬亭候多警，為有齊上將，豈其然乎！

translations.literal: when frontier beacons were often alarming, to have such Northern Qi generals—is it not so!
translations.idiomatic: when frontier beacons flared again and again, to have such generals of Northern Qi—is it not exactly so!

sentences.zh: 當以志謝矜功，名不渝實，不以威權禦物，不以智數要時，欲求覆餗，其可得也。

translations.literal: This must be because they declined ambition and rejected boasting of merit, their names never betrayed reality, they did not use intimidation and power to confront others, and did not use schemes and calculations to seize the moment—who seeking to overturn the pot and undo the meal could have succeeded against them?
translations.idiomatic: Surely it was because they renounced ambition and refused to boast of merit, their reputations never outran reality, they did not meet the world with intimidation and power, and did not grasp the times with cunning stratagems—who, seeking to overturn the cauldron and spoil the feast, could have succeeded against men like these?

sentences.zh: 《禮》云「率性之謂道」，此其效歟！

translations.literal: The Book of Rites says, "To follow one's nature is called the Way"—is this not its proof!
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites says, "To follow one's nature is called the Way"—is this not the proof of it!

sentences.zh: 斛律金以神武撥亂之始，翼成王業，忠款之至，成此大功，故能終享遐年，位高百辟。

translations.literal: Hulü Jin, from the start when Divine Martial quelled disorder, aided the completion of the royal enterprise. Sincerity and loyalty at their utmost achieved this great merit, so he could end his days in longevity at a rank above the hundred ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Hulü Jin, from the moment Divine Martial quelled chaos, helped complete the royal enterprise. Loyalty and sincerity at their fullest won this great merit, so he lived out his years in honor, standing above the hundred ministers.

sentences.zh: 視其盈滿之戒，動之微也，才及後嗣，遂至誅夷。

translations.literal: Consider his warning against fullness when the caldron was full—the stirring was slight, yet it reached his descendants and led to execution and extermination.
translations.idiomatic: Recall his warning against fullness when the vessel brimmed—the stir was slight, yet when it reached his descendants it ended in execution and extinction.

sentences.zh: 既處威權之重，蓋符道家所忌。

translations.literal: Since they already occupied the weight of intimidation and power, it surely matched what Taoism warns against.
translations.idiomatic: Once they held such crushing authority, it was precisely what the Way warns against.

sentences.zh: 光以上將之子，有沈毅姿，戰將兵權，暗同韜略，臨敵制勝，變化無方。

translations.literal: Guang, son of a great general, had a bearing of deep resolve. As a fighting commander with military authority, his hidden mastery matched strategies; facing the enemy he secured victory, changing without fixed form.
translations.idiomatic: Guang, born of a great general, had a bearing of deep resolve. As a field commander wielding military power, his hidden mastery matched the finest stratagems; facing the enemy he always prevailed, shifting without fixed pattern.

sentences.zh: 自關、河分隔，年將四紀，以高氏霸王之期，屬宇文草創之日，出軍薄伐，屢挫兵威。

translations.literal: Since Pass and River were divided, nearly four decades had passed. At the time of the Gao clan's hegemonic rule, it fell on the day the Yuwen regime was first being forged; when armies went out on punitive expeditions, their military might was repeatedly blunted.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Pass and the River were divided, nearly four decades had passed. The Gao clan's age of hegemony coincided with the Yuwen house's first founding days; whenever armies marched west on punitive campaigns, Northern Qi's martial prestige was repeatedly blunted.

sentences.zh: 而大寧已還，東鄰浸弱，關西前收巴蜀，又殄江陵，葉建瓴而用武，成併吞之壯志。

translations.literal: But after the Da Ning era the eastern neighbor gradually weakened; in the west the Zhou had taken Bashu and also destroyed Jiangling. Abandoning the posture of pouring from a high eave, they took up arms and formed the mighty ambition of swallowing all.
translations.idiomatic: But after the Da Ning era the eastern neighbor grew steadily weaker; the west had already taken Bashu and destroyed Jiangling. Abandoning the posture of pouring from a high eave, Zhou took up arms and nursed the grand ambition of swallowing all under heaven.

sentences.zh: 光每臨戎誓眾，式遏邊鄙，戰則前無完陣，攻則罕有全城；

translations.literal: Whenever Guang drew up his army and swore before the troops, he held back the frontier marches. In battle, no enemy line stayed intact before him; in assault, few cities remained whole.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Guang mustered his army and swore before the ranks, he checked the frontier. In battle no enemy formation stood whole before him; in siege scarcely a city remained intact.

sentences.zh: 齊氏必致拘原之師，秦人無復啟關之策。

translations.literal: The Qi would inevitably bring Zhou armies to a standstill on the plains; the Qin men had no further plan to open the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi could always pin Zhou armies on the open plain; the men of Qin had no further strategy for forcing the passes.

sentences.zh: 而世亂讒勝，詐以震主之威；

translations.literal: Yet in a chaotic age slander prevailed; deception was used with awe that overwhelmed the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in a chaotic age slander won out; treachery wielded a majesty that overawed the throne.

sentences.zh: 主暗時艱，自毀籓籬之固。

translations.literal: The ruler was dim, the times were hard, and he himself destroyed the firmness of his protective barrier.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler was dark to peril, the times were dire, and he tore down the very bulwark that guarded him.

sentences.zh: 昔李牧之為趙將也，北翦胡冠，西卻秦軍，郭開譖之，牧死趙滅。

translations.literal: In the past, when Li Mu served as a general of Zhao, he cut down the Hu in the north and repelled the Qin army in the west; Guo Kai slandered him, and when Mu died Zhao was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Li Mu served Zhao as a general: he destroyed the Hu in the north and drove back the Qin in the west—until Guo Kai slandered him; when Li Mu died, Zhao perished with him.

sentences.zh: 其議誅光者，豈秦之反間歟？

translations.literal: Those who urged the execution of Guang—were they not Qin's agents of subversion?
translations.idiomatic: Were those who urged Guang's execution not Zhou's agents of subversion?

sentences.zh: 何同術而同亡也！

translations.literal: How alike in method and alike in ruin!
translations.idiomatic: How alike their gifts—and how alike their ruin!

sentences.zh: 內令諸將解體，外為強鄰滅仇。

translations.literal: Within, they made the generals disband; without, they destroyed a foe for a powerful neighbor.
translations.idiomatic: Within, they broke the army apart; without, they destroyed a foe for a powerful neighbor.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 後之君子，可為深戒者歟！

translations.literal: Later gentlemen—may this not be a lesson to take deeply to heart!
translations.idiomatic: Later gentlemen—let this be a warning taken deeply to heart!
